steps.status_note: generated from a craft-consensus rule; the technique itself was not separately verified

steps.title: Rem steps for display headings
steps.do: Give display headings overflow-wrap: anywhere and step the h1 down in a rem media query (max-width: 30rem), with less hero padding, so a word like 'terminal' at 96 px does not stretch the page; do not use clamp() with vw for this.
steps.how: Measured 2026-11-06 in Chrome (Playwright, channel chrome) on the recipe demo page at 320 px with the root font size at 200%; the h1 at 3rem became 96 px at 200%; the word was 364 px wide in a 224 px column and widened the page; the media-query step-down removed the overflow and the a11y-resize-text probe no longer reported a fluid-type problem.
steps.label: standard
steps.measured: Measured 2026-11-06 in Chrome (Playwright, channel chrome) on the recipe demo page at 320 px with the root font size at 200%; the h1 at 3rem became 96 px at 200%; the word was 364 px wide in a 224 px column and widened the page; the media-query step-down removed the overflow and the a11y-resize-text probe no longer reported a fluid-type problem.

recipes.generate_hint: Choose a palette with named roles, assert every text/background pair meets 4.5:1 (3:1 for large text and UI), keep neon for accents on solid surfaces, add a dedicated focus color, and avoid any flashing.

recipes.title: Glass, pastel and soft palettes without washed-out text
recipes.summary: Keep the translucency, blur and gentle colors. Decide the worst-case backdrop first, make the panel dark or light enough for that case, and use pastel as fills with dark text and visible borders.
recipes.keep: Frosted panels, soft color fields, rounded forms.
recipes.avoid: White text on a light translucent panel; pastel text on pastel backgrounds; glass borders as the only separator between controls and background.

contrast.pair: white text on 72% dark panel over #FFFFFF backdrop
white text on 72% dark panel over #FFE066 backdrop
white text on 72% dark panel over #7CF2FF backdrop
dark text on pastel lilac button

steps.title: Test glass on the worst backdrop
steps.do: For glass, compute contrast against the worst backdrop the panel can sit on (white, a bright yellow, a bright cyan), not the average one. The verified panel is 72% near-black; white text on it stays above 4.5:1 over all three backdrops (see the table).
steps.how: Panel color rgba(11,13,18,0.72) with white text. The check uses pure white as the backdrop because a blur is a per-channel weighted average of the pixels behind it and so cannot be lighter than the lightest pixel; this bound assumes browsers composite in sRGB (general knowledge, not on a page read). Raise the opacity before lowering text contrast.
steps.label: craft-consensus
steps.status_note: bound rests on sRGB compositing and blur averaging (reasoning, not a read source)

steps.title: Opaque fallback for backdrop blur
steps.do: Provide an opaque fallback for browsers or settings where backdrop-filter does not apply, and do not rely on blur to separate text from a busy background.
steps.how: backdrop-filter is Baseline 2024 (newly available) and only affects content behind the element up to its backdrop root; an ancestor with opacity below 1 can stop it working. Write the opaque background first and enhance inside @supports (backdrop-filter: blur(1px)), or provide the fallback in @supports not (...). @supports is widely available since September 2015.
steps.label: craft-consensus

steps.title: Dark text on pastel fills
steps.do: Use pastel as a fill and keep dark text on it. Check muted text and links on the pastel background, not on white.
steps.how: Verified pairs: #2B1B45 on #F7F1FF, #5B4B77 on #F7F1FF, #2B1B45 on #CDB4FF, link #5A2FC2 on #F7F1FF.
steps.label: craft-consensus

steps.title: Control edges at 3:1
steps.do: Give inputs, cards that act as controls and icon buttons a border or fill that reaches 3:1 against what surrounds them.
steps.how: Input border #7A68A3 on #F7F1FF is verified above 3:1.
steps.label: craft-consensus

steps.title: Label the modal dialog
steps.do: Build modals with a titled dialog element or role=dialog plus aria-labelledby, and keep all its controls inside it.
steps.how: Open each dialog; query [role=dialog],[role=alertdialog],dialog[open]; assert accessible name is non-empty and that no interactive control needed by the dialog sits outside it. (Derived from the rule; see its sources.)
steps.label: craft-consensus

steps.title: Manage dialog focus and Escape
steps.do: On open focus the first control (or the start of long content), trap Tab, wire Escape and a visible Close button, and restore focus to the opener on close.
steps.how: Keyboard only: activate the opener, verify focus is inside; Tab through the whole dialog and confirm wrap; press Escape and confirm close and focus on the opener; confirm a visible close control exists. (Derived from the rule; see its sources.)
steps.label: craft-consensus

steps.title: Make modal backgrounds inert
steps.do: Make the background inert and dimmed whenever the dialog is modal; for popovers that leave the page usable, do not set aria-modal.
steps.how: With the dialog open, try to Tab, click and screen-reader-navigate to background content. If any works, aria-modal must be absent. If aria-modal is present, confirm a dim or blur overlay covers the page. (Derived from the rule; see its sources.)
steps.label: craft-consensus

steps.title: Scrim behind text on media
steps.do: Put a solid or gradient scrim behind any text that sits on a photo or video and verify the contrast on the brightest area.
steps.how: Screenshot each section with text on imagery at 375, 768 and 1440 px (and at the video's brightest frame). Sample the backdrop under each text line's bounding box, take the pixel closest to the text color, compute the WCAG ratio. Fail below 4.5:1 (3:1 for 24px+ or 18.66px+ bold). (Derived from the rule; see its sources.)
steps.label: craft-consensus

steps.title: Re-check contrast in dark mode
steps.do: Author the dark palette as its own set of tokens, check contrast in both themes, and dim bright images instead of inverting anything.
steps.how: Run the contrast audit (text 4.5:1, large 3:1, UI components 3:1) twice, once per emulated color scheme, over all pages and states (hover, focus, disabled excluded). Fail any pair that passes light but fails dark. Flag use of `filter: invert()` on the page root. (Derived from the rule; see its sources.)
steps.label: craft-consensus
steps.status_note: generated from a craft-consensus rule; the technique itself was not separately verified

steps.title: Small padding on nested glass
steps.do: Keep padding on nested glass panels small under 30rem (panel 1rem, backdrop 1rem) and give the panel heading overflow-wrap: anywhere with a smaller rem size; stacked padding inside a glass panel can leave a column of about 96 px at 200% text.
steps.how: Measured 2026-11-06 in Chrome (Playwright, channel chrome) on the recipe demo page at 320 px with the root font size at 200%; a 72 px h1 in a 96 px column overflowed 17 px; after reducing padding and stepping the size down, there was no overflow.
steps.label: standard
steps.measured: Measured 2026-11-06 in Chrome (Playwright, channel chrome) on the recipe demo page at 320 px with the root font size at 200%; a 72 px h1 in a 96 px column overflowed 17 px; after reducing padding and stepping the size down, there was no overflow.

recipes.generate_hint: Test text against the worst-case backdrop, add an opaque fallback, keep text dark on pastel fills, and make control borders at least 3:1.

recipes.title: Minimal and quiet-luxury pages that remain clear and usable
recipes.summary: Keep the whitespace and restraint. Restraint must not remove contrast, borders, focus, hit areas, labels or the hint that more content exists.
recipes.keep: Whitespace, small type, few elements, muted palette.
recipes.avoid: Light gray text, borderless inputs, placeholder-only labels, tiny icon links, a first screen that looks finished when it is not.

steps.title: Keep muted text at 4.5:1
steps.do: Keep secondary text at or above 4.5:1; #6A6A64 on #FAFAF7 is verified. Do not lighten muted text further for elegance.
steps.how: Check every gray in the palette against every background it touches.
steps.label: craft-consensus

steps.title: Visible field edges at 3:1
steps.do: Give form fields and controls a visible edge at 3:1 or better; a hairline at #8C8C85 on #FAFAF7 is verified.
steps.how: A subtle fill is fine only if it meets 3:1 against the page.
steps.label: craft-consensus

steps.title: Solid offset focus ring
steps.do: Make focus obvious: a solid ring in the text color with an offset suits a minimal style.
steps.how: Use :focus-visible (Baseline widely available since March 2022) so the browser decides when the ring shows. MDN: the indicator needs at least 3:1 contrast (WCAG 1.4.11) and must not simply be removed. In forced-colors mode outline-color and border-color are forced to system colors and stay visible, but box-shadow is forced to none, so draw the ring with outline (as below) and do not rely on box-shadow alone. MDN advises against building a separate forced-colors design; do not use forced-color-adjust to override users' colors.
steps.label: craft-consensus

steps.title: Targets of at least 24 px
steps.do: Keep targets at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels, or spaced so a 24 px circle around each fits without overlap; give small text links padding.
steps.how: WCAG spacing exception: a 24 px circle centered on each undersized target must not intersect another target or another undersized target's circle; WCAG's example is 20×20 px buttons with a 4 px gap passing, and with no gap failing. Other exceptions: an equivalent control, inline text links, user-agent controls, essential targets. Pad icon buttons and footer links rather than enlarging the glyph.
steps.label: craft-consensus

steps.title: Visible label on every field
steps.do: Keep a visible label on every field; use placeholders only for examples.
steps.how: Float labels are acceptable only if the label stays visible after input.
steps.label: craft-consensus

steps.title: One line, one action, a cue
steps.do: Say what the page is and what to do in one line plus one primary action in the first viewport, and show a cut-off element or cue that more content follows.
steps.how: A restrained first screen is fine; an unexplained one is not. Let the next section peek in at the bottom edge.
steps.label: our-take

steps.title: Wire tabs to their panels
steps.do: Give the tablist an aria-label, link every tab to its panel with aria-controls and aria-labelledby, and keep aria-selected in sync with the visible active state.
steps.how: Query the DOM: every [role=tab] is a child of [role=tablist]; exactly one tab has aria-selected=true; each tab aria-controls resolves to a [role=tabpanel] whose aria-labelledby resolves to that tab; tablist has aria-label or aria-labelledby. Confirm with a screen reader that the selected state is announced. (Derived from the rule; see its sources.)
steps.label: craft-consensus

steps.title: Accordions as heading plus button
steps.do: Write accordions as h3 > button[aria-expanded] followed by a div that gets the hidden attribute when collapsed.
steps.how: For each toggle: tagName is BUTTON, parent is h1-h6 (or role=heading with aria-level), the button is the heading's only child, aria-expanded is 'true' or 'false' and flips on click, the hidden panel is display:none or [hidden] when collapsed. (Derived from the rule; see its sources.)
steps.label: craft-consensus
steps.status_note: generated from a craft-consensus rule; the technique itself was not separately verified

steps.title: Prefer visible labels over tooltips
steps.do: Prefer visible labels; if a tooltip is unavoidable, trigger on hover and focus, allow Escape, and keep it text only.
steps.how: Hover and Tab to each tooltip trigger; press Escape; move the pointer onto the bubble; check aria-describedby; check the bubble DOM for a, button, input. (Derived from the rule; see its sources.)
steps.label: craft-consensus
steps.status_note: generated from a craft-consensus rule; the technique itself was not separately verified

steps.title: Show toggle state beyond color
steps.do: Style toggles from [aria-pressed=true] and add a knob position or check icon, not only a color change.
steps.how: Grayscale screenshot of both states; confirm still distinguishable. Check CSS selectors key off aria-pressed/aria-checked/:checked. (Derived from the rule; see its sources.)
steps.label: craft-consensus
steps.status_note: generated from a craft-consensus rule; the technique itself was not separately verified

steps.title: Short words, check reading grade
steps.do: Use short, common words and one clause per sentence, then check the grade score before finishing.
steps.how: Run Flesch-Kincaid grade (Hemingway, Word, or a script) on the concatenated body copy of each page, excluding proper names and titles. Fail above 9 for general audiences unless the brief names an expert audience. (Derived from the rule; see its sources.)
steps.label: craft-consensus
steps.status_note: generated from a craft-consensus rule; the technique itself was not separately verified

steps.title: Spell out acronyms and brand names
steps.do: Write the full phrase the first time and in every heading or button, and describe each branded name in plain words next to it.
steps.how: Extract all-caps tokens of 2 or more letters and capitalised product names from headings, nav and buttons; confirm each is expanded or described adjacent. Confirm first body use is expanded. Whitelist PDF, FAQ, URL. (Derived from the rule; see its sources.)
steps.label: craft-consensus
steps.status_note: generated from a craft-consensus rule; the technique itself was not separately verified

steps.title: Headline as one buyer's result
steps.do: Write the headline as the result one named buyer gets, using a noun or number only this product can claim.
steps.how: Read the H1 and subhead alone. (1) Does it say what is offered and for whom? (2) Paste it with a competitor's name: does it still read true? If yes, fail. (3) Fail if it matches the template 'The [AI-powered|modern|all-in-one] [noun] for [teams|businesses|everyone]'. (Derived from the rule; see its sources.)
steps.label: craft-consensus
steps.status_note: generated from a craft-consensus rule; the technique itself was not separately verified

steps.title: Headings that state the finding
steps.do: Write each heading as the finding of its section, so the headings alone tell the story.
steps.how: Extract the heading outline. Fail any heading matching the blocklist (case-insensitive: introduction, overview, features, benefits, our approach, why us, about, welcome). Then read the outline alone: a reader should be able to say what the page offers. (Derived from the rule; see its sources.)
steps.label: craft-consensus
steps.status_note: generated from a craft-consensus rule; the technique itself was not separately verified

steps.title: Buttons labelled verb plus object
steps.do: Label each button with a verb plus its object ('Book a demo', 'Download the price list').
steps.how: Collect text of button, [role=button], input[type=submit] and .btn-like links. Fail if the first word is not a verb (use a verb list), if the word count is over 4, or if the label matches the blocklist: submit, ok, click here, learn more, get started, go, continue (unless a save step is stated). (Derived from the rule; see its sources.)
steps.label: craft-consensus
steps.status_note: generated from a craft-consensus rule; the technique itself was not separately verified

steps.title: Link text names the destination
steps.do: Write link text that names the destination and say 'PDF, 2 MB' or 'opens in a new window' when it applies.
steps.how: Collect all anchors with accessible names. Fail if two different hrefs share the same name, if a name matches /^(click here|here|more|read more|link|this)$/i or contains 'link', if an href ends in a document extension without format and size in the name, or if target=_blank lacks a notice placed after the main text. (Derived from the rule; see its sources.)
steps.label: craft-consensus
steps.status_note: generated from a craft-consensus rule; the technique itself was not separately verified

steps.title: Specific, actionable error text
steps.do: Start empty-field errors with a verb ('Enter your email address') and wrong-value errors with the field name plus 'must be'.
steps.how: Trigger every validation and failure state (empty, wrong format, too long, network failure, server error). Fail any message that does not name the problem and a fix, matches the generic list, or shows a raw code. Automated part: grep message strings for the generic list. (Derived from the rule; see its sources.)
steps.label: craft-consensus
steps.status_note: generated from a craft-consensus rule; the technique itself was not separately verified

steps.title: Facts instead of adjectives
steps.do: For every adjective, write the fact that made you choose it and use the fact instead.
steps.how: Grep for the abstract-adjective list. For each hit, require a number, a named object or a verifiable example in the same sentence, otherwise rewrite. Check that no three feature cards share the same structure of icon, two-word title and filler sentence. (Derived from the rule; see its sources.)
steps.label: craft-consensus
steps.status_note: generated from a craft-consensus rule; the technique itself was not separately verified

steps.title: Cap line length near 55ch
steps.do: Wrap every block of running text in a container with max-inline-size of about 45ch to 55ch for proportional fonts (never wider than 60ch), and let the container, not the viewport, decide the line length; then count characters per line in the browser.
steps.how: Measured 2026-11-06 in Chrome on macOS: ch is the width of the digit 0, wider than an average letter, so 66ch gave 87 to 96 characters per line (system-ui, Georgia, Arial, Helvetica Neue), 60ch gave 77 to 89, 55ch gave 69 to 83, 50ch gave 67 to 74 and 45ch gave 59 to 67. Use 50ch to 55ch and verify the real count with the audit. Other platforms' fonts were not measured.
steps.label: craft-consensus
steps.status_note: generated from a craft-consensus rule; the technique itself was not separately verified
steps.measured: Measured 2026-11-06 in Chrome 156 on macOS: characters per line counted for system-ui, Georgia, Arial and Helvetica Neue at 45ch to 66ch (see content/learn/recipes/_proposals/measurements-b).

steps.title: Body text at 1rem or larger
steps.do: Set the body size to 1rem (16px) or larger, sized up (17-20px) for long reading, and use smaller sizes only for captions and legal lines.
steps.how: At 320 and 1280 px, collect computed font-size of every text node inside p, li, td, label, input, textarea, select, button. Fail when any is under 16px, unless the node is inside figcaption, small, footer legal text or a caption. List every text node under 14px for manual review (14px is our review threshold, not from a source). (Derived from the rule; see its sources.)
steps.label: craft-consensus
steps.status_note: generated from a craft-consensus rule; the technique itself was not separately verified

steps.title: Stepped rem sizes for headings
steps.do: Set headline sizes in rem and step them at em/rem media queries (for example 3rem, 4rem, 7rem), keeping the smallest at least 40% of the largest; do not use clamp(rem + vw) for text that must scale; test at 200% zoom and 320 px.
steps.how: Measured in Chrome 2026-11-05 (content/learn/measurements/type-zoom-2026-11-05.json): clamp(rem + vw) and vw sizes did not reach 200% at 200% zoom; stepped rem with small >= 40% of large did. See also step bt-scalable in big-type-and-modes.
steps.label: craft-consensus

steps.title: Breakpoints where content breaks
steps.do: Build the layout with fluid grid rules first and add a breakpoint in em only where you can see the content break.
steps.how: Sweep the viewport from 320 to 1920 px in 40px steps. At each step assert no horizontal scrollbar (scrollWidth <= clientWidth), no element overlapping its sibling's box, and the measure rule still passes. Inspect media queries: list breakpoint values and flag any matching device presets (375, 414, 768 and 1024 px) written in px for review. (Derived from the rule; see its sources.)
steps.label: craft-consensus
steps.status_note: generated from a craft-consensus rule; the technique itself was not separately verified

steps.title: Wrap headings and button links
steps.do: Give display headings overflow-wrap: anywhere (a 3rem h1 is 96 px at 200% text and a word such as 'Furniture' is about 400 px wide) and give button-like links max-width: 100% with overflow-wrap: anywhere.
steps.how: Measured 2026-11-06 in Chrome (Playwright, channel chrome) on the recipe demo page at 320 px with the root font size at 200% and the audit probes; the page scrolled 215 px sideways at 320 px with 200% text and a link collapsed to 12 px under the text-spacing overrides; both were gone after the change.
steps.label: standard
steps.measured: Measured 2026-11-06 in Chrome (Playwright, channel chrome) on the recipe demo page at 320 px with the root font size at 200% and the audit probes; the page scrolled 215 px sideways at 320 px with 200% text and a link collapsed to 12 px under the text-spacing overrides; both were gone after the change.

recipes.generate_hint: Keep muted text at 4.5:1 or better, borders and controls at 3:1, show a clear focus ring, use 24 px minimum targets, visible labels, a one-line purpose with a primary action in the first viewport, and a cue that more content follows.

recipes.title: 3D, WebGL, cursor effects and interactive art
recipes.summary: Keep the spectacle. Treat the 3D scene as an enhancement over a complete page: real content first, a meaningful static fallback, keyboard parity, and a performance budget measured on mid-range devices.
recipes.keep: A real-time 3D or shader scene, interactive objects, cursor-following effects.
recipes.avoid: Scene as the only way to reach content; canvases that trap focus; effects that need drag; heavy initialization before the first content paints.

steps.title: Core content works without the scene
steps.do: Build the headline, copy, navigation and call to action as normal HTML that works without the scene. The scene replaces or decorates a static image, not the content.
steps.how: Resilient Web Design (Layers): start from a well-structured HTML baseline everyone can use and enhance per capability; identify core functionality versus enhancement; feature-detect rather than sniff. Test by disabling JavaScript and throttling the network: the message and navigation must still appear.
steps.label: craft-consensus

steps.title: Script-revealed scene controls
steps.do: Controls that only work once the scene runs (rotate, zoom, pause, skip link) start hidden and are shown by the scene script; with JavaScript off they must not appear.
steps.how: Use the hidden attribute and add [hidden]{display:none !important}: an author rule such as .controls{display:grid} overrides the browser's hidden style, so the controls stayed visible with JavaScript off in the demo until that rule was added. Add a noscript style as a second guard. If the scene fails to start (getContext returns null, shader link fails), remove the canvas and the controls and leave the poster.
steps.label: our-take
steps.status_note: measured in the demo: with JavaScript disabled the controls and canvas were visible until [hidden]{display:none !important} was added; Playwright no-JS pass afterwards showed them hidden and the poster visible
steps.measured: Measured 2026-11-06 in Chrome (Playwright, channel chrome) on content/learn/recipes/demos/webgl-and-3d.html with JavaScript on and off, and by audit; see the step text for what was observed.

steps.title: Static poster as LCP element
steps.do: Show a static poster image of the scene as the LCP element, discoverable in the initial HTML and not lazy-loaded; initialize WebGL after first paint.
steps.how: Use a real img for the poster with fetchpriority="high", discoverable in the initial HTML and not lazy-loaded (web.dev). Start the scene after first paint: requestIdleCallback has limited availability (not Baseline), so call it with a timeout and fall back to setTimeout, or start on the load event. Avoid synchronous head scripts.
steps.label: craft-consensus

steps.title: Test scene and no-WebGL paths
steps.do: Test the scene path and the no-WebGL path: with WebGL unavailable the poster stays, the controls disappear and nothing throws.
steps.how: Check getContext('webgl2') for null and shader compile and link errors; on failure remove the canvas and hide the controls. Headless Chrome without GPU flags has no WebGL, so a default audit run only ever exercises this fallback; launch Chrome with --use-gl=angle --use-angle=swiftshader --enable-unsafe-swiftshader to audit the live scene.
steps.label: our-take
steps.status_note: both paths were run with the audit: default flags (fallback) and swiftshader flags (live scene); both had zero fails
steps.measured: Measured 2026-11-06 in Chrome (Playwright, channel chrome) on content/learn/recipes/demos/webgl-and-3d.html with JavaScript on and off, and by audit; see the step text for what was observed.

steps.title: Serve the poster as a file
steps.do: Serve the poster as a real image file (or URL), not a data: URI, if you want it to count as the LCP element.
steps.how: In Chrome 156 an 800x600 img whose src is a data: URI was not reported as an LCP candidate: the LCP entry was a tiny h1 instead (PerformanceObserver type largest-contentful-paint). Self-contained pages cannot therefore prove the poster is the LCP element; measure on the real asset.
steps.label: our-take
steps.status_note: measured once with a single test page in Chrome 156 (headless, Playwright); not checked in other browsers
steps.measured: Measured 2026-11-06 in Chrome (Playwright, channel chrome) on content/learn/recipes/demos/webgl-and-3d.html with JavaScript on and off, and by audit; see the step text for what was observed.

steps.title: Reserve space for scene controls
steps.do: Reserve the space of controls that appear when the scene starts, so starting the scene moves nothing.
steps.how: Render the controls in the first HTML with visibility:hidden (it keeps the box) and switch to visible when the scene is ready; do not go from display:none to display:grid after load. Give the stage an aspect-ratio and put the poster image inside it with width and height attributes.
steps.label: craft-consensus

steps.title: Keep the main thread free
steps.do: Keep the main thread free: render in requestAnimationFrame, avoid layout reads inside pointer handlers, cap device pixel ratio (for example at 2), and pause rendering when the canvas is off-screen or the tab is hidden.
steps.how: Run the render loop only while the canvas is visible, using IntersectionObserver (Baseline widely available since March 2019; its callbacks run on the main thread, so keep them light; feature-detect it). Use the Page Visibility API (visibilitychange, document.hidden; widely available since 2015) for work the browser does not stop itself: browsers already stop requestAnimationFrame in background tabs, but not audio, timers or network. Measure INP in the field; lab tools only approximate it.
steps.label: craft-consensus

steps.title: Fallback content inside the canvas
steps.do: Put alternative content inside the canvas element (a text description, or an image with alt). Mark a purely presentational canvas role="presentation". If the scene is interactive, map each interactive region to a real focusable element in the fallback content; the canvas itself exposes nothing.
steps.how: MDN: a canvas is a bitmap that exposes nothing to assistive technology; fallback content goes between the canvas tags; role="presentation" is only for purely presentational canvases; MDN advises avoiding canvas in accessible sites where possible. The HTML Standard says fallback content must convey the same function, focusable descendants of a canvas remain usable, and interactive regions should map one-to-one to focusable areas in the fallback. No page read mentions aria-label on canvas. Put the same information in the page text.
steps.label: craft-consensus

steps.title: Make the canvas skippable
steps.do: Make the canvas skippable: it is not in the tab order unless it has controls, and focus can always leave it. Provide a visible way to skip past an interactive scene.
steps.how: WCAG 2.1.2: if focus can enter a component, the keyboard must be able to leave it; a non-standard exit must be explained to the user; Esc is a common standard exit; a modal that cycles focus and closes by Esc or buttons passes. Keep the canvas out of the tab order unless it has controls, and give interactive scenes a visible way to skip past them.
steps.label: craft-consensus

steps.title: Buttons and keys beside dragging
steps.do: Anything done by dragging or orbiting also works with buttons or keys (rotate left and right, zoom in and out), and with a single tap.
steps.how: WCAG 2.5.7 (technique G219): put buttons beside the drag, or use tap-to-place, direct selection or a typed value. A keyboard alternative alone does not satisfy 2.5.7: pointer-operable controls are needed (they may be visually hidden). Add visible rotate and zoom buttons next to any drag-to-rotate scene.
steps.label: craft-consensus

steps.title: Tap to turn, pan-y to scroll
steps.do: Make a tap on the canvas turn the scene one step, and set touch-action: pan-y on the canvas so vertical swipes still scroll the page.
steps.how: Use pointer events: record pointerdown, treat movement over about 6 px as a drag, and on pointerup without movement call the same function as the Rotate right button. With touch-action: pan-y a horizontal drag rotates and a vertical swipe scrolls, so the canvas does not trap touch scrolling. Make sure the object is visibly different when turned (a rotationally symmetric object shows nothing when rotated; add pattern or asymmetry).
steps.label: our-take
steps.status_note: Playwright: mouse drag, mouse click and touch tap each changed the rendered frame under reduced motion; touch-action computed as pan-y

steps.title: Respect reduced motion
steps.do: Respect reduced motion: show the poster or a still frame, stop continuous camera movement, and keep the motion minimal for everyone around the headline and call to action.
steps.how: Check matchMedia("(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)") before starting the loop and listen for its change event (Baseline widely available since September 2020) so the scene reacts when the setting changes.
steps.label: craft-consensus

steps.title: Check reduced motion inside the loop
steps.do: Do not rely on the change event alone to react to a reduced-motion switch while a render loop reads .matches; compare the current value inside the loop too.
steps.how: In Chrome (Playwright emulateMedia), when a requestAnimationFrame loop read matchMedia(...).matches every frame, the page's own change listener did not fire after the setting changed, although a freshly created MediaQueryList did receive the event. Keeping a lastReduce variable and calling the apply function when reduce.matches !== lastReduce inside the frame fixed it. Also keep user-initiated rotate and zoom working under reduced motion, as instant jumps instead of easing.
steps.label: our-take
steps.status_note: reproduced with Playwright media emulation in one Chrome build; not reproduced with a real OS setting change

steps.title: Cursor effects never replace the cursor
steps.do: Cursor-following effects add to the system cursor and never replace it on interactive elements; keyboard focus gets the equivalent highlight; turn the effect off on touch devices and under reduced motion.
steps.how: Animate transform and opacity only (web.dev: the only two compositor-only properties) and keep layers few (do not promote everything with will-change). Use passive listeners where you never call preventDefault: wheel, touchstart and touchmove on window or document are passive by default, element-level listeners are not. One requestAnimationFrame loop.
steps.label: our-take
steps.status_note: the recommendation is our judgement; the supporting facts (compositor-only properties, passive listener defaults) are verified

steps.title: Cursor glow behind content
steps.do: Put a cursor glow behind the page content, never over it: fixed, pointer-events:none, z-index below content, transform only, and enable it only for (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine) when motion is not reduced. Keep the glow achromatic or warm and the accent off cyan on a near-black page: a cyan or teal radial halo with alpha under 0.3 fails distinct-no-decorative-glow and a cyan accent on near-black fails distinct-no-ai-palette.
steps.how: Give html the background and leave body transparent so a z-index:-1 layer is visible. On keyboard focus (focusin where :focus-visible matches) move the glow to the focused control. Declare the pointermove listener passive and drive the glow from the same requestAnimationFrame loop as the scene. Axe reported no contrast problems with the low-opacity glow behind light text. Measured 2026-11-06: switching the accent to sand (#E3C08D) and the halo to rgba(238,243,242,.12) cleared both audit failures; the halo is position:fixed so it never causes scroll.
steps.label: our-take
steps.status_note: the placement choices are our judgement; the touch gating was checked with Playwright mobile emulation (hover:hover and pointer:fine both false) and the reduced-motion gating by emulation

steps.title: Manage dialog focus and Escape
steps.do: On open focus the first control (or the start of long content), trap Tab, wire Escape and a visible Close button, and restore focus to the opener on close.
steps.how: Keyboard only: activate the opener, verify focus is inside; Tab through the whole dialog and confirm wrap; press Escape and confirm close and focus on the opener; confirm a visible close control exists. (Derived from the rule; see its sources.)
steps.label: craft-consensus

steps.title: Prefer visible labels over tooltips
steps.do: Prefer visible labels; if a tooltip is unavoidable, trigger on hover and focus, allow Escape, and keep it text only.
steps.how: Hover and Tab to each tooltip trigger; press Escape; move the pointer onto the bubble; check aria-describedby; check the bubble DOM for a, button, input. (Derived from the rule; see its sources.)
steps.label: craft-consensus
steps.status_note: generated from a craft-consensus rule; the technique itself was not separately verified

steps.title: Use a native range input
steps.do: Prefer input type=range; add output text next to it and aria-valuetext when units matter.
steps.how: Inspect value attributes; keyboard test arrows/Home/End/PageUp/PageDown; check aria-valuetext shows units; test with VoiceOver on iOS or TalkBack. (Derived from the rule; see its sources.)
steps.label: craft-consensus

steps.title: Auto-fit grids with min() tracks
steps.do: Write card grids as repeat(auto-fit, minmax(min(15rem, 100%), 1fr)): minmax(15rem, 1fr) is a 480 px track at 200% text.
steps.how: Measured 2026-11-06 in Chrome (Playwright, channel chrome) on the recipe demo page at 320 px with the root font size at 200% and the audit probes; the li right edge was 520 px at 320 px; inside the viewport after the change.
steps.label: standard
steps.measured: Measured 2026-11-06 in Chrome (Playwright, channel chrome) on the recipe demo page at 320 px with the root font size at 200% and the audit probes; the li right edge was 520 px at 320 px; inside the viewport after the change.

recipes.generate_hint: Ship the page content as HTML first, use a static poster for LCP, start WebGL after first paint, pause off-screen, give keyboard and single-pointer alternatives, never trap focus, and honor reduced motion.

recipes.title: Hero video, ambient loops and marquees
recipes.summary: Keep the moving backdrop. Decide whether the video is decorative or carries information, give viewers a pause control, never autoplay sound, and keep key messages out of the moving layer.
recipes.keep: Full-bleed muted looping video, ambient background loops, ticker rows of logos or text.
recipes.avoid: Autoplaying sound; no way to stop motion; important messages inside a scrolling ticker; large video as the LCP with no poster.

steps.title: Decide decorative or informative video
steps.do: Decide: is the video decorative and silent, or does it carry speech or information? Decorative: mark it as such and keep every message in text. Informative: it needs captions and a description or transcript.
steps.how: WCAG 1.2.1 requires an alternative or an audio track for prerecorded video-only content, and its Understanding page does not exempt decorative or background video; 1.1.1 says pure decoration should be ignorable by assistive technology. So: treat a loop as decoration (aria-hidden, no information in it, every message also in text) as an inference from 1.1.1, and add the pause control (2.2.2). A video with speech needs captions (1.2.2) and an audio description or text alternative (1.2.3, 1.2.5).
steps.label: craft-consensus
steps.status_note: WCAG does not address background video directly; the decorative treatment is an inference from 1.1.1

steps.title: Never autoplay sound
steps.do: Never autoplay sound. Autoplay muted (or with no audio track), with playsinline, and provide controls to start sound.
steps.how: Browsers generally block audible autoplay; muted and silent video may autoplay, and playsinline is needed for autoplay in Safari.
steps.label: craft-consensus

code.text:
<video autoplay muted loop playsinline poster="/hero.jpg" aria-hidden="true">
  <source src="/hero.mp4" type="video/mp4">
</video>
<!-- script swaps the label between "Pause background video" and "Play background video"; no aria-pressed -->
<button type="button" class="motion-toggle">Pause background video</button>

steps.title: Keyboard-reachable pause control
steps.do: Give a visible, keyboard-reachable control that pauses or stops automatically starting motion (video, ambient loop, ticker); ideally one control for all moving content. A control that only pauses while hovered or focused does not meet WCAG 2.2.2.
steps.how: WCAG 2.2.2 applies to moving content that starts automatically (including by hover, focus or scrolling into view), lasts more than five seconds and runs alongside other content; auto-updating content has no five-second exception. Because the label changes between "Pause" and "Play", do not add aria-pressed: the APG button pattern says a toggle's label must stay the same when aria-pressed is used. Remember the choice for the session.
steps.label: craft-consensus

steps.title: Poster and play button fallback
steps.do: If autoplay is blocked or reduced motion is on, show the poster image and a play button instead of an empty frame.
steps.how: Catch the play() promise rejection (NotAllowedError) and show the poster or play button.
steps.label: craft-consensus

steps.title: Poster as the LCP candidate
steps.do: Make the poster the LCP candidate: an image discoverable in the initial HTML with fetchpriority="high" and not lazy-loaded; load the video file after it.
steps.how: A video element is an LCP candidate: its time is the poster image load or the first frame, whichever is earlier. Make the poster an img-like resource discoverable early with fetchpriority="high" where it is the largest element, never lazy-load it, and defer the video file.
steps.label: craft-consensus

steps.title: Tickers for decoration only
steps.do: Use tickers for decoration only: pause on hover and focus, duplicate content hidden from assistive technology, no critical information inside, static when reduced motion is on, and never styled like an ad.
steps.how: Pause on hover or focus is an extra, not a replacement for a persistent control (WCAG: a control that pauses only while focused does not qualify). A static row of the same logos is the reduced-motion version. The APG carousel pattern is a model for rotating content: the rotation control is the first tab stop and rotation stops when focus enters or the mouse hovers.
steps.label: craft-consensus

steps.title: Calm loops around headline and CTA
steps.do: Keep the loop calm and slow around the headline and call to action, and let the headline, tagline and logo stay static.
steps.how: Choose footage with low motion near text areas, or add a scrim.
steps.label: our-take
steps.status_note: our judgement

steps.title: Scroll-snap sliders without autoplay
steps.do: Build sliders as scroll-snap lists with labelled prev/next buttons and no autoplay.
steps.how: Load the page for 30 seconds without input: nothing moves. Tab through: arrows reachable, scroller focusable with visible focus, hidden slides' links not focusable. Check prev/next buttons have names. (Derived from the rule; see its sources.)
steps.label: craft-consensus
steps.status_note: generated from a craft-consensus rule; the technique itself was not separately verified

steps.title: Live captions for live streams
steps.do: If you embed a live stream, use a player and a captioning service that supply live captions.
steps.how: If the page embeds a live stream, enable captions in the player during the live event and confirm they track speech; otherwise mark not applicable. (Derived from the rule; see its sources.)
steps.label: craft-consensus

steps.title: Scrim behind text on media
steps.do: Put a solid or gradient scrim behind any text that sits on a photo or video and verify the contrast on the brightest area.
steps.how: Screenshot each section with text on imagery at 375, 768 and 1440 px (and at the video's brightest frame). Sample the backdrop under each text line's bounding box, take the pixel closest to the text color, compute the WCAG ratio. Fail below 4.5:1 (3:1 for 24px+ or 18.66px+ bold). (Derived from the rule; see its sources.)
steps.label: craft-consensus

steps.title: Skip link above video and scrim
steps.do: Give the skip link a z-index above the hero video and scrim so it is visible when focused.
steps.how: A skip link that is not positioned paints under a later position:relative or absolute hero; set position:absolute with z-index (for example 100) on the skip link. Found by auditing the recipe demo page in Chrome (the Tab traversal probe reported the focused skip link as covered).
steps.label: craft-consensus

steps.title: Stepped rem hero heading
steps.do: Step the hero h1 in rem (2rem, then 2.75rem from min-width: 40em) with overflow-wrap: anywhere; do not use clamp() with vw, which the resize-text check flags.
steps.how: Measured 2026-11-06 in Chrome (Playwright, channel chrome) on the recipe demo page at 320 px with the root font size at 200% and the audit probes; a fixed 2.75rem h1 overflowed a 224 px content box by 33 px at 200% text; the stepped size fitted the longest word at 223 px in a 256 px box.
steps.label: standard
steps.measured: Measured 2026-11-06 in Chrome (Playwright, channel chrome) on the recipe demo page at 320 px with the root font size at 200% and the audit probes; a fixed 2.75rem h1 overflowed a 224 px content box by 33 px at 200% text; the stepped size fitted the longest word at 223 px in a 256 px box.

recipes.generate_hint: Decorative muted looping video with a poster as LCP, a visible pause control, no autoplaying sound, static fallback for reduced motion, and key messages in HTML text.

recipes.title: Scroll-driven stories, parallax and text effects
recipes.summary: Keep the sense of a narrative that unfolds. Use native scrolling, keep content in the page whether or not the effect runs, give the most important information and the main action early, and offer a reduced version.
recipes.keep: Pinned sections, chapters, reveal-on-scroll, parallax layers, kinetic type.
recipes.avoid: Scroll hijacking; content that exists only after an animation; the call to action buried at the end; effects with no reduced-motion version.

steps.title: Keep native scrolling
steps.do: Use the browser's own scrolling with sticky positioning or scroll-linked animation; do not take over scroll speed or direction.
steps.how: CSS scroll-driven animations (animation-timeline: scroll() or view()) are Baseline 2026 and absent in older browsers; feature-detect with @supports and show the final state when unsupported. Declare animation-timeline after the animation shorthand.
steps.label: craft-consensus

steps.title: Sticky figures on wide screens only
steps.do: Pin a figure with position: sticky only where there is room beside the text (about 56em and wider); on narrow screens let it scroll with the page. Do not make the header sticky.
steps.how: A sticky figure in a single column covers the paragraphs it should sit beside, and a sticky header can fully cover a focused link. Use scroll-padding-top if a fixed bar is unavoidable, and keep decorative fixed elements (a progress bar) pointer-events:none and aria-hidden.
steps.label: our-take
steps.status_note: design advice; no fixed header was tested because the demo avoids one

steps.title: Base style is the finished state
steps.do: Every effect, including purely decorative ones such as a progress bar, must have a base style that is already its finished state; set the effect's starting state only inside the @supports block.
steps.how: Put the whole effect layer in @supports (animation-timeline: view()) { ... } and keep the base rules free of starting states (opacity:0, translate, scaleX(0)). In the demo the progress bar had transform:scaleX(0) in the base rule, so in a browser without scroll timelines it would sit at zero forever; the fix was display:none in the base rule and display:block plus scaleX(0) inside @supports.
steps.label: our-take
steps.status_note: checked by renaming animation-timeline in a copy of the page to simulate no support and reading computed styles; the other effects were already final in that state

steps.title: Content in the DOM first
steps.do: All text and links exist in the DOM in reading order, visible without the animation. An effect may reveal or move content, not create it.
steps.how: Test with JavaScript off and with the effect stylesheet removed.
steps.label: craft-consensus

steps.title: Open with the point
steps.do: Open with the point: what the page is and who it is for in the first chapter, and the primary action visible in the first viewport and repeated as the story ends.
steps.how: A story can build, but the first screen must already answer what and why.
steps.label: our-take

steps.title: Fades instead of large movement
steps.do: Under reduced motion replace large movement (parallax, scaling, sliding) with fades or a static layout, and keep what the motion conveyed.
steps.how: Swap transforms for opacity changes in the reduce media query rather than deleting content.
steps.label: craft-consensus

steps.title: Opacity-only reveals under reduce
steps.do: In the reduce query, keep the reveals as an opacity-only fade on the same timeline and set parallax and pinned-figure animation to none, so the figure shows its final state and the caption states what the motion showed.
steps.how: Nest @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) inside the @supports block and swap the keyframes name for an opacity-only keyframe; set animation:none on parallax layers and on the pinned figure. Playwright with reducedMotion:'reduce' confirmed computed transform:none on the parallax layer, the water level and the line masks, with opacity fades still driven by view(). Always give the figure a text caption with the numbers or years the motion conveyed.
steps.label: craft-consensus

steps.title: Shallow parallax, never behind text
steps.do: Keep parallax shallow, never behind text, and stop it when the user asks for less motion; parallax layers are decoration.
steps.how: WCAG 2.3.3 (Level AAA) names parallax scrolling as a common non-essential motion effect and recommends honoring the reduced-motion setting (technique C39, JavaScript SCR40). Limiting depth and turning it off on small screens is our judgement.
steps.label: our-take
steps.status_note: depth and small-screen advice is our judgement; the rule that parallax should be disable-able is verified

steps.title: Keep text as real text
steps.do: Keep text as real text. Prefer effects that do not split it (masks, whole-line reveals). If you must split text into spans, keep the full string available to assistive technology once, and hide the pieces.
steps.how: MDN: aria-label is not supported on generic elements (a bare div or span), so do not rely on it on a parent of split spans. Either give the container a role that supports naming where one genuinely fits, or add one screen-reader-only element holding the full text (WebAIM: off-screen positioning or a 1 px clip-based technique; never display:none or hidden) and mark the split spans aria-hidden (MDN lists duplicated or redundant text as a use; never on or around focusable elements). Use sparingly and test with a screen reader.
steps.label: craft-consensus
steps.status_note: the two techniques are verified; applying them to split-text effects is our composition and no page addresses it

steps.title: Animate transform and opacity only
steps.do: Drive effects from compositor-friendly properties (transform, opacity) and avoid reading layout in scroll handlers.
steps.how: Prefer CSS timelines or IntersectionObserver to scroll listeners, and animate transform and opacity only (the only compositor-only properties, per web.dev).
steps.label: craft-consensus

steps.title: Keep animated shapes in their box
steps.do: Keep animated geometry inside its container: scale an SVG shape from its edge (transform-box: fill-box; transform-origin: 50% 100%) instead of translating a taller shape out of its viewBox.
steps.how: axe-core's color-contrast rule reported 'background color could not be determined because it is overlapped by another element' for the figcaption under a pinned SVG, caused by a translated rect whose box extended below the SVG's viewBox. Removing the animation cleared it; replacing translateY with scaleY and transform-box: fill-box cleared it with the animation kept (a11y-contrast-text went from 'check' to clean).
steps.label: our-take
steps.status_note: axe incomplete count went from 1 to 0 on the demo at desktop and mobile widths after the change

steps.title: Sentences of about 15 words
steps.do: Write body sentences of about 15 words, split any that pass 25, and read each aloud before keeping it.
steps.how: Extract visible text of p, li and blockquote elements, split on sentence terminators, count words per sentence. Fail on any sentence over 25 words; fail the page if the mean exceeds 20. Ignore headings, buttons and legal text. (Derived from the rule; see its sources.)
steps.label: craft-consensus
steps.status_note: generated from a craft-consensus rule; the technique itself was not separately verified

steps.title: Headings that state the finding
steps.do: Write each heading as the finding of its section, so the headings alone tell the story.
steps.how: Extract the heading outline. Fail any heading matching the blocklist (case-insensitive: introduction, overview, features, benefits, our approach, why us, about, welcome). Then read the outline alone: a reader should be able to say what the page offers. (Derived from the rule; see its sources.)
steps.label: craft-consensus
steps.status_note: generated from a craft-consensus rule; the technique itself was not separately verified

steps.title: Minmax tracks and wrapping words
steps.do: Give one-column grids an explicit grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr) (an implicit auto track grows to its min-content), use minmax(min(15rem, 100%), 1fr) for card grids and overflow-wrap: anywhere on headings and paragraphs.
steps.how: Measured 2026-11-06 in Chrome (Playwright, channel chrome) on the recipe demo page at 320 px with the root font size at 200% and the audit probes; scrollWidth went 520, then 327, then 351 (text spacing on long words) and finally 320 after the three changes.
steps.label: standard
steps.measured: Measured 2026-11-06 in Chrome (Playwright, channel chrome) on the recipe demo page at 320 px with the root font size at 200% and the audit probes; scrollWidth went 520, then 327, then 351 (text spacing on long words) and finally 320 after the three changes.

recipes.generate_hint: Use native scroll and CSS timelines with @supports, keep all content in the DOM, put the point and primary action early, add a reduced-motion version, and keep effects to transform and opacity.

recipes.title: Intro animations and preloaders
recipes.summary: Prefer no preloader. If the brand needs an opening moment, keep it short, skippable and non-blocking so it costs no loading time, causes no layout shift and does not read as a popup.
recipes.keep: A designed opening moment, a branded reveal.
recipes.avoid: A screen that blocks content until assets load; long sequences on every visit; counters that count up while nothing is ready; layout shifts when the overlay leaves.

steps.title: Ask if a preloader is needed
steps.do: First ask whether the preloader is needed. A progressive reveal of real content (headline, then image) gives the same feeling without hiding the page.
steps.how: NN/g lists popups and splash screens among the most disliked homepage elements, except where legally required.
steps.label: evidence

steps.title: Short, skippable, once per session
steps.do: If you keep it: show it once per session, make it very short, let any key press or click skip it, and remove it from the page afterwards.
steps.how: Store a session flag; skip entirely under reduced motion. WCAG 2.2.2 notes a preload animation may count as essential only when users cannot interact during the preload and the animation signals progress.
steps.label: our-take
steps.status_note: the session flag and skip behavior are our judgement

steps.title: Narrow skip keydown handler
steps.do: Expect the audit to flag a document-level keydown handler for the skip, and keep the handler narrow: it only removes the curtain, then unregisters itself.
steps.how: The audit counts addEventListener('keydown') on window or document at registration time and reports a11y-char-shortcuts as 'incomplete' (a person must check), not as a failure. Registering on the curtain element is not possible because it is not focusable and has pointer-events:none. Remove the listener inside done() and do not map any individual key to another action.
steps.label: our-take
steps.status_note: the audit printed 'check [major] a11y-char-shortcuts: 1 document-level keydown handler(s) registered' for the demo; no failure

steps.title: Read session flag before paint
steps.do: Read the session flag and the reduced-motion setting in a tiny inline script before first paint, and add the 'intro-on' class only if the intro should play.
steps.how: If the decision is made after paint, returning visitors see the curtain flash. A one-line synchronous script in the head (sessionStorage.getItem plus matchMedia, wrapped in try/catch because storage can throw) avoids that. This is the one head script this recipe allows; keep it under about 300 bytes and put everything else at the end of the body. Measured with the audit: LCP 40 to 50 ms, CLS 0.000, TBT 0 ms with it.
steps.label: our-take
steps.status_note: the cost of the script was measured in lab runs; the flash it prevents was reasoned about, not recorded

steps.title: Decorative curtain mechanics
steps.do: Implement the intro as a decorative curtain: aria-hidden, position:fixed, pointer-events:none, animated with transform only and finishing in visibility:hidden, removed from the DOM on animationend, with a timeout as a safety net.
steps.how: The real page underneath is already painted and interactive. Hide the curtain by default in CSS and show it only when a flag is set, so with JavaScript off it never appears (add a noscript rule too). Any key press or pointerdown calls the same done() function, which removes the curtain, removes both listeners and stores the session flag. Playwright confirmed: curtain present at 100 ms, removed by 1.75 s, removed within 80 ms after Space or a click, absent after a reload in the same session, never present under reduced motion or with JavaScript off.
steps.label: our-take

steps.title: Never delay main content
steps.do: Never delay the main content for the animation. Measure LCP with and without the preloader; the page content loads underneath it.
steps.how: Make the LCP resource discoverable in the initial HTML and not lazy-loaded; keep render-blocking CSS and head scripts small.
steps.label: craft-consensus

steps.title: Measure LCP and CLS both ways
steps.do: Measure LCP and CLS twice, with the flag unset and with it preset, using a PerformanceObserver; the difference should be noise.
steps.how: In Playwright, run once normally and once with addInitScript("sessionStorage.setItem('flag','1')"), and observe largest-contentful-paint and layout-shift with buffered:true. Demo result in lab Chrome: with the curtain LCP 52 ms (h1), without 36 ms (h1), CLS 0 in both; the curtain's own text was not the LCP element.
steps.label: craft-consensus
steps.status_note: single-run lab numbers on a local file; field data will differ

steps.title: Overlay exit moves nothing
steps.do: The overlay leaving must not move content: reserve all space, animate with transform and opacity, and keep fonts and images from reflowing.
steps.how: Set width and height or aspect-ratio on images and video, reserve space for anything that arrives late, and animate transform and opacity rather than top, left or box-shadow so the overlay leaving does not move content. Check layout shift in a performance trace across the whole sequence.
steps.label: craft-consensus

steps.title: Minmax tracks and wrapping buttons
steps.do: Use minmax(0, 1fr) for hero grid tracks, minmax(min(15rem, 100%), 1fr) for card grids, and overflow-wrap: anywhere with max-width: 100% on buttons and long call-to-action labels, so nothing stretches the page at 320 px with 200% text.
steps.how: Measured 2026-11-06 in Chrome (Playwright, channel chrome) on the recipe demo page at 320 px with the root font size at 200% and the audit probes; a 1fr track sized to its min-content gave a 335 px column, cards at minmax(15rem,1fr) were 480 px; after the changes scrollWidth was 320.
steps.label: standard
steps.measured: Measured 2026-11-06 in Chrome (Playwright, channel chrome) on the recipe demo page at 320 px with the root font size at 200% and the audit probes; a 1fr track sized to its min-content gave a 335 px column, cards at minmax(15rem,1fr) were 480 px; after the changes scrollWidth was 320.

steps.title: Avoid the cream-terracotta-serif reflex
steps.do: If the page uses cream, terracotta and serif display type together, that trips distinct-palette-not-reflex-cream and an HTML comment does not satisfy the audit: pick sans headings or another palette unless the brief requires the combination, and record the reason in direction.md.
steps.how: Measured 2026-11-06 in Chrome (Playwright, channel chrome) on the recipe demo page at 320 px with the root font size at 200% and the audit probes; advisory failed with cream, terracotta and serif; it passed after switching to bold system sans headings. The check is static and ignores comments.
steps.label: our-take
steps.measured: Measured 2026-11-06 in Chrome (Playwright, channel chrome) on the recipe demo page at 320 px with the root font size at 200% and the audit probes; advisory failed with cream, terracotta and serif; it passed after switching to bold system sans headings. The check is static and ignores comments.
steps.status_note: Recorded from one audit run on one demo page; the audit check is a heuristic and the technique has no independent source.

recipes.generate_hint: Default to no preloader; if one is required keep it once-per-session, skippable, non-blocking, free of layout shift, and off under reduced motion.

recipes.title: Unusual navigation, asymmetric and app-like layouts
recipes.summary: Spend your convention budget deliberately. Be unusual in looks and composition while keeping a visible way to reach the main sections, a logical code order, a skip link and a working keyboard path.
recipes.keep: Expressive navigation, off-grid composition, dock and command-palette patterns, app-like shells.
recipes.avoid: Hiding all navigation on desktop; reordering content visually without reordering the code; sticky elements that cover focus; keyboard-only shortcuts as the sole way in.

steps.title: Keep primary sections visible
steps.do: On desktop keep the primary sections visible as links, even in a compact or unusual form. On mobile show up to four directly; use a menu button for more, and add in-page links to key content.
steps.how: In the cited study navigation was used in 27% of desktop tasks when hidden versus 48% visible (2016, six sites). A command palette or hamburger can supplement visible links.
steps.label: evidence

steps.title: Skip link and landmarks
steps.do: Put a skip link first in the DOM, and use landmarks (header, nav, main, footer) with labels where there are several.
steps.how: A skip link (technique G1) should be the first focusable control; WCAG does not require it to be visible when it lacks focus, so one that appears on focus passes, though always visible is preferred. WebAIM: a hidden-until-focus link must become prominently visible on focus, and display:none or the hidden attribute must not be used. Landmarks (ARIA11) or headings (H69) also satisfy 2.4.1, and WebAIM notes a starting h1 or main region can meet it. Layering: give the skip link a z-index above positioned hero layers (a position:relative hero later in the DOM paints over an unpositioned skip link and hides it on focus); the recipe demo pages caught this in a real browser.
steps.label: craft-consensus

steps.title: Disclosure buttons for dropdowns
steps.do: Build site-navigation dropdowns as disclosure buttons, not ARIA menus: a real button with aria-expanded (aria-controls is optional in the pattern), Enter and Space toggle it, Escape closes the dropdown and returns focus to the button, and the link for the current page carries aria-current="page".
steps.how: APG's disclosure navigation example states it deliberately does not use the ARIA menu role, because typical site navigation does not need menu keyboard behavior. Tab moves through buttons and links; arrow keys, Home and End are optional additions. Test with a screen reader.
steps.label: craft-consensus

steps.title: Command palette as native dialog
steps.do: Build a command palette as a native dialog opened with showModal(), containing a labelled combobox input, a listbox with tabindex=-1, a visible Close button and a role=status line for the result count. Opening moves focus to the input, Escape clears the text first and then closes, and closing returns focus to the button that opened it.
steps.how: Keyboard pass in Chrome 2026-11-06: Ctrl+K and Enter or Space on the Search buttons open it with focus in the input; typing filters and aria-activedescendant resolves to an option; Down and Up move it with wrap; Enter on an option closes the dialog, updates the hash and focuses the target section; the first Escape clears the text, the second closes and focus returns to the opener. Tab never reaches the page behind (native showModal makes it inert; the Tab after the last control goes to the browser UI, not the page). Pitfall measured: when the listbox has overflow:auto and its options overflow, Chrome makes the listbox itself a Tab stop (an extra stop between the input and the Close button); tabindex="-1" on the listbox removes it, which is correct here because the options are reached through aria-activedescendant. Options are plain role=option items, so the same destinations must also exist as real links elsewhere (the demo builds the palette from the footer site index).
steps.label: craft-consensus

steps.title: Keep DOM in reading order
steps.do: Compose off-grid with CSS Grid areas and positioning while keeping the DOM in reading order. Avoid using order or absolute positioning to rearrange content that carries sequence.
steps.how: WCAG 1.3.2: failure F1 is CSS positioning that changes meaning; technique C27 makes the DOM order match the visual order. MDN: the CSS order property changes only the visual order, not the logical or tab order, and creates a mismatch for screen reader and keyboard users. Disabling CSS to read the order is a practical check (inferred; not described on WCAG's page).
steps.label: craft-consensus

steps.title: Sticky bars must not hide focus
steps.do: Sticky docks, headers and banners must not hide the focused element; leave room with scroll padding.
steps.how: WCAG technique C43 (CSS scroll-padding) is the only sufficient technique listed for 2.4.11; failure F110 is a sticky header or footer that completely hides focused elements, and partial covering is allowed. A sticky banner can also pass by being modal, closing when it loses focus, or not overlapping content. MDN's scroll-padding page shows the fixed-header anchor case. Test with the keyboard at several viewport sizes.
steps.label: craft-consensus

code.text: html { scroll-padding-top: var(--dock-height); }

steps.title: Bottom dock needs scroll padding
steps.do: A fixed bottom dock needs scroll-padding-bottom and matching body padding, not only scroll-padding-top. Make the dock fixed only when the viewport leaves room (for example min-width:20em and min-height:30em); below that let it sit in the page flow.
steps.how: Measured 2026-11-06 in Chrome with a real Tab pass over 28 stops of the demo page: with scroll-padding-bottom and body padding, no focused element was covered at 1440x900 or 390x844. Removing both left 2 stops partly covered at 1440x900 (one 4 of 5 sample points) and 11 stops partly covered at 390x844. The audit's own check only fails when a focus target is entirely covered, so these partial covers are invisible to it; WCAG 2.4.11 allows partial covering but a link 80% under the dock is not usable. A dock that stays fixed at 320x225 (400% zoom) would take about a third of the viewport, so below the size query it falls back to a static bar at the end of the page (checked: 0 covered stops at 320x225, 640x450, 390x844, 1440x900).
steps.label: craft-consensus

steps.title: Single-key shortcuts can be turned off
steps.do: Single-key shortcuts (for example "/" or "k") can be turned off or only work when their component has focus; the same actions are reachable by ordinary controls.
steps.how: List every single-key shortcut (letters, numbers, punctuation, symbols, including those needing Shift, and sequences such as G then A). Each must be able to be turned off, remapped to include a non-printable key, or be active only while its component has focus (technique G217; failure F99). Give each a visible button equivalent as good practice.
steps.label: craft-consensus

steps.title: Use a modifier for palette shortcut
steps.do: Use Ctrl or Command plus a key (for example Ctrl+K) for a palette shortcut and keep the visible button. Expect the audit to list the document-level keydown handler as 'check' for a11y-char-shortcuts; answer it by showing the shortcut needs a modifier.
steps.how: WCAG 2.1.4 covers shortcuts made of letters, numbers, punctuation or symbols only; a shortcut that needs a modifier such as Ctrl is not covered. Measured 2026-11-06: a single document keydown listener for Ctrl/Cmd+K makes the audit report a11y-char-shortcuts as 'check' (not a failure) because it cannot tell modifier shortcuts from single-key ones.
steps.label: craft-consensus
steps.status_note: audit behaviour measured; the claim that modifier shortcuts are outside 2.1.4 is from the WCAG understanding page

steps.title: Hide JavaScript-only controls
steps.do: Controls that only work with JavaScript (the palette buttons) start with the hidden attribute and are revealed by the script that wires them. Add [hidden] { display: none !important } because author display rules such as display:flex override the attribute. All routes stay plain anchors so the page works with JavaScript off.
steps.how: Found with a JavaScript-off Playwright pass 2026-11-06: a .controls { display:flex } rule overrode the hidden attribute, so dead Previous and Next buttons stayed visible; adding the !important rule hid them. With JavaScript off the demo still reaches every section by Tab and Enter on the rail, the dock or the footer index.
steps.label: craft-consensus

steps.title: Logo links home
steps.do: Keep the logo linking home in a findable place, even in an unusual layout.
steps.how: Conventional placement (top-left in left-to-right languages) is the safe default.
steps.label: evidence

steps.title: Collapse to one column at 320 px
steps.do: App shells and split screens collapse to a single column at narrow widths (320 CSS px) without two-dimensional scrolling.
steps.how: Check at 320 px wide and at 400% zoom.
steps.label: craft-consensus

steps.title: Test reflow at 320 px and 200%
steps.do: Test reflow twice: at a 320 px viewport and at 320 px with the root font size raised to 200%. Let nav lists wrap, switch to multi-column grids only above a breakpoint (rem column gaps in a 12-column grid add up to more than 320 px at 200% text), and add overflow-wrap:anywhere to paragraphs that hold long strings such as email addresses and to headings and labels. Give a one-column form grid grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr), or its inputs and buttons stretch it past the viewport (a heading that cannot break, 333 px in a 256 px column at 200% text, also overflowed).
steps.how: Measured 2026-11-06 with html { font-size: 200% } at a 320 px viewport: the first draft of the demo scrolled horizontally because (1) a 12-column hero grid with 1rem gaps needed 11 rem of gap (352 px at 200%), (2) the dock was one non-wrapping row of five 3.5 rem buttons, and (3) an email address could not break. After a grid that starts at 48em, a wrapping dock list, a static dock below the size query and overflow-wrap:anywhere, scrollWidth equalled clientWidth at 320 px for 100% and 200% text. The audit's reflow probe only checks 100% text, so none of this showed up there.
steps.label: craft-consensus

steps.title: Justify each unconventional choice
steps.do: Write down why each unconventional choice earns its cost, and keep the rest of the page conventional.
steps.how: One or two surprises per page is a workable limit; this is a judgement, not a measured number.
steps.label: our-take
steps.status_note: our judgement

steps.title: Menu role for action menus only
steps.do: Use role=menu only for action menus and implement every key the APG lists, or use a disclosure instead.
steps.how: Keyboard-test: open with Enter, Space, Down; move with arrows (Home/End); Escape returns focus to the button; Tab closes. Check aria-expanded flips. (Derived from the rule; see its sources.)
steps.label: craft-consensus

steps.title: Site nav without menu roles
steps.do: Build header menus as nav > ul with a button[aria-expanded] per dropdown and plain links inside.
steps.how: In header nav: assert no [role=menu|menubar|menuitem]; submenus triggered by button[aria-expanded]; first link of an opened list follows the button in focus order; nav has accessible name when more than one. (Derived from the rule; see its sources.)
steps.label: craft-consensus
steps.status_note: generated from a craft-consensus rule; the technique itself was not separately verified

steps.title: Prefer native select
steps.do: Prefer a native select; build a custom listbox only with full APG keys and short option labels.
steps.how: Inspect roles and states; keyboard test Up/Down/Home/End and typing a letter; scan options for nested a/button/input. (Derived from the rule; see its sources.)
steps.label: craft-consensus

steps.title: Combobox focus stays in the input
steps.do: Keep DOM focus in the input and move aria-activedescendant through the options.
steps.how: Open the popup and assert on the input: role=combobox, aria-expanded=true, aria-controls resolves to a visible listbox, aria-activedescendant changes with Down arrow and resolves to an option; label via label/aria-labelledby. (Derived from the rule; see its sources.)
steps.label: craft-consensus

steps.title: Combobox keyboard keys per APG
steps.do: Implement Down, Up, Enter, Escape and Alt+Down exactly as the APG lists.
steps.how: Type, press Down, Enter, Escape, Tab in order and verify each outcome and that focus never leaves the input. (Derived from the rule; see its sources.)
steps.label: craft-consensus

steps.title: Provide a second route
steps.do: Provide main navigation and a second route (search, sitemap or footer index) on every multi-page site.
steps.how: Pick 3 inner pages and show two independent routes to each (nav + search, nav + sitemap, home page links + previous/next). Process pages (checkout steps, search results) are exempt. (Derived from the rule; see its sources.)
steps.label: craft-consensus

steps.title: Link text names the destination
steps.do: Write link text that names the destination and say 'PDF, 2 MB' or 'opens in a new window' when it applies.
steps.how: Collect all anchors with accessible names. Fail if two different hrefs share the same name, if a name matches /^(click here|here|more|read more|link|this)$/i or contains 'link', if an href ends in a document extension without format and size in the name, or if target=_blank lacks a notice placed after the main text. (Derived from the rule; see its sources.)
steps.label: craft-consensus
steps.status_note: generated from a craft-consensus rule; the technique itself was not separately verified

steps.title: Breakpoints where content breaks
steps.do: Build the layout with fluid grid rules first and add a breakpoint in em only where you can see the content break.
steps.how: Sweep the viewport from 320 to 1920 px in 40px steps. At each step assert no horizontal scrollbar (scrollWidth <= clientWidth), no element overlapping its sibling's box, and the measure rule still passes. Inspect media queries: list breakpoint values and flag any matching device presets (375, 414, 768 and 1024 px) written in px for review. (Derived from the rule; see its sources.)
steps.label: craft-consensus
steps.status_note: generated from a craft-consensus rule; the technique itself was not separately verified

recipes.generate_hint: Be inventive in layout but keep visible primary links on desktop, a skip link first, code order equal to reading order, sticky elements that do not cover focus, a single-column reflow at 320 px, and a written reason for each unconventional choice.

recipes.title: Drag interactions and horizontal scrolling
recipes.summary: Keep the tactile, sideways-moving feel. Add buttons and keys that do the same thing, make sure a single tap works, and let narrow screens stack the content.
recipes.keep: Draggable galleries, swipe rows, horizontally scrolling sections.
recipes.avoid: Drag as the only way to move; scroll containers that keyboards cannot reach; horizontal scroll that cannot reflow; gestures that need two fingers.

steps.title: Previous and next buttons
steps.do: Provide previous and next buttons (visible, labelled, 24 px or larger) for every draggable or swipeable row; dragging stays as a bonus.
steps.how: Single pointer, no drag required (technique G219). WCAG's own carousel example has forward and back buttons that may be visually hidden but must be pointer-operable. At either end, mark the button aria-disabled="true" (and style it as disabled) rather than hiding it or using the disabled attribute, which can drop keyboard focus when the pressed button disables itself (our judgement; Chrome behaviour with disabled not measured).
steps.label: craft-consensus

steps.title: Mouse-only drag that keeps taps
steps.do: Add mouse drag only for pointerType 'mouse', without pointer capture, and keep taps working: ignore moves under 5 px, set pointer-events:none on links while a drag is in progress, call preventDefault on dragstart, switch scroll-snap off during the drag and back on after it, and add scroll-padding-inline equal to the scroller's padding so the first card snaps to scrollLeft 0. Leave touch and pen to native scrolling (no two-finger gesture).
steps.how: Playwright 2026-11-06: a 200 px mouse drag moved the strip one card (292 px) and left the URL hash empty; a drag that started on a card link did not follow the link; a plain click on a link followed it; a CDP touch swipe scrolled the strip natively (288 px). Without scroll-padding-inline the first card snapped at scrollLeft 4, which left Previous enabled at the start.
steps.label: craft-consensus

steps.title: aria-disabled at either end
steps.do: Give Previous and Next visible text (an SVG arrow with aria-hidden is fine) and use aria-disabled="true" rather than the disabled attribute at either end, ignoring clicks while it is set, so a keyboard user who presses Next to the end keeps focus on the button.
steps.how: Measured 2026-11-06: pressing Enter on Next 12 times left document.activeElement on Next at the end (aria-disabled). Icon-only buttons whose text was an arrow character made axe report color-contrast and label-content-name-mismatch as 'incomplete' (non-text characters, unverifiable label); visible words Previous and Next with an aria-hidden SVG produced no axe violations or incompletes. Not measured: what Chrome does with focus when a focused button gets the disabled attribute; the aria-disabled choice is our judgement about avoiding that.
steps.label: our-take
steps.status_note: focus staying on an aria-disabled button measured; the alternative with disabled was not measured

steps.title: Keyboard-scrollable row
steps.do: Make sure keyboard users can reach and scroll the row: if the items are focusable, the browser scrolls focus into view; if the scroller has no focusable children, the scroller itself must be focusable.
steps.how: Chrome makes scrollers with no focusable children keyboard-focusable by default (announced for 130, rollout delayed to 132); with focusable children, Tab goes to the children. Deque's axe rule: make the scroller or a static element inside it focusable (tabindex="0"); a region whose only content is tabindex="-1" controls fails. Avoid tabindex="-1" on a scroller users need. Accessible names for scrollers are not addressed by the Chrome or Deque pages; MDN says a bare div cannot take aria-label, so a name would need a role that supports one.
steps.label: craft-consensus
steps.status_note: naming a focusable scroller is not covered by any page read

steps.title: Inert cards that are mostly off-screen
steps.do: Make the scroller a labelled region with tabindex=0 and set inert on cards that are less than half visible (IntersectionObserver rooted at the scroller), except a card that contains focus. Without JavaScript every card link stays focusable and the browser scrolls it into view.
steps.how: Measured 2026-11-06 in Chrome at 1280 px: scroll-snap-type:x mandatory with a focused scroller scrolled by arrow keys (scrollLeft 4, 292, 580: one card per press), so no custom key handler was needed; Home and End did not scroll it. With inert on off-screen cards, Tab from the scroller reached only the 4 visible card links of 8 and each landed inside the scroller box. With JavaScript off, ArrowRight scrolled the scroller and Tab reached the last card link (scrollLeft 1176).
