This resolves the tension between dh-keyboard (focusable items scroll into view) and the content-slider rule (hidden slides' links not focusable): use inert when JavaScript runs and leave the links focusable when it does not.
steps.label: craft-consensus

steps.title: Stack items on narrow screens
steps.do: Below a narrow width, stack the items in a single vertical column or let the row wrap, instead of requiring horizontal scrolling for the whole page.
steps.how: WCAG Reflow: vertically scrolling content at 320 CSS px wide and horizontally scrolling content at 256 CSS px tall, without two-dimensional scrolling. A horizontal carousel passes if each panel fits within 320 px (G225); a table in its own scrollable container passes if the surrounding content reflows; exceptions cover maps, diagrams, video, games, presentations, data tables and toolbar-in-view interfaces.
steps.label: craft-consensus

steps.title: Check stacked layout at 200% text
steps.do: Check the stacked layout at a 320 px viewport with the root font size at 200% as well: let nav lists wrap and add overflow-wrap:anywhere to paragraphs that contain long strings such as email addresses and to headings, and give flex children that hold a heading min-width:0.
steps.how: Measured 2026-11-06 with html { font-size: 200% } at 320 px: the nav list (display:flex without wrap) and an email link in the help section scrolled the page horizontally. flex-wrap:wrap and overflow-wrap:anywhere fixed both; afterwards no body descendant extended beyond the viewport.
steps.label: craft-consensus

steps.title: Script-revealed prev and next
steps.do: Previous and Next start with the hidden attribute and are revealed by the script that wires them, with [hidden] { display: none !important } in the CSS. Hide them too in the stacked layout where there is nothing to scroll.
steps.how: JavaScript-off Playwright pass 2026-11-06: the author rule .controls { display:flex } overrode the hidden attribute and left dead buttons on screen; the !important rule fixed it. Stacked widths 320, 390 and 640 px had no horizontal scroll and the strip had no overflow.
steps.label: craft-consensus

steps.title: Use a native range input
steps.do: Prefer input type=range; add output text next to it and aria-valuetext when units matter.
steps.how: Inspect value attributes; keyboard test arrows/Home/End/PageUp/PageDown; check aria-valuetext shows units; test with VoiceOver on iOS or TalkBack. (Derived from the rule; see its sources.)
steps.label: craft-consensus

steps.title: Scroll-snap sliders without autoplay
steps.do: Build sliders as scroll-snap lists with labelled prev/next buttons and no autoplay.
steps.how: Load the page for 30 seconds without input: nothing moves. Tab through: arrows reachable, scroller focusable with visible focus, hidden slides' links not focusable. Check prev/next buttons have names. (Derived from the rule; see its sources.)
steps.label: craft-consensus
steps.status_note: generated from a craft-consensus rule; the technique itself was not separately verified

steps.title: Breakpoints where content breaks
steps.do: Build the layout with fluid grid rules first and add a breakpoint in em only where you can see the content break.
steps.how: Sweep the viewport from 320 to 1920 px in 40px steps. At each step assert no horizontal scrollbar (scrollWidth <= clientWidth), no element overlapping its sibling's box, and the measure rule still passes. Inspect media queries: list breakpoint values and flag any matching device presets (375, 414, 768 and 1024 px) written in px for review. (Derived from the rule; see its sources.)
steps.label: craft-consensus
steps.status_note: generated from a craft-consensus rule; the technique itself was not separately verified

steps.title: Name the strip so audits check it
steps.do: Name the strip with a 'carousel' class (or any element the audit's carousel selector matches) so the audit raises the drag and pointer-gesture rules for human review instead of marking them not applicable.
steps.how: The audit's gesture probe counts draggable=true attributes, range inputs, canvases and carousel library classes. A strip that uses only pointer events and has no matching class is reported as 'not applicable' for a11y-dragging and a11y-pointer-gestures, which hides the one place a drag alternative must be checked. Measured by reading the probe source and by the 'check' status the demo received once its wrapper used the class carousel.
steps.label: our-take
steps.status_note: about the audit tool, not WCAG; the real fix is a better probe

recipes.generate_hint: Every drag or swipe gets visible buttons and arrow-key support, works with a single tap, and stacks vertically at narrow widths.

recipes.title: Oversized and expressive type, and theme switching
recipes.summary: Keep the giant, characterful type. Size it in a way that still scales with the user's settings, keep headings real headings, and keep switches between modes predictable.
recipes.keep: Huge headlines, lettering, theme or mode changes.
recipes.avoid: Type sized only in viewport units; headlines as images; lettering that is the only place the page states its purpose; mode switches that rename things.

steps.title: Big type in rem, not viewport units
steps.do: Size big type in rem or em, stepped at breakpoints, with no viewport units in font-size. Keep the smallest-breakpoint size at least 40% of the largest so a high page zoom can still reach twice the 100% size. Keep the largest hero size at 6rem (96 px) or less and the hero headline under 40 characters: the audit's distinct-hero-headline-proportion fails a hero above 96 px, and one of 72 px or more with 40 or more characters.
steps.how: Measured 2026-11-05 in headless Chrome (see content/learn/measurements/type-zoom-2026-11-05.json): at 100% the sizes were 118 (clamp with vw), 112 (stepped rem) and 102 px (8vw). Under 200% text-only enlargement: stepped rem doubled to 224 px; clamp with vw grew only to 134 px (1.14×); 8vw did not change (1.0×). Under 200% page zoom the breakpoint shrank the sizes: stepped rem showed 80 and 96 device px against 112 at 100%. WCAG accepts shrinking at small breakpoints if 200% is still reachable; computed at the 500% browser maximum, a 2.5rem small size reaches 200 px (1.79×, short) and a 3rem small size reaches 240 px (2.14×). WCAG lists viewport-unit misuse as failure F94. Measured 2026-11-06: at 7rem the audit reported '112 px is over 96 px, 112 px and 61 characters'; at 6rem with a 38-character h1 no failure (small size 3rem is 50% of the large).
steps.label: craft-consensus

steps.title: Wrap everything, check 320 px at 200%
steps.do: Put overflow-wrap:anywhere on h1, h2 and paragraphs, and let nav lists wrap, then check a 320 px viewport with the root font size at 200%.
steps.how: Measured 2026-11-06 at 320 px with html { font-size: 200% }: h1 was 96 px and did not scroll the page (overflow-wrap:anywhere), but the nav list (display:flex without wrap) scrolled it to 461 px, and long words such as 'pavement.' overflowed their cards (price text at 64 px inside 144 px of content). After flex-wrap:wrap and overflow-wrap:anywhere on p, no element extended beyond the viewport.
steps.label: craft-consensus

steps.title: Smallest size at half the largest
steps.do: If 200% must be reachable at 400% page zoom (not only at the 500% browser maximum), keep the smallest breakpoint size at or above half of the largest (for example 3.5rem against 7rem) instead of 40%.
steps.how: Measured 2026-11-06 on the demo (h1 3rem, 4rem at 48em, 7rem at 80em; 1280 px screen): device pixels of the h1 were 112 at 100%, 96 at 200% (0.86x), 144 at 300%, 192 at 400% (1.71x) and 240 at 500% (2.14x). Under text-only enlargement (root font size 200%) it was 224 (2.00x). So the 40% rule from bt-scalable gives 2x only at about 500%. Raising the small size to 3.5rem would give 224 device px at 400% (computed, not rendered).
steps.label: our-take
steps.status_note: the 3.5rem figure is arithmetic from the measured sizes; a person must judge whether 56 px headings still fit a 320 px column

steps.title: Headlines as real heading text
steps.do: Headlines and key labels are real text in real heading elements, even if they are drawn with a custom face; avoid images of text.
steps.how: WCAG 1.4.5: use real text when the technology can achieve the look. Images of text are allowed only for logotypes, when the presentation is essential, or when users can customize them. Repeating the heading as real text next to decorative lettering is a common mitigation but is not a listed exception.
steps.label: craft-consensus

steps.title: Predictable mode switch
steps.do: A theme or mode switch keeps the same labels, order and positions across modes, remembers the choice, starts from the system preference, and announces its state.
steps.how: Use a toggle button with aria-pressed and a label that does not change (for example "Dark mode"), or a button whose label changes ("Switch to dark" / "Switch to light") without aria-pressed; do not combine them (APG button pattern). Read prefers-color-scheme (Baseline widely available since January 2020) for the initial state. MDN's page does not cover manual overrides, so store the user's choice yourself.
steps.label: craft-consensus

steps.title: Light, dark and system radios
steps.do: For Light, Dark and System, use a fieldset with a legend and three native radios (labels never change), an inline script in the head that applies a saved explicit choice before first paint, CSS that follows prefers-color-scheme unless data-theme says otherwise (with color-scheme set), a role=status line stating the current theme, and the switch hidden until JavaScript runs. Choosing System removes the saved value.
steps.how: Playwright keyboard pass 2026-11-06 with the OS set to dark: the page starts as System and dark; Tab lands once on the checked radio; ArrowLeft selects Dark then Light (background changes, localStorage written, status text updates); the choice survives reload; labels and positions are identical in light and dark; choosing System clears the value and follows a live OS change from dark to light; with JavaScript off the page follows the OS and the switch is hidden. axe-core found no violations or incompletes in light, in dark through the OS setting, in dark through data-theme, and with data-theme=light over an OS dark setting.
steps.label: craft-consensus

steps.title: Name toggles after the setting
steps.do: Name toggles after the setting ('Dark mode') and flip only aria-pressed or aria-checked.
steps.how: Toggle each control and assert its accessible name is identical before and after, aria-checked/aria-pressed/checked is explicit 'true' or 'false', and Space toggles it. (Derived from the rule; see its sources.)
steps.label: craft-consensus
steps.status_note: generated from a craft-consensus rule; the technique itself was not separately verified

steps.title: Headline as one buyer's result
steps.do: Write the headline as the result one named buyer gets, using a noun or number only this product can claim.
steps.how: Read the H1 and subhead alone. (1) Does it say what is offered and for whom? (2) Paste it with a competitor's name: does it still read true? If yes, fail. (3) Fail if it matches the template 'The [AI-powered|modern|all-in-one] [noun] for [teams|businesses|everyone]'. (Derived from the rule; see its sources.)
steps.label: craft-consensus
steps.status_note: generated from a craft-consensus rule; the technique itself was not separately verified

steps.title: Headings that state the finding
steps.do: Write each heading as the finding of its section, so the headings alone tell the story.
steps.how: Extract the heading outline. Fail any heading matching the blocklist (case-insensitive: introduction, overview, features, benefits, our approach, why us, about, welcome). Then read the outline alone: a reader should be able to say what the page offers. (Derived from the rule; see its sources.)
steps.label: craft-consensus
steps.status_note: generated from a craft-consensus rule; the technique itself was not separately verified

steps.title: Cap line length near 55ch
steps.do: Wrap every block of running text in a container with max-inline-size of about 50ch to 55ch (never above 60ch) and let the container, not the viewport, decide the line length.
steps.how: At widths 320, 768, 1280 and 1920 px, find every paragraph/list-item/blockquote with more than two lines of text. Compute characters per line (text length divided by rendered line count, or compute container inline-size divided by the width of one '0' glyph, i.e. in ch). Fail if any exceeds 75. For the lower bound, where the viewport allows it (>= 768px), flag single-column text below 45 characters per line for manual review. (Derived from the rule; see its sources.)
steps.label: craft-consensus
steps.status_note: generated from a craft-consensus rule; the technique itself was not separately verified

steps.title: Stepped rem sizes for headings
steps.do: Set headline sizes in rem and step them at em/rem media queries (for example 3rem, 4rem, 7rem), keeping the smallest at least 40% of the largest; do not use clamp(rem + vw) for text that must scale; test at 200% zoom and 320 px.
steps.how: Measured in Chrome 2026-11-05 (content/learn/measurements/type-zoom-2026-11-05.json): clamp(rem + vw) and vw sizes did not reach 200% at 200% zoom; stepped rem with small >= 40% of large did. See also step bt-scalable in big-type-and-modes.
steps.label: craft-consensus

recipes.generate_hint: Use fluid type that includes a rem component, keep headings as real text, and keep mode switches predictable and announced.

recipes.title: Editorial, newspaper and serif-led layouts that read easily
recipes.summary: Keep the serif headlines, the columns, the rules and the front-page hierarchy. Hold body text at 18px or more, write in short plain sentences, keep tables as real tables, and give the page a paper colour that is not the default cream.
recipes.keep: Large serif display type, multi-column text, rules between stories, pull quotes, mastheads, a lead story that is bigger than the rest, captions and bylines.
recipes.avoid: Sentences over 25 words and grade-12 prose; justified text without hyphenation; kicker labels above every heading; a kicker above the main headline; dashes in headings; cream paper with a terracotta accent by reflex; thin serif cuts at body size; tables drawn as images or divs; a feed made of identical cards.

steps.title: Body at 1.125rem, 55ch measure
steps.do: Set running text at 1.125rem (18px) with line-height 1.55 and cap every text block at 55ch. Captions may drop to 0.875rem; nothing else goes below 1rem.
steps.how: Measured 2026-11-06 in Chrome 156 via Playwright (channel "chrome"): on a test article the smallest computed size of p, li, td and th was 18px at both 320 and 1280 px viewports, with no horizontal overflow. Butterick advises 15 to 25 px for web body text and an average line length of 45 to 90 characters (66ch is the usual target). A rem size lets the user's browser setting scale the page.
steps.label: craft-consensus

steps.title: Multi-column text with hairline rule
steps.do: Build newspaper columns with CSS multi-column (column-width, not a fixed count), a hairline column-rule, and column-span: all on headings. Keep text start-aligned; justify only with hyphens: auto and a lang attribute on html.
steps.how: Measured 2026-11-06 in Chrome 156 via Playwright (channel "chrome"): with columns: 22rem 3 the text ran in one 288 px column at 320 px and three 363 px columns at 1280 px, and scrollWidth equalled the viewport width at both. Computed hyphens was auto on the justified paragraphs. Source order is the reading order in multi-column, so keyboard and screen reader order stay meaningful. WCAG 1.4.12 needs layouts that survive user text-spacing overrides, so give columns no fixed height.
steps.label: craft-consensus
steps.status_note: The reflow, hyphens and no-overflow facts were measured and the rule exception (justified plus hyphens plus lang) comes from the guidelines. The 22rem minimum column width (about 40 characters at 18px) is our judgement; Butterick advises 45 to 90 characters and says justified text needs hyphenation and wide enough lines, so very narrow justified columns can still look gappy. Not tested with a screen reader.

steps.title: One type scale, three heading levels
steps.do: Use one scale of body 1.125rem, h3 1.4rem, h2 1.75rem and an h1 stepped in rem (2.25rem, then 3.75rem from min-width: 48em); no clamp() with vw. Style at most three heading levels in articles, with at least one step of 1.25 or more.
steps.how: Measured 2026-11-06 in Chrome 156 via Playwright (channel "chrome"): computed sizes were 18, 22.4, 28 and 36 px at 320 px (step ratios 1.24, 1.25, 1.29) and 18, 22.4, 28 and 60 px at 1280 px (the h1 step is 2.14); the figures were taken with an earlier clamp(2.25rem, 1.6rem + 3vw, 3.75rem) h1, and the stepped sizes in the sample give the same 36 and 60 px at the two ends. The stepped rem sizes (small 2.25rem is 60% of large) scale with the user's text-size setting, whereas a clamp with a vw term was measured not to reach 200% (type-zoom-2026-11-05). Keep the h1 under 6rem and use line-height 1.05 to 1.15 on wrapped headlines. Butterick advises at most three heading levels (two is better) with the smallest visible size increment between them, so the display h1 is the one big step and h2 and h3 differ by roughly 1.25.
steps.label: craft-consensus

steps.title: Serif with an optical-size axis
steps.do: Choose a serif with an optical-size axis for body and display (Newsreader, Source Serif 4 and Literata all have opsz and wght axes) and keep Light cuts (weight 300 or below) for display lines of 24px and up. Body and captions stay at weight 400 or heavier.
steps.how: Google Fonts metadata (fetched 2026-11-06) lists Newsreader (opsz 6 to 72, wght 200 to 800), Source Serif 4 (opsz 8 to 60, wght 200 to 900) and Literata (opsz 7 to 72, wght 200 to 900) as variable serifs, none on the overused-font list in the display-font rule (Fraunces and Instrument Serif are). With font-optical-sizing: auto the face draws sturdier letterforms at small sizes. Delicate high-contrast faces such as Cormorant Garamond (weights 300 to 700) and Bodoni Moda (wght 400 to 900, opsz 6 to 96) belong at display size.
steps.label: craft-consensus
steps.status_note: Font axes and ranges were read from Google Fonts metadata. The 300-or-lighter-at-24px-and-up limit comes from the guideline, whose Apple HIG source was only partly read. Sample rendering of each face was not checked.

steps.title: Pick paper color for the subject
steps.do: Pick the paper colour for the subject. The palette above uses a cool newsprint grey (#EEF0F2) with near-black ink; if you want warm cream, record the subject reason and avoid pairing it with a terracotta accent and a serif display face by default.
steps.how: Computed with the WCAG 2 formula: ink on newsprint 15.74:1, muted captions 7.12:1, oxblood 7.9:1, link blue 6.9:1, white on oxblood 9.02:1. The rule colour #6F767E reaches 4.02:1 against the paper, so column rules and table lines that mark structure meet 3:1 (a lighter #8A9098 only reaches 2.81:1). Cream #F4F1EA matches the reflex-cream test (minimum channel 234, red at least green at least blue, red minus blue 10). Define every colour once as a role token.
steps.label: craft-consensus

steps.title: Limit kickers, arrows and dashes
steps.do: Limit kickers (small tracked labels above headings) to ceil(sections / 3) per page, none above the main headline. Use numbers only for real sequences, at most two arrow-ended links, one dot-separated meta line, and keep em dashes out of headings and under one per 300 words. Write headings and navigation in sentence case; set bylines and dates with layout (a dl or flex gap), not middle dots.
steps.how: The limits are the rules' own thresholds. Butterick rejects title case and all caps for headings; GOV.UK says to write all headings in sentence case. A front page can still carry a masthead and a section label where the label adds information (a section name such as "Local news" does; a decorative "01 / Stories" does not).
steps.label: craft-consensus
steps.status_note: Sentence case sources were read. The dash, arrow, kicker and middle-dot limits come from the detector-based guidelines, whose sources are partly read (impeccable-repo) or our-take (em dashes). Treat them as review thresholds.

steps.title: Short sentences and paragraphs
steps.do: Write each sentence at 25 words or fewer, averaging 20 or fewer; paragraphs of one idea and at most five sentences (marketing pages three); open every article or long section with a one- or two-sentence summary that states the conclusion; choose the plain word; start with the first real fact instead of a filler opener.
steps.how: Sources: GOV.UK, NN/g and COGA agree on short sentences, one idea per paragraph, conclusion first; WCAG 3.1.5 asks for a summary or simpler version when text needs more than lower-secondary reading ability. A quick local check with a rough Flesch-Kincaid script (our own syllable heuristic, not an official tool, so use Hemingway or textstat for real scoring) gave grade 1.9 and a longest sentence of 12 words for a four-sentence news brief, against grade 27 and one 34-word sentence for the same news set as one long clause. Long-form voice is a craft choice: a literary feature may exceed grade 9, so open it with a plain-language standfirst and record the exception.
steps.label: craft-consensus
steps.status_note: The thresholds and sources were read. The grade figures came from our own approximate script and are illustrative; the exact scores depend on the tool. Whether a literary feature should be held to grade 9 is our judgement.

steps.title: Real lists and captioned tables
steps.do: Turn three or more parallel items and every procedure into ul or ol. Mark data (schedules, results, specs) as a table with a caption, th scope="col" and scope="row". If the table is wider than its container, scroll it inside a labelled container with tabindex="0".
steps.how: Measured 2026-11-06 in Chrome 156 via Playwright (channel "chrome"): a 4-column table in a 288 px container with overflow-x: auto and no tabindex was flagged by axe-core 4.14 as scrollable-region-focusable (serious); adding tabindex="0", role="region" and aria-labelledby pointing at the caption cleared it, and the page itself did not overflow (scrollWidth 320). WCAG 1.4.10 lets a data table scroll in its own container as a two-dimensional exception, while headings and paging around it must still reflow.
steps.label: craft-consensus

steps.title: Lead story and varied blocks
steps.do: For a front page or feed, make one story the lead (larger headline, more room), vary the layout of the next blocks (a list, a two-up, a rule-separated column), vary section padding, and keep the HTML in the order a reader should meet the stories. Each story is li > heading > one link; extend the click area with a stretched a::after, not a wrapping anchor.
steps.how: The stretched-link pattern comes from Inclusive Components (cards); the grid measurements for the same pattern (one tab stop per card, tab order equal to source order, no axe violations) are in the bento-and-card-grids recipe. The rhythm targets (no layout family for more than two consecutive sections, at least four families in eight sections, non-identical section padding) are the guideline thresholds.
steps.label: craft-consensus
steps.status_note: Card markup was tested in a scratch page (see the bento recipe); the front-page rhythm advice is our judgement guided by the guideline thresholds, and its sources were partly read.

recipes.generate_hint: Serif headlines and real columns, body at 18px and 55ch, plain sentences with the summary first, a cool newsprint or subject-driven paper colour, real tables, one lead story and varied blocks.

recipes.title: Condensed display type and serif-sans pairings
recipes.summary: Keep the tall, tight display lines and the contrast between two typefaces. Set condensed headlines in sentence case, limit capitals to short labels with real letter-spacing, stay at two families, and make sure fallback fonts do not shift the layout.
recipes.keep: Narrow, tall display faces set large and tight; a deliberate serif and sans pairing; strong size and weight contrast.
recipes.avoid: Whole headlines or buttons in capitals; capitals with no letter-spacing; a third or fourth family added for flavour; condensed faces used for paragraphs; fixed-height boxes that clip when users loosen text spacing; font swaps that move the layout.

steps.title: Sentence case for condensed headlines
steps.do: Set condensed headlines in sentence case and let the tall letterforms carry the style. Use text-transform: uppercase only for labels of three words or fewer that fit on one line. Buttons stay in sentence case.
steps.how: Measured 2026-11-06 in Chrome 156 via Playwright (channel "chrome"): a scan of the computed styles on a test page (condensed h1 and h2 in sentence case, a one-line uppercase label "Issue 04") found one uppercase element, one line and 8 characters; the audit snippet below lists every uppercase element with its line count and length so you can enforce the limits in CI. Butterick: capitals are fine for less than one line and wrong for whole paragraphs. UX Movement recommends sentence case for button labels and discourages all caps because the lack of word shape lowers readability.
steps.label: craft-consensus

steps.title: Track uppercase labels 0.05 to 0.12em
steps.do: Give every uppercase or small-caps label letter-spacing between 0.05em and 0.12em (0.08em works). Keep body text at letter-spacing normal. A large condensed headline may be tightened slightly (about -0.01em); do not widen lowercase text.
steps.how: Measured 2026-11-06 in Chrome 156 via Playwright (channel "chrome"): the uppercase label computed to 0.08em; the h1 used -0.01em; the body paragraph stayed normal. Butterick recommends 5 to 12% extra space (0.05em to 0.12em in CSS) for capitals and small caps, and says lowercase letters do not ordinarily need letterspacing.
steps.label: craft-consensus

steps.title: Rem clamp sizing for condensed h1
steps.do: Size condensed display type in rem stepped at breakpoints (no clamp() with vw, which cannot reach 200% under text enlargement), keep the h1 at 6rem or below, wrap it with text-wrap: balance, and use a tight line-height only on headlines (0.9 to 1.05). Choose a condensed family from the subject rather than the first one that comes to mind: Barlow Condensed (static cuts), Sofia Sans Extra Condensed (variable weight 1 to 1000), Archivo (variable width 62 to 125, so one file gives you condensed and regular) all exist in Google Fonts.
steps.how: Google Fonts metadata (fetched 2026-11-06) confirms the three families and the Archivo wdth axis (62 to 125) and Sofia Sans Extra Condensed wght axis (1 to 1000). Because condensed glyphs are narrow, an h1 can be larger before it wraps, but keep to the 6rem cap and about 45 characters per line. Stepped rem sizes (3rem, 4.5rem, 6rem: the small size is 50% of the large) follow the browser text-size setting and reach 200%; a clamp() with a vw term was measured not to (Roselli; type-zoom-2026-11-05).
steps.label: craft-consensus
steps.status_note: Font availability and axes were read from metadata; the face names are examples chosen by us, not a ranking, and none was rendered. The 6rem cap and 45-character wrap come from the guidelines.

steps.title: Let headline blocks grow
steps.do: Leave condensed headline blocks to grow: no fixed height, no overflow: hidden on boxes that hold text, and tight line-height only on the headline itself. Test with the WCAG text-spacing override.
steps.how: Measured 2026-11-06 in Chrome 156 via Playwright (channel "chrome"): a 320 px card with a 0.9 line-height condensed-style headline, then the WCAG 1.4.12 overrides injected (line-height 1.5, letter-spacing 0.12em, word-spacing 0.16em, paragraph spacing 2em): the card grew from 234 to 533 px and scrollHeight still equalled clientHeight, so nothing was clipped and the page did not scroll sideways (scrollWidth 320). The test used the fallback face (Arial Narrow or Arial), not a web font.
steps.label: craft-consensus

steps.title: Exactly two type families
steps.do: For a serif and sans pairing, use exactly two families (plus mono for code if needed). Build hierarchy from size, weight, colour and case inside them: the display or headline face in one, the reading text in the other, and do not add a third face for pull quotes or buttons.
steps.how: Measured 2026-11-06 in Chrome 156 via Playwright (channel "chrome"): the audit below counted the first font-family of every rendered text element on a test page and returned two (Sofia Sans Extra Condensed and Newsreader). Pair for contrast in structure (a high-contrast serif with a plain sans, or a condensed display with a text serif) and make sure the two share a similar x-height at body size so the switch does not look accidental. Apple HIG and web.dev both point to a small number of families.
steps.label: our-take
steps.status_note: The two-family limit is a guideline we hold as our-take. The family count script was tested on a page whose web fonts were not loaded, so it reads the declared first family, which is what the guideline checks. No pairing quality claim was tested.

steps.title: Tune fallback metrics for swap
steps.do: Stop the swap from moving the layout: preload the one display file you need, use font-display: swap or optional, and tune the fallback face with size-adjust, ascent-override, descent-override and line-gap-override so its metrics match the web font. Keep CLS at 0.1 or below.
steps.how: web.dev (Optimize CLS): fonts can shift layout even while text is invisible because the fallback sets the layout; font-display: optional avoids a re-layout when the font is not ready; size-adjust and the related overrides reduce the size gap; a good CLS is 0.1 or less for at least 75% of visits. Compute the override values from the two fonts' metrics with a tool and measure CLS afterwards.
steps.label: craft-consensus
steps.status_note: The mechanism is from web.dev. No override values are given because they depend on the chosen pair, and a font-swap CLS measurement with real font files was not run.

recipes.generate_hint: Set condensed headlines large in sentence case, use capitals only for short tracked labels, keep to two families, and tune the fallback font so the swap does not move the layout.

recipes.title: Swiss grids, utilitarian interfaces and corporate-clean pages that are not generic
recipes.summary: Keep the strict grid, the plain type, the dense tables and the blue-and-white product look. Choose a display face that is not the default, keep table text at 16px, use labels sparingly, and show the real product so the page does not pass the swap test.
recipes.keep: A visible column grid, neutral grotesque type, strong alignment, small labels, rules, tables, system-UI details, blue accents, product screenshots and clear sections.
recipes.avoid: Inter, Helvetica or Arial as the display face by default; table cells under 16px; a label above every heading; arrow and middle-dot chrome on every link and meta line; library defaults (radius, colours, font) left as shipped; div-built product mock-ups; a hero that would read the same with a competitor's logo.

steps.title: Pick a neutral grotesque
steps.do: Pick a neutral grotesque that is not on the overused list (Inter, Roboto, Open Sans, Lato, Montserrat, Arial, Helvetica, Geist, Plus Jakarta Sans, Space Grotesk and others) unless it is the brand's own face. Candidates present in Google Fonts: Hanken Grotesk, Schibsted Grotesk, Albert Sans, Familjen Grotesk, Public Sans, Archivo, IBM Plex Sans. Write the choice and the reason in the direction file.
steps.how: Google Fonts metadata (fetched 2026-11-06) lists each of the seven families as sans serif; Hanken Grotesk, Albert Sans, Familjen Grotesk and Public Sans are variable in weight, Archivo and IBM Plex Sans in weight and width. Neutral Swiss character comes from even stroke, closed apertures and tight, regular spacing; judge it by setting your real headline in two or three candidates. If the brand owns a face, use it and record the exception.
steps.label: craft-consensus
steps.status_note: Availability was verified from metadata. The overused list comes from the guideline, whose sources were mostly read but whose detector is partly read. Which candidate feels most Swiss is our judgement; none was rendered.

steps.title: Twelve-column grid with fixed gutter
steps.do: Build the grid as 12 equal columns with a fixed gutter in a centered container no wider than 1200 to 1400px. Place items by column span at wide viewports and let every item take the full width (grid-column: 1 / -1) at narrow ones. Add overflow-wrap: anywhere to grid children so long strings cannot push the page sideways.
steps.how: Measured 2026-11-06 in Chrome 156 via Playwright (channel "chrome"): a 12-column grid (repeat(12, minmax(0, 1fr)), 1rem gutters, 75rem max) with a heading spanning 4 columns and text spanning 8 had scrollWidth 320 at a 320 px viewport and 1280 at 1280 px, with a long unbroken string inside. Without overflow-wrap: anywhere the same string pushed scrollWidth to 471 at 320 px. Place by source order; if you place items on explicit lines, keep the DOM in reading order. The guideline cites GOV.UK layout and USWDS spacing units for capping the page container at 1400px or less.
steps.label: craft-consensus

steps.title: Hierarchy by ratio and weight gap
steps.do: Make hierarchy visible with size and weight: pick a ratio of 1.25 to 1.333 between roles (body 1rem, h3 1.333rem, h2 1.777rem, h1 2.369rem at ratio 1.333) and a weight gap of at least 200 between headings and body (400 body, 700 headings). Define the scale as tokens.
steps.how: The ratios are computed (1.333 compounding gives 1, 1.333, 1.777, 2.369). The guideline needs one step of at least 1.25 between neighbours and a weight gap of at least 200 for 80% of headings. Swiss typography relies on a few sizes and weights with strict alignment rather than on colour or ornament. Limit article headings to three levels (Butterick).
steps.label: craft-consensus

code.text:
:root { --step-0: 1rem; --step-1: 1.333rem; --step-2: 1.777rem; --step-3: 2.369rem; }
body { font-weight: 400; } h1, h2, h3 { font-weight: 700; }

steps.status_note: The scale values are arithmetic and the thresholds come from the guideline (detector sources partly read). Whether 1.333 suits a given brand is a craft choice; the Swiss style does not require it.

steps.title: Density from layout, not tiny type
steps.do: Keep information density in the layout, not in tiny type: table cells, list items and form text stay at 1rem (16px) or above, and you get density from tight row padding and a 12-column grid. Use labels (captions, table headers, metadata) only where they add information, at 1rem unless they are true captions, at most ceil(sections / 3) labels above headings, and give capital labels 0.05 to 0.12em letter-spacing.
steps.how: The body-size rule counts table cells and form text as running text: only captions, footnotes and legal text may be smaller than 16px. Measured 2026-11-06 in Chrome 156 via Playwright (channel "chrome"): a pricing-style table at 1rem with 0.75rem cell padding stayed inside its scrolling region at 320 px with no page overflow; axe flagged the scroller without tabindex="0" and passed it with tabindex, role="region" and aria-labelledby on the caption. See the editorial recipe for the markup. Letter-spacing of 0.05em to 0.12em on capitals is Butterick's range.
steps.label: craft-consensus

steps.title: Plain labels, few arrows and dots
steps.do: Write plain link and button labels. No more than two links or buttons end in an arrow, no more than one meta string uses middle dots (separate dates, authors and tags with layout: a dl in a grid, or a flex gap), em dashes stay rare, and no icon-plus-heading-plus-sentence card row is the main section.
steps.how: These are the guideline thresholds. GOV.UK link guidance asks for descriptive link text: say what happens, not an arrow. The system-UI feel of a utilitarian page comes from real controls (native selects, tables, rules, monospace data) rather than from decorative glyphs.
steps.label: craft-consensus
steps.status_note: The numeric limits come from detector-based guidelines whose sources are partly read. Our-take on style: use them as review thresholds.

steps.title: Blue and grays that pass contrast
steps.do: Use blue as a text and button colour only where it passes: #1D4ED8 on white, with white text on a blue button. Mute secondary text no lighter than #4B5563 on a light grey surface. Draw structural rules at #767676 or darker. Give focus its own ring (#0B5FFF, 3px outline, 2px offset).
steps.how: Computed with the WCAG 2 formula: blue link on white 6.7:1; white on blue 6.7:1; body 14.67:1; muted 6.86:1 on #F3F4F6; a #6B7280 muted grey is only 4.83:1 on white, close to the line; rule #767676 4.54:1; focus ring 5.12:1 on white and 4.65:1 on surface. For a Swiss red, #E10600 on white reaches 4.96:1 while #C40500 reaches 6.23:1 and 5.56:1 on off-white, with white text on it at 6.23:1.
steps.label: craft-consensus

code.text: :focus-visible { outline: 3px solid var(--focus); outline-offset: 2px; }

steps.title: Prove the page is this company's
steps.do: Prove the page is this company's. Show the real product (a captured screen with alt text, real data, not a rectangle mock-up), build the first two viewports around one idea only this subject could carry, set your own radius, colour and type tokens before using any component library, then run the swap test: replace the logo with a competitor's and ask a reviewer who did not build it which site it is.
steps.how: This is the guideline's own manual check. To customise library defaults, change the radius, primary colour and font variables to your tokens and record them in the direction file; do not leave the library's init values in the shipped CSS. A corporate-clean page is allowed to be conventional in structure; the distinctiveness comes from the content, the imagery and the one idea.
steps.label: our-take
steps.status_note: Craft opinion. The checks come from guidelines labeled our-take or built on partly read sources; no experiment shows the swap test predicts anything.

recipes.generate_hint: Keep a visible 12-column grid and plain type; choose a display face that is not the default; table text at 16px; show the real product; set your own tokens; verify blue and grey contrast.

recipes.title: Luxury and opulent styles: gold, thin type and ornament that stay readable
recipes.summary: Keep the deep colours, the gold, the generous space and the ornament. Use a gold that passes on its ground, keep light type weights for large display lines, write in plain words, and make ornament decorative so it never carries the message.
recipes.keep: Near-black or burgundy grounds, ivory text, gold accents, serif display lines, ornament and dense detail, long quiet spacing, product-focused imagery.
recipes.avoid: Gold text on white; light or thin weights at body size; letterspaced lowercase paragraphs; ornament behind text; stock marketing verbs (elevate, curated, timeless tapestry); text set as an image; ten equal choices on the first screen.

palette.name: Ivory and gold on night, with a burgundy variant, computed

steps.title: Choose gold by its ground
steps.do: Choose gold by the ground it sits on. On near-black use #C9A24B for text and buttons (with night text on the button). On ivory use a deep gold such as #7A5A12 for text. Use #8F7433 or lighter for thin decorative lines only where 3:1 is enough.
steps.how: Computed with the WCAG 2 formula: gold #C9A24B on #0E0D0B 8.09:1; ivory text 16.79:1; muted #B5AE9F 8.8:1; a #8F7433 hairline 4.36:1. The same gold #C9A24B on white is only 2.39:1, so it fails for text and for icons that carry meaning. Deep gold #7A5A12 on ivory #FAF7F0 5.95:1. Burgundy #4A0F1F: ivory 13.16:1, gold #D9B866 7.97:1. A metallic gradient on text must be tested at its darkest and lightest stops.
steps.label: craft-consensus

steps.title: Light weights for large display only
steps.do: Reserve weight 300 or lighter for display lines of 24px and up; body and anything under 24px stays at 400 or heavier. Keep lowercase body text at letter-spacing normal. Track only uppercase labels (0.05 to 0.12em) and keep those to three words or fewer on one line.
steps.how: Thin high-contrast serifs (Cormorant Garamond, weights 300 to 700; Bodoni Moda, 400 to 900 with an optical-size axis; both in Google Fonts) look refined at display size and break up at body size, so raise the size or the weight instead of the tracking. Butterick: capitals take 5 to 12% letterspacing, lowercase does not ordinarily need it; capitals are for less than one line.
steps.label: craft-consensus
steps.status_note: Capitals and tracking advice was read from Butterick. The 300-weight and 24px threshold comes from the guideline (Apple HIG source partly read), and the font axes from metadata. The label is set at 1rem: the body-size rule counts a label paragraph as running text, so a smaller label size would fail. No face was rendered.

steps.title: Luxury copy as plain facts
steps.do: Write luxury copy as facts in ordinary words: where it is made, by whom, how long it takes, what is guaranteed. Remove stock marketing verbs and metaphors (unlock, elevate, curated, journey, tapestry, realm), use sentence case in headings, buttons and navigation, and name navigation items literally ("Watches", "Book a visit", not "Discover the journey").
steps.how: The buzzword list and plain-language rules come from the guidelines and GOV.UK, NN/g and COGA. A rough local score (our own approximate syllable script, illustrative only) gave grade 16 for "Elevate your journey with an unparalleled tapestry of timeless craftsmanship, where every moment is curated to transcend the ordinary." and grade 3 for "Each watch is made by hand in our Geneva workshop. One maker builds one watch, which takes about nine weeks. We service every watch for life." The plain version carries three checkable facts; the buzzword version carries none. Prestige can still come from restraint: short lines and specific numbers.
steps.label: craft-consensus
steps.status_note: Rules and sources were read; the readability scores came from an approximate script and the example brand is invented. Whether plain facts make a luxury brand feel more or less premium is our judgement.

steps.title: Ornament as decoration only
steps.do: Treat ornament as decoration: borders, flourishes, monograms and patterns are CSS backgrounds or SVG with alt="" (or aria-hidden="true"), never the only place a name, price or instruction appears. Put text on a solid panel, not on a patterned or photographic ground. Keep headings and prices as real text, and use an image of text only for a logo.
steps.how: NN/g: an image is decorative if users can complete all tasks and understand all information without it, and gets an empty alt. WCAG 1.4.5 allows images of text for logotypes or when the presentation is essential. For text over ornament or photography, the scrim math in the hero-and-photography recipe applies: a 60% black overlay keeps white text at 5.74:1 even over a pure white backdrop (measured in Chrome).
steps.label: craft-consensus

steps.title: One dominant thing per screen
steps.do: Give each screen one dominant thing and at most five main choices. An opulent page may be dense in detail, but make the one feature or call to action visibly larger than the others and move secondary links under a titled "more" link or into the footer. Keep prices, fees and conditions visible where the choice is made.
steps.how: COGA asks for about five or fewer main choices per screen and one visually dominant feature; the same document asks for costs to be stated at the start of a booking or purchase. Luxury practice often hides the price; that is a brand choice that conflicts with the guidance, so record the exception if you keep it.
steps.label: our-take
steps.status_note: The COGA guidance was read, but applying it to luxury is our judgement and trades some mystique for clarity.

recipes.generate_hint: Gold that passes on its ground, light weights only at display size, plain factual copy in sentence case, ornament as decoration, one dominant choice per screen.

recipes.title: Bento, catalog and gallery grids that reflow and read in order
recipes.summary: Keep the mosaic of mixed-size tiles, the product grid and the image wall. Start from a one-column grid that needs no media query to fit 320px, add spans only on wide screens, keep the HTML in reading order, make each card one list item with one link, and let one item lead.
recipes.keep: Tiles of different sizes, rounded cards, dense product or image grids, a dominant lead tile.
recipes.avoid: Spans that overflow at 320px; grid-auto-flow: dense or order used to move content out of source order; whole-card wrapper links with several tab stops; rows of identical icon cards; cards nested inside cards; ten equal choices on the first screen; images without reserved space.

steps.title: Auto-fit grid, spans in media query
steps.do: Base the grid on repeat(auto-fit, minmax(min(100%, 15rem), 1fr)) so every tile fits a 320px viewport with no media query. Add column and row spans only inside a min-width media query, set min-inline-size: 0 and overflow-wrap: anywhere on tiles, and wrap the grid in a centered container no wider than 1200 to 1400px.
steps.how: Measured 2026-11-06 in Chrome 156 via Playwright (channel "chrome"): a 6-tile bento (one 2x2 lead, one 2-wide tile, four singles) in a 75rem container had scrollWidth 320 with one 288px column at a 320 px viewport, and four 288px columns with the lead spanning 592px at 1280 px. WCAG 1.4.10 requires content to work at 320 CSS px without two-dimensional scrolling. Switch to spans at 50em because that is where four tracks fit, not at a device width.
steps.label: craft-consensus

steps.title: HTML in reading order
steps.do: Write the HTML in the order you want read and tabbed, most important tile first. Do not use order or grid-auto-flow: dense to rearrange content that has a meaning order, and check with a script that visual order equals DOM order.
steps.how: Measured 2026-11-06 in Chrome 156 via Playwright (channel "chrome"): three tiles (two spanning 2 columns, one spanning 1) in a 3-column grid had DOM order one, two, three and the same visual order by default. With grid-auto-flow: dense the third tile moved up beside the first, so the visual order became one, three, two while keyboard focus still went one, two, three. MDN: order and grid placement change visual order only, not the order assistive technology or tab navigation use, and style sheets that use them for logical reordering are non-conforming. In the 6-tile bento above (no dense) tab order equalled visual order at 320 and 1280.
steps.label: craft-consensus

steps.title: Card markup with stretched link
steps.do: Mark each tile as li > heading > a, make the heading link the only tab stop, and extend the click area with a stretched a::after. Draw the focus ring on that ::after so it surrounds the whole card. Decorative images get alt=""; a "read more" cue is non-interactive text.
steps.how: Measured 2026-11-06 in Chrome 156 via Playwright (channel "chrome"): each of six tiles held exactly one focusable element; Tab visited them in DOM order; axe-core 4.14 reported no violations at 320 and 1280 px. In a separate one-card page, the computed style on the focused link's ::after was outline: solid 3px rgb(11, 95, 255), a ring of 5.12:1 against white (5.12:1 computed). The ::after covers the whole tile, so the target is well above 24 by 24 px. Link text carries the purpose (the heading), as WCAG 2.4.4 asks.
steps.label: craft-consensus

steps.title: Lead tile takes the most space
steps.do: Let the most important tile take the most space (2x2 or full width) and show it as a real example, not an icon. Size the other tiles to their content, not to fill a pattern. Group content inside a tile with space, rules and type, never with a second bordered card inside the first. Do not use emoji as tile icons.
steps.how: These follow the guideline checks: no section made mainly of three or more same-size icon-heading-sentence cards; no bordered or shaded container inside another; section order and block count driven by the buyer's questions. The bento above uses a 2x2 lead and a 2-wide tile so the widths differ.
steps.label: craft-consensus
steps.status_note: The thresholds come from detector-style guidelines whose sources were partly read, and the our-take section-order rule; this is craft advice, not tested against user outcomes.

steps.title: One lead, about five choices
steps.do: Show one dominant item and at most about five equal choices in each viewport-height section. For a catalog or gallery with many items, put the first row or two on screen, then use filters, a paged list or a real "show more" button; keep price, fees and key conditions on each product card. Reserve each image's space with width and height or aspect-ratio and crop with object-fit: cover and object-position, not by stretching.
steps.how: COGA: about five or fewer main choices per screen, one visually dominant feature, costs shown at the start. A shop grid necessarily lists many products, so the guidance is applied as hierarchy (one lead, filters, paging) rather than as a hard cap. The image-space and CLS measurement is in the hero-and-photography recipe: without width and height an image loading late gave CLS 0.0293 in Chrome and with them 0. Product images that show the product need alt text that names it; purely decorative tiles use alt="" (NN/g).
steps.label: craft-consensus
steps.status_note: The five-choice limit is COGA guidance, not a studied threshold, and a shop grid cannot meet it literally; the hierarchy approach is our judgement.

recipes.generate_hint: Use auto-fit minmax(min(100%, 15rem), 1fr) with spans only on wide screens, keep source order equal to reading order, li > heading > one link with a stretched ::after, and let one tile lead.

recipes.title: Photography-led and centered heroes with readable text and fast images
recipes.summary: Keep the full-bleed photograph and the big centered headline. Put a measured scrim behind text, reserve image space and never lazy-load the hero image, write real alt text, centre only short lines, and build the first screen around something only this subject has.
recipes.keep: Large photographs, a centered headline and subline, a strong first screen, cropped imagery with a clear subject.
recipes.avoid: White text straight on a photo; a hero image that loads late and shifts the page; the hero image as a CSS background or lazy-loaded; alt text that describes nothing; centered paragraphs of three lines or more; the stock centered badge, headline, two buttons and logo row; a headline a competitor could publish unchanged.

palette.name: Scrim math for text over the brightest photo, computed

contrast.pair: white text on 60% black scrim over pure white
white text on 55% black scrim over pure white
large white text (24px+) on 42% scrim over pure white
white text on 50% black scrim over bright yellow #FFD400

steps.title: Scrim between photo and text
steps.do: Put a scrim between the photo and any text: a 60% black overlay (or a gradient that stays at or above 55% under the text lines) keeps white text at 4.5:1 or better over even a pure white photo. Test the brightest area at 375, 768 and 1440px, not the average.
steps.how: Computed: the minimum black overlay alpha for white text at 4.5:1 over pure white is 0.54 (0.42 for 24px-and-larger text at 3:1). A 0.6 overlay gives 5.74:1, 0.55 gives 4.74:1, and over bright yellow #FFD400 a 0.5 overlay gives 5.27:1. Measured 2026-11-06 in Chrome 156 via Playwright (channel "chrome"): a 20rem hero with a pure-white image and a 0.6 gradient overlay rendered #666666 under the heading (pixel sampled from a screenshot), a ratio of 5.74:1 with white text. Real photos have bright spots, so check the lightest area behind each line.
steps.label: standard

steps.title: Hero img with alt and priority
steps.do: Put the hero image in the HTML as an img with width and height, fetchpriority="high" and no loading="lazy". Write alt text for what the image adds in context (under about 150 characters, key words first), alt="" if it is decoration, and describe the destination for linked images.
steps.how: Measured 2026-11-06 in Chrome 156 via Playwright (channel "chrome"): a test page whose below-the-fold figure loaded 800 ms late measured CLS 0.0293 without width and height attributes and 0.0000 with them. web.dev: never lazy-load the LCP image, make it discoverable in the initial HTML (not a CSS background or script-injected), and fetchpriority="high" on one or two images at most. NN/g: decorative images get alt=""; informative images say what they contribute; keep alt under roughly 150 characters with the important words first.
steps.label: craft-consensus

steps.title: Crop to the subject, never stretch
steps.do: Fill the frame with object-fit: cover and set object-position to the subject; at small widths switch to a portrait crop with picture and media, instead of letting the subject fall outside the frame. Never stretch: the rendered ratio must match the file unless object-fit crops it.
steps.how: The picture element selects a different crop per media condition (web.dev Learn Responsive Design, The picture element and Responsive images). object-fit and aspect-ratio are Baseline features documented on MDN; pair aspect-ratio or width/height with the crop so the box is reserved before load.
steps.label: craft-consensus

code.text: .hero img { inline-size: 100%; block-size: 100%; object-fit: cover; object-position: 60% 40%; }

steps.status_note: The crop techniques are documented, but the MDN object-fit and aspect-ratio pages were only partly read and no crop was rendered or measured here.

steps.title: Center only headline and short subline
steps.do: Center only the headline and a subline that wraps to two lines or fewer. Below 48em start-align the subline, above it cap it near 56ch so it stays at two lines. Balance the headline with text-wrap: balance and keep it at 6rem or below.
steps.how: Measured 2026-11-06 in Chrome 156 via Playwright (channel "chrome"): a 98-character subline with a 34ch cap, centered at 768 px and wider, wrapped to 3 lines (fails the "no centered paragraph of 3 lines or more" check); with a 56ch cap above 48em it wrapped to 2 lines at 768 and 1280 px, and below 48em it was start-aligned (3 lines at 320 and 390 px). The guideline's sources (Butterick on justified text and hyphenation, WCAG 1.4.8 visual presentation) favour start-aligned body text.
steps.label: craft-consensus
steps.status_note: The line counts were measured for one sample sentence and fonts; recheck with your copy. Source support for avoiding centered paragraphs is general (start-aligned text), not a numeric line limit; the 3-line cut-off is the guideline's.

steps.title: Show something real in first viewport
steps.do: Make the first viewport show something real from the subject (the product screen, the work, the place, the object) and keep at most two of the five stock signals: centered headline, badge or eyebrow above it, exactly two buttons, a logo row in the next section, a three-card feature row after that. A centered photographic hero usually keeps the first and drops the badge.
steps.how: These are the guideline's checks. No "New" or "Live" pill unless it is bound to a real state or release. Name the lead element of the hero in the written direction file before building so it is a decision, not a leftover.
steps.label: craft-consensus
steps.status_note: The five-signal count comes from detector-style guidelines with partly read sources; NN/g homepage principles (read) support showing real content on the first screen, not the exact threshold.

steps.title: Headline that passes the swap test
steps.do: Write the H1 and subline so they name the outcome, the offer or the audience, then run the swap test: paste a direct competitor's name in and see whether it is still true. If so, rewrite with a noun, number or place only this product can claim. Avoid the template "The [modern] [category] for [teams]".
steps.how: Weak (illustrative): "The modern platform for teams that move fast." Stronger (illustrative): "Pay 40 suppliers in one afternoon", which states an outcome and a number. NN/g: headings are pick-up lines, so lead with the specific value in the first words. The page title should name the page's purpose too, so it is not left as the brand name alone.
steps.label: craft-consensus
steps.status_note: The swap test is a manual check with a craft rationale; the example headlines are invented for illustration, and no experiment is cited that these convert better.

recipes.generate_hint: Photo hero with a 60% scrim behind text, hero img in HTML with width, height and fetchpriority high, center only a two-line subline, and a first screen built around a real subject element and a headline a competitor could not copy.

recipes.title: SaaS stacks, single-column pages, social proof, pricing tables and event sites
recipes.summary: Keep the classic landing sequence, the single centered column, the logo and testimonial proof, the featured pricing plan and the event countdown. Order sections by the buyer's questions, vary their shape, show only proof you can name, build pricing as a real table with units, and caption any live stream.
recipes.keep: Hero, proof, features, pricing and final call to action in a familiar order; one centered reading column; logos, quotes and numbers; a highlighted plan; event dates, schedule and registration.
recipes.avoid: The stock sequence with no reason; eight sections of identical padding and layout; invented logos, numbers and quotes; a logo marquee that cannot be paused; a featured plan shown by colour alone; plan names with no stated limits; hidden fees; a live stream without live captions; an auto-updating countdown that is announced every second.

steps.title: Order sections by buyer questions
steps.do: Write the page brief as a list of the questions this buyer asks and the section that answers each, then order the stack by it. Keep the hero, proof, features, pricing and call to action only if each answers a question; vary section shapes (full-bleed, split, list, quote, table) so no layout family runs more than two sections in a row and an eight-section page uses at least four families. Vary the vertical padding.
steps.how: These are the guideline checks. For the hero, see the hero-and-photography recipe. For tile grids, see bento-and-card-grids. Content strategy sources (Halvorson, NN/g homepage principles) support organizing by user goals rather than by template.
steps.label: craft-consensus
steps.status_note: The thresholds are from detector-style guidelines; sources were partly read or are practitioner posts. This is craft advice with no study behind the numbers.

steps.title: Named grid lines in one column
steps.do: For a single-column page, build the column with named grid lines so text sits at 55ch, figures break out to a wider track and one band runs full width. That varies the rhythm without leaving the one-column reading order.
steps.how: Measured 2026-11-06 in Chrome 156 via Playwright (channel "chrome"): with this grid, paragraphs were 288 px wide at 320 px (no overflow, scrollWidth 320) and 729 px (66ch at 18px serif) at 768, 1280 and 1920 px, and the wide figure was 969 px at 1280 and 1920, with no horizontal scroll at 320, 768, 1280 or 1920 px. Zero the default figure margin or the figure shrinks (it was 208 px at 320 until margin: 0).
steps.label: craft-consensus

steps.title: Show only proof you can name
steps.do: Show only proof you can name. Every statistic, quote, logo, award and superlative has a source on the page (customer name, role, date, report link) or is removed. List missing proof as a content gap for the owner instead of inventing it. Run a placeholder check before shipping. Show logos as img with alt text of the company name, no auto-scrolling marquee, in grey that keeps 3:1 against the ground.
steps.how: Computed: logo grey #767676 on white is 4.54:1 (a lighter #B0B0B0 is 2.16:1, which fails 3:1 for a graphic that identifies a customer). Measured 2026-11-06 in Chrome 156 via Playwright (channel "chrome"): the placeholder pattern below matched "Acme Corp saved us 40%", "John Doe, CEO" and "Lorem ipsum dolor" and did not match "Mara Ilves, head of ops at Tallinn Bakery". WCAG 2.2.2 requires auto-moving content that runs longer than five seconds to be pausable, so prefer a static logo row. Prefer a named figure with a date ("Median ticket reply time, Q3 2026") over an unlabeled big number.
steps.label: our-take

code.text:
const placeholder = /\b(lorem ipsum|john doe|jane (doe|smith)|acme|globex|initech|company name|your (company|name) here)\b/i;
[...document.querySelectorAll("main *")].filter(e => placeholder.test(e.textContent) && !e.children.length);

steps.status_note: Contrast and the regex behavior were computed and tested. The rule "show only proof with a named source" is our-take; whether named proof converts better than anonymous proof was not tested.

steps.title: Testimonials as figure and blockquote
steps.do: Mark each testimonial as a figure with a blockquote and a figcaption holding the name, role, company and date, with a cite link to the source when one exists. Use static quotes or a plain list, not an autoplaying carousel. Quote text keeps 4.5:1 on its surface.
steps.how: figure and blockquote carry the quote and its attribution in the markup (WCAG 1.3.1). NN/g found carousels are often skipped, and the APG carousel pattern requires a control to stop and start any automatic rotation. Computed: near-black text on #F3F4F6 16.34:1, caption #4B5563 6.86:1.
steps.label: craft-consensus
steps.status_note: Markup follows WCAG and HTML semantics; the example quote and person are invented placeholders and must be replaced by supplied proof. Screen reader output was not tested.

steps.title: Pricing as a real table
steps.do: Build the comparison as a real table: caption (stating currency, billing period and tax), thead with th scope="col", every row label a th scope="row", limits with units ("Up to 15 users", "100 GB"), all recurring costs in the table. Mark the featured plan with text ("Most popular"), not colour alone, and keep white text on its header at 4.5:1. On narrow screens let the table scroll inside a focusable labelled region.
steps.how: Measured 2026-11-06 in Chrome 156 via Playwright (channel "chrome"): a 3-plan table in a 288 px wrapper (min table width 36rem) had page scrollWidth 320 (no page-level overflow) and its wrapper scrolled to 576 px; axe-core 4.14 flagged the wrapper as scrollable-region-focusable (serious) until it had tabindex="0", role="region" and aria-labelledby="cap", then reported no violations. White on #1D4ED8 is 6.7:1; the "Most popular" badge, ink on #FDE68A, is 14.44:1. NN/g: state the differences between options explicitly, with units, and show all costs together.
steps.label: craft-consensus

code.text:
Plans compared. Prices are per workspace per month, billed monthly, in US dollars, excluding tax.
FeatureStarter Team Most popularBusiness
UsersUp to 3 usersUp to 15 usersUp to 100 users

steps.title: Stable-name billing toggle
steps.do: If a monthly or yearly switch changes the prices, make it one native toggle button named "Billed yearly" whose name never changes and whose state is aria-pressed (or two radios in a fieldset with a legend). After the switch, update the prices in the table and announce the change through a status region that already exists in the DOM; show the yearly total beside the monthly figure.
steps.how: Measured 2026-11-06 in Chrome 156 via Playwright (channel "chrome"): a toggle button named "Dark mode" kept the same accessible name before and after, exposed "pressed" through aria-pressed, and toggled with both Space and Enter; a role="status" region filled after an action was read back as text (see the interaction recipe). The same markup applies to a billing switch. Radios in a fieldset also satisfy the guideline.
steps.label: craft-consensus
steps.status_note: The control behavior was tested on a dark-mode toggle, not on a live billing switch; screen reader announcements were not tested. The advice to show the yearly total with the monthly figure comes from the costs-up-front guidance (COGA).

steps.title: Live captions for event streams
steps.do: If the event page embeds a live stream or webinar, use a player and a captioning service that supply live captions of speech, speaker identification and significant non-speech sounds, and say on the page how to turn them on. If there is no live audio, mark the requirement not applicable. Publish recordings with captions and a transcript afterwards. Write dates as time elements with a time zone; the countdown is a visual extra, never the only place the start time appears, and it is not announced every second.
steps.how: WCAG 1.2.4 (Level AA) requires captions for live audio in synchronized media. It is a blocker for event sites that stream. Auto-updating content that starts automatically and lasts more than five seconds must be pausable (2.2.2); a second-by-second countdown should be visually fine but hidden from assistive technology (aria-hidden on the ticking digits) with the start date and time in plain text beside it. Show "Live" only while a stream is actually live. Event colours: white on #0F172A is 17.85:1, yellow #FACC15 on it 11.65:1, with night text on a yellow button 11.65:1.
steps.label: standard

code.text:
Starts 12 November 2026, 09:00 CET

3 days 4 hours

steps.status_note: The requirements were read from the WCAG Understanding pages. We did not test a live captioning provider or player, so no vendor is recommended; the countdown advice and the date markup are our practical guidance and were not screen-reader tested.

recipes.generate_hint: Order sections by buyer questions, vary section shapes, use only named proof, build pricing as a captioned table with units and a text-marked featured plan, and give any live stream live captions.

recipes.title: Dark, light and mixed-theme pages with their own checked palettes
recipes.summary: Keep a dark page, a light page or alternating bands. Declare color-scheme, define each theme as its own token set with contrast checked, treat bands as local themes, and make any theme switch a labelled toggle that remembers its state. For neon and glow see dark-neon-contrast; for mode switches that rename things see big-type-and-modes.
recipes.keep: A dominant dark or light ground, or light and dark sections alternating; a strong accent colour; imagery that suits the ground.
recipes.avoid: Making the dark theme by inverting the light one; reusing the light accent on a dark ground; a flash of the wrong theme at load; native controls and scrollbars in the wrong scheme; a dark band whose links use light-page tokens; a theme switch that renames itself.

palette.name: Light and dark token sets, each computed

contrast.pair: dark: dark text on accent button

steps.title: Declare schemes with light-dark()
steps.do: Declare the schemes the page supports in a meta tag placed before any CSS and in CSS on :root, define colours once as role tokens with light-dark(), and let prefers-color-scheme choose the default. A deliberately single-theme page may declare color-scheme: only light or only dark, knowing that this also opts the page out of the browser's automatic dark rendering.
steps.how: Measured 2026-11-06 in Chrome 156 via Playwright (channel "chrome"): with <meta name="color-scheme" content="light dark"> and :root { color-scheme: light dark } plus light-dark() tokens, emulating colorScheme light gave a white background and #16181D text, and dark gave rgb(18, 20, 26) and rgb(232, 234, 240); getComputedStyle(html).colorScheme was "light dark" in both; a native text input drew a dark background (rgb(59, 59, 59)) in the dark scheme. MDN: color-scheme changes canvas, scrollbars and form controls and is Baseline widely available since January 2022; the meta tag before CSS helps avoid a flash at load; it does not restyle your own content, so use prefers-color-scheme or light-dark() for that.
steps.label: craft-consensus

code.text:
<meta name="color-scheme" content="light dark">
<style>
 :root { color-scheme: light dark;
   --bg: light-dark(#FFFFFF, #12141A); --text: light-dark(#16181D, #E8EAF0);
   --accent: light-dark(#1F4FD8, #8FB0FF); --focus: light-dark(#0B5FFF, #7FB3FF); }
 body { background: var(--bg); color: var(--text); }
</style>

steps.title: Separate dark tokens, check both themes
steps.do: Author the dark palette as its own set of tokens and check every pair in both themes: 4.5:1 for text, 3:1 for large text, borders, icons and focus rings. Use lighter, less saturated accents on dark grounds, and dark text on a light accent button.
steps.how: Computed with the WCAG 2 formula (table above): light text 17.75:1, dark text 15.3:1; light accent link 6.62:1 but reusing that same #1F4FD8 on the dark ground gives only 2.77:1, which fails, so the dark accent is the lighter #8FB0FF (8.61:1) with #0B1020 text on a button of that colour (8.85:1). Borders are 3.91:1 light and 3.87:1 dark; focus rings 4.66:1 on the light surface and 7.76:1 on the dark one. Prefer off-black (#12141A) to pure black for large areas; pure white on pure black is 21:1 but glaring. Axe's color-contrast rule reported no violations in either scheme on the test page.
steps.label: craft-consensus

steps.title: Dim photos, dark logo variants
steps.do: Do not invert or filter the whole page to get a dark theme. Dim bright photographs a little in dark mode, supply dark variants of logos and diagrams with transparent backgrounds through picture and a prefers-color-scheme media query, and keep photographs' colours.
steps.how: Measured 2026-11-06 in Chrome 156 via Playwright (channel "chrome"): img { filter: brightness(.85) } inside @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) computed to "brightness(0.85)" in dark and "none" in light. The 0.85 value is our choice. The guideline, built on Apple HIG dark mode and web.dev theming, asks for a palette authored for dark, not an inverted or filtered light one.
steps.label: craft-consensus

code.text: @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) { img:not([data-keep]) { filter: brightness(0.85); } }

steps.status_note: The media-query behavior was measured; the 0.85 strength is our judgement, not from a source, and no image was assessed visually.

steps.title: Each band as a local theme
steps.do: For alternating light and dark sections, make each band its own local theme: set color-scheme on the band and override the role tokens (background, text, accent, focus) with that theme's checked values. Components inside use only tokens, so a link or input in a dark band is correct without extra CSS. Give each band a heading so the bands are real sections.
steps.how: Measured 2026-11-06 in Chrome 156 via Playwright (channel "chrome"): a .band with color-scheme: dark and the dark token values, inside a light page, gave a link colour rgb(143, 176, 255) in both emulated schemes and a native input with the dark control background (rgb(59, 59, 59)) even when the page itself was light; axe color-contrast reported no violations in either page scheme. The dark accent on the dark ground is 8.61:1; the light accent #1F4FD8 would be 2.77:1 there. Keep the order, labels and positions of navigation and controls the same in every band.
steps.label: craft-consensus

code.text:
.band-dark { color-scheme: dark; --bg: #12141A; --text: #E8EAF0; --muted: #A3AABB;
  --accent: #8FB0FF; --focus: #7FB3FF; background: var(--bg); color: var(--text); }

steps.title: Stable-name theme switch
steps.do: If you offer a theme control, make it a button with aria-pressed named after the setting ("Dark mode") that never changes its name, place it in the header or footer in the same spot on every page, start from the system preference, and remember the choice. Set the stored theme on the html element from a small inline script in the head before first paint so there is no flash. Style the on state with more than colour.
steps.how: Measured 2026-11-06 in Chrome 156 via Playwright (channel "chrome"): a button named "Dark mode" with aria-pressed kept the same accessible name before and after toggling, exposed [pressed] after Space, and returned to unpressed after Enter (see the interaction recipe). The guideline, built on Inclusive Components' theme switcher, asks for a labelled toggle whose state persists. Store the choice in localStorage inside try/catch, since storage can be blocked.
steps.label: craft-consensus

code.text:
<script>
 try { const t = localStorage.getItem("theme"); if (t) document.documentElement.dataset.theme = t; } catch (e) {}
</script>
<button type="button" aria-pressed="false" id="theme">Dark mode</button>

steps.title: Honor contrast and forced colors
steps.do: Respect the user's contrast preferences in either theme: under prefers-contrast: more strengthen borders and muted text, and make focus, borders and state survive forced-colors: active by using real borders and outlines, not shadows or background tints alone.
steps.how: Measured 2026-11-06 in Chrome 156 via Playwright (channel "chrome"): with contrast: "more" emulated, a border defined as var(--line) in a prefers-contrast: more block changed from #7A8190 to rgb(58, 65, 80). In forced-colors mode outline and border colours stay visible but box-shadow is removed (MDN), so draw focus rings with outline.
steps.label: craft-consensus

code.text: @media (prefers-contrast: more) { :root { --line: #3A4150; --muted: #2B3040; } }

steps.status_note: The prefers-contrast switch was tested in Chrome emulation; the forced-colors facts were read on MDN but forced-colors rendering was not emulated here.

recipes.generate_hint: Meta and CSS color-scheme, light-dark() role tokens, a separately checked dark palette, bands as local themes with their own tokens, and a labelled "Dark mode" toggle that persists.

recipes.title: Hover effects, micro-interactions and page transitions that work without a mouse
recipes.summary: Keep the hover reactions, the small animated feedback and the animated route changes. Make hover only an enhancement with a keyboard and touch equivalent, keep feedback under 200ms and out of the way of input, mirror every toast on the page, and run transitions only for users who allow motion, with focus, title and status handled.
recipes.keep: Hover lifts and reveals, animated toggles and buttons, success feedback, smooth cross-fades and shared-element route changes.
recipes.avoid: Content that exists only on hover; tooltips that vanish when the pointer moves onto them or cannot be dismissed; tabs or menus that open only on hover; feedback over 200ms or that blocks the next click; overshoot easing; a toast as the only record of an action; toggles that rename themselves; page transitions that drop focus, keep the old title, ignore reduced motion or run for seconds.

steps.title: Hover reveals as enhancement only
steps.do: Make every hover reveal an enhancement. Show the content by default, and only inside @media (hover: hover) hide it until the card is hovered or contains focus (:hover and :focus-within together). On touch devices and keyboards the content is simply there.
steps.how: Measured 2026-11-06 in Chrome 156 via Playwright (channel "chrome"): a card with an extra line hidden only inside @media (hover: hover) had opacity 0 at rest on a desktop context, 1 after hover (and 0 again after leaving), and 1 after Tab moved focus to the link; in a touch context (hasTouch and isMobile, where (hover: hover) was false) the line was visible at rest with no hover. MDN: the hover media feature reports whether the primary input can hover conveniently; devices that only emulate hover on long tap report none, so hover must not be the only way to reach important content; hybrid devices report only the primary input, so keyboard and focus parity is still needed.
steps.label: craft-consensus

steps.title: Accessible tooltips when needed
steps.do: Prefer a visible text label to a tooltip. If you need a tooltip, show it on hover and keyboard focus, link it with aria-describedby, keep it text only, let Escape dismiss it without moving focus, and keep it visible while the pointer is over the bubble. For help that must work on touch, use a click-activated toggletip: a real button plus an empty role="status" region that you fill on click.
steps.how: Measured 2026-11-06 in Chrome 156 via Playwright (channel "chrome"): the tooltip appeared when the button received focus, disappeared on Escape while focus stayed on the button, reappeared on the next hover, and stayed visible while the pointer moved onto the bubble. The toggletip button had no aria-describedby, and after Enter the status region held "Billed monthly in US dollars, excluding tax."; Escape cleared it. WCAG 1.4.13 requires such content to be dismissible, hoverable and persistent; native title tooltips are excluded because the browser controls them.
steps.label: craft-consensus

code.text: Saves a draft

steps.title: Hover-driven tabs follow the tabs pattern
steps.do: When a hover effect also drives tabs or a menu, build it as the tabs pattern: only the selected tab is in the Tab order, arrow keys move between tabs, Home and End jump to the ends, and a panel that starts with non-focusable content has tabindex="0". Hover may preview a tab, but selection and content come from click and keys.
steps.how: Measured 2026-11-06 in Chrome 156 via Playwright (channel "chrome"): a three-tab list with role=tablist, aria-selected, aria-controls and roving tabindex: Tab entered on the selected tab (tabindexes 0, -1, -1), ArrowRight moved to the next, End went to the last, ArrowRight wrapped to the first, Home returned to the first, and Tab from the tablist landed on the panel (tabindex 0). Do not use tabs for site navigation (use links).
steps.label: craft-consensus

steps.title: Feedback timing of 100 to 400 ms
steps.do: Time interface feedback: hover, press and toggle transitions 100 to 200ms (150ms is a good default), other functional transitions at most 400ms and never over 500ms. Use ease-out for things entering and ease-in for things leaving, no overshoot curves, and keep the control usable during the animation. Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, drop transforms and movement and keep a plain colour or opacity change.
steps.how: Measured 2026-11-06 in Chrome 156 via Playwright (channel "chrome"): transitions computed to 0.1s (press scale) and 0.15s (colour) on buttons and 0.2s on a checkmark, with cubic-bezier(0.2, 0.8, 0.2, 1) (no y value outside 0 to 1); three rapid clicks on a button during its transition were all counted (the count rose by 3), so input was not blocked; with reducedMotion: "reduce" emulated, the card reveal transition computed to 0s. NN/g and Apple HIG motion guidance support short UI transitions; prefers-reduced-motion is Baseline widely available since January 2020 and MDN advises replacing large movement with gentler effects such as fades rather than removing the information.
steps.label: craft-consensus

steps.title: Animated toggles from ARIA state
