steps.do: Build animated toggles from a native button with aria-pressed (or a checkbox, or role="switch" with aria-checked) and a fixed name such as "Dark mode". Drive the visual state from the ARIA attribute in CSS so look and state cannot diverge, show state with more than colour (a check, a knob position or text), and keep Space and Enter working.
steps.how: Measured 2026-11-06 in Chrome 156 via Playwright (channel "chrome"): the button's accessible name was "Dark mode" before and after, with [pressed] added by aria-pressed="true" after Space and removed after Enter; the checkmark animated through a stroke-dashoffset transition selected by button[aria-pressed=true]; axe-core found no violations. Do not change the label as well as aria-pressed (APG button pattern).
steps.label: craft-consensus

code.text:
button[aria-pressed="true"] { background: #14171A; color: #fff; }
button[aria-pressed="true"] .check { stroke-dashoffset: 0; }   /* visible check, not only colour */

steps.title: Immediate feedback with status region
steps.do: After every action show immediate visible feedback and mirror any toast in persistent page state. Put an empty role="status" region in the page at load and write the message into it, update an on-page count or list (the cart total, the saved list), and let a toast be a convenience, not the only record. Do not use a toast for information needed to finish a task.
steps.how: Measured 2026-11-06 in Chrome 156 via Playwright (channel "chrome"): clicking "Add to cart" updated the visible count (0 to 1, then 4 after three rapid clicks) and filled the status region with "Added to cart. 1 items in cart." (fix the plural in real copy). The live region existed before the message, which is what lets assistive technology announce it without moving focus (WCAG 4.1.3). Keep at most one signature motion moment and let other animations answer an action.
steps.label: craft-consensus

code.text: Cart: 0 items

steps.title: Cross-document view transitions
steps.do: For multi-page sites, opt in to cross-document view transitions in CSS on both pages, inside a prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference block, and keep the animation short (about 250ms). Treat it as progressive enhancement: Firefox does not run it and the pages must work without it. Both pages must be same-origin.
steps.how: Measured 2026-11-06 in Chrome 156 via Playwright (channel "chrome") (Chrome 156): with @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference) { @view-transition { navigation: auto } } on two local pages, a link click produced a ViewTransition on the destination (pagereveal event had viewTransition set); with reducedMotion: "reduce" emulated it did not. After the navigation focus was on the body, as with any normal navigation, and each page keeps its own title. Chrome documents cross-document view transitions from Chrome and Edge 126 and Safari 18.2, not Firefox, requires same-origin navigations and both pages to opt in, and skips the transition if the navigation takes over four seconds. MDN lists @view-transition as Limited availability (not Baseline), so feature-detect or accept non-support.
steps.label: craft-consensus

steps.title: Guarded single-page view transitions
steps.do: For a single-page route change, wrap the DOM swap in document.startViewTransition only when the user allows motion and the API exists. After the swap, update document.title, move focus to the new page heading (an h1 with tabindex="-1"), push history, and write a short message into a pre-existing role="status" region. Keep the transition at 300ms or less: input is blocked while it runs.
steps.how: Measured 2026-11-06 in Chrome 156 via Playwright (channel "chrome"): in an SPA test, after the swap document.activeElement was BODY (the clicked link had been removed), and calling h1.focus() on a tabindex="-1" heading put focus on it; title read "About"; the status region held "Navigated to About"; with reducedMotion: "reduce" no transition was started and the same focus handling still worked. With a deliberately long 1500ms transition, a click on another button 300 ms after the start was held back about 1.4 s until the transition ended (Playwright waited for actionability), and a raw mouse click during it did nothing, so long transitions make the page unresponsive. MDN notes that keeping old and new content around can cause loss of reading position, focus confusion and odd live-region behaviour, and lists stopping accidental interaction with old content among the problems hand-written transitions must solve.
steps.label: craft-consensus
steps.status_note: Focus, title, status text and the input-blocking behavior were measured in Chrome 156; MDN supports the focus and live-region risks. Moving focus to the h1 is common practice rather than a rule from a source we read, and we did not test with a screen reader, Safari or Firefox.

recipes.generate_hint: Hover effects only as enhancements inside (hover: hover) with focus and touch parity; 100 to 200ms ease-out feedback; toggles as aria-pressed buttons with fixed names; toasts mirrored on the page; view transitions only for no-preference motion, with focus, title and status handled.

recipes.title: Brutalist, neo-brutalist and edgy styles that stay usable
recipes.summary: Keep the thick outlines, hard offset shadows, flat saturated blocks, raw tables and a sharp voice. Make the roughness come from borders, type weight and layout, not from shouting capitals, stretched images, bare div widgets or a shadow that is the only boundary.
recipes.keep: Black outlines, hard offset shadows, flat saturated fills, default-looking underlined links, raw tables and tabs, heavy grotesque or monospace type, a blunt voice.
recipes.avoid: Headings, paragraphs and buttons in all capitals; stretched or squashed images; tabs, accordions and tables built from bare divs; a thick coloured stripe on one side of a rounded card; error messages that mock the user; shadows or fills as the only sign of a boundary or a state.

contrast.pair: edgy: near-black text on acid button

steps.title: Flat fills with near-black ink
steps.do: Set flat saturated fills with near-black ink on top and check every pair. Ink #111111 on paper is 18.88:1, on yellow #FFD600 13.37:1, pink #FF90E8 9.36:1, blue #A3C4FF 10.7:1, green #B8F2A0 14.61:1. Links #1D2BFF are 7.39:1 on paper and 5.23:1 on yellow. Never put white text on these fills.
steps.how: Choose the fill for its saturation, then set the text to ink or paper, whichever passes, and recompute. The 3px ink border is 18.88:1 against paper, far above the 3:1 UI minimum, which is why thick outlines solve the boundary problem that thin grey outlines create. Edgy dark variant: white on #0A0A0A is 19.8:1, acid #C6FF00 is 16.69:1 (use as large text, icons or a button fill with #0A0A0A text at 16.69:1), and error red #FF3B30 is 5.58:1 for text. Harsh contrast is the look here, so none of it needs lowering. Rendered and measured in a Chrome demo: the computed colours match the claimed pairs.
steps.label: standard

steps.title: Shout with weight, not uppercase
steps.do: Get the shouting look from weight, size and tight tracking on sentence-case text, and keep uppercase for labels of three words or fewer. Never uppercase a heading of more than three words, a paragraph or a button label. Every uppercase label gets letter-spacing of 0.05em to 0.12em. Do not put a tracked uppercase label directly above the hero heading (distinct-eyebrow-restraint): place it after the heading or leave it out. Step the h1 in rem (2.5rem, 3.5rem from min-width: 40rem, 5rem from 64rem) instead of clamp() with vw, and put overflow-wrap: anywhere on headings, paragraphs, chips and buttons: heavy words overflowed the page by 67 px at 320 px with 200% text and text spacing until we did.
steps.how: Practical Typography: caps work for text shorter than a line and need letter-spacing of about 5 to 12 percent; GOV.UK content guidance: no block capitals for large amounts of text. The 40-character cut-off in the rule is our own review threshold. In the Chrome demo the label measures 0.08em and no heading or button is uppercase. Large lowercase headlines at weight 900 with -0.02em tracking already read as blunt.
steps.label: craft-consensus

steps.title: Raw photos without stretching
steps.do: Make photos look raw with filters, hard crops, borders and a slight rotation, never with a stretched aspect ratio. Fit every image with object-fit: cover and an object-position that keeps the subject in view.
steps.how: MDN: the default object-fit: fill distorts; cover crops and contain letterboxes. A grayscale(1) contrast(1.3) filter, a 3px border and rotate(-2deg) give the harsh look without changing the ratio. Measured in Chrome: a 400x300 source in a 300x300 box with object-fit: cover keeps its proportions (cropped), while the same image with the default fill is the distorting case. Check small screens for the subject with object-position. Measured 2026-11-06 in Chrome (Playwright, channel chrome) on the recipe demo page with the audit probes; a fixed width: 300px photo overflowed a 272 px content box at 320 px (right edge 329 px); width: min(300px, 100%) with aspect-ratio fixes it.
steps.label: craft-consensus

code.text:
.photo { width: min(300px, 100%); height: auto; aspect-ratio: 1; object-fit: cover; object-position: 50% 30%;
  border: 3px solid #111; filter: grayscale(1) contrast(1.3); transform: rotate(-2deg); }

steps.title: Hard shadow snap on press
steps.do: Use the snap of the hard shadow as the interaction: on hover or press the button moves toward its shadow in about 100 ms with a decelerating curve, and returns with an accelerating one. Do not use linear easing on the transform.
steps.how: NN/g: about 100 ms for feedback, ease-out for things appearing, ease-in for leaving, exits shorter than entrances. Material motion tokens: decelerate for enter, accelerate for exit. Measured in Chrome: transition-duration 0.1s and cubic-bezier(0, 0, 0.2, 1) on transform. Mapping the pressed state to "entering" and release to "leaving" is our interpretation. The 3 to 6 px translation is small, but wrap larger movement in prefers-reduced-motion.
steps.label: craft-consensus
steps.status_note: Duration and easing guidance are from the sources read; treating press as an entrance and release as an exit is our reading of the rule.

steps.title: Underlined links, bordered buttons
steps.do: Keep the raw default look of links and make it explicit: underline every inline link, give every button a fill and a 3px border, and keep targets at least 44 px tall (WCAG minimum is 24 by 24).
steps.how: An underlined link in a different colour passes the "not colour alone" test; Chrome demo measures underline on inline links and 44 px tall buttons and tabs. Do a grayscale screenshot: every link and button should still be findable.
steps.label: craft-consensus

steps.title: Hard shadow only on pressables
steps.do: Reserve the hard offset shadow for things you can press. Static cards, chips and stickers get the flat 3px border and a fill, with no shadow.
steps.how: In this style the shadow is what reads as raised and pressable. If a decorative card carries the same shadow as a button, a visitor cannot tell the two apart. Check the grayscale screenshot for anything non-interactive that looks like a control.
steps.label: our-take
steps.status_note: Our recommendation; COGA asks that non-interactive items do not look clickable, the shadow-as-affordance reading is ours.

steps.title: Outline focus, borders for forced colors
steps.do: Draw focus with an outline in a colour that contrasts with both paper and fills, not with the hard shadow, and keep the 3px borders so boundaries survive forced colours. Add a prefers-contrast: more token that thickens borders and darkens muted text.
steps.how: MDN: in forced-colors mode border-color and outline-color are kept as system colours while box-shadow becomes none, and :focus-visible indicators need 3:1. Focus ring #1D2BFF is 7.39:1 on paper and 5.23:1 on yellow. Measured in Chrome 156 with forced colours emulated: the button shadow computes to none and the 3px solid borders remain; with contrast: more emulated the border token becomes 5px and muted text turns to ink. Keyboard focus measured as a 4px solid #1D2BFF ring with 3px offset.
steps.label: craft-consensus

code.text:
:focus-visible { outline: 4px solid var(--focus); outline-offset: 3px; }
@media (prefers-contrast: more) { :root { --border: 5px; --muted: #111; } }

steps.title: Radius and elevation per role
steps.do: Define radius and elevation per role: cards and inputs 0, buttons 8 px, tags pill, images 0; shadows sm (3px 3px 0) and md (6px 6px 0) with zero blur. Mark emphasis with a fill or a full border, not a thick coloured stripe on one side of a rounded card.
steps.how: The rule fails a page where every role shares one radius of 16 px or more, where three or more adjacent cards pair a hairline border with a blur of 32 px or more, or where a rounded element has one thick coloured side. Hard shadows have zero blur, so they pass by construction. If you want a left bar on a callout, use radius 0 on that element. Chrome demo: the roles compute to different radii, no element has a single thick side border with a radius of 4 px or more.
steps.label: craft-consensus
steps.status_note: Thresholds come from practitioner detectors and articles (one is rated low weight in sources.json); we measured the demo against the rule text, not against a standard.

steps.title: Raw look, real semantics
steps.do: Raw does not mean unstructured. Style the real patterns: a tablist with role=tab buttons, aria-selected on exactly one, aria-controls and a labelled tabpanel; accordion headers as h3 containing one button with aria-expanded; tables with a caption and th scope. Wrap a wide table in a focusable scroll region: div role=region, aria-label, tabindex=0, overflow-x: auto. Controls that only work with script (tab buttons, accordion buttons) must not exist without it: leave every panel visible in the HTML, keep the tablist hidden (with [hidden] { display: none !important } so no author display rule overrides it) or build the accordion button from the plain heading in the script, and make call-to-action buttons real links or form submits.
steps.how: Follow the ARIA Authoring Practices tabs and accordion patterns and Inclusive Components for tables and collapsible sections. Chrome demo checks: every tab sits in a named tablist, one aria-selected=true, each panel points back with aria-labelledby, ArrowRight moves selection and focus, tabindex=-1 on inactive tabs; the accordion button is the only child of its heading, aria-expanded flips on click and the collapsed panel is display:none so its links are not focusable; the table has a caption, th scope=col and scope=row. Native details/summary is a reasonable alternative but the rule check expects a button inside a heading. Measured 2026-11-06 in Chrome (Playwright, channel chrome) on the recipe demo page with the audit probes; at 200% root text and 320 px a three-column table overflowed by 133 px (219 px with text spacing applied); the scroll wrapper removed the page-level overflow and axe accepted the focusable region.
steps.label: standard

code.text: ...

steps.title: Attitude in marketing, literal elsewhere
steps.do: Let attitude live in marketing lines and keep a plain statement of the offer on the first screen. Errors, checkout, security and deletion text stays neutral and literal: say what the system needs, no jokes, no apology, none of invalid, incorrect, please, sorry, oops. Chips that are not a live status must not read New, Live or Beta, and warning or error icons are inline SVG, not emoji.
steps.how: Mailchimp: voice stays constant while tone shifts with the reader's state; NN/g and GOV.UK: errors are specific, non-blaming, without humour. Pattern for an empty field is "Enter your email address", for a wrong value "Card number must be 16 digits". A blunt headline ("Send invoices that get paid") sits next to a plain offer line. Chrome demo greps its error strings for the banned list and exclamation marks: none found.
steps.label: craft-consensus

recipes.generate_hint: Use ink on flat fills with verified contrast, 3px solid borders and hard shadows with zero blur, sentence-case headings and uppercase only for short letterspaced labels, object-fit cover for every image, real tab, accordion and table markup, a blue focus ring, and neutral literal error text.

recipes.title: Playful, quirky and friendly voices that stay clear
recipes.summary: Keep the personality, the jokes, the mascot and the warm colours. Put the wit in kickers and supporting lines, keep headings, buttons, errors and money screens literal, and let motion respect reduced-motion settings.
recipes.keep: A distinct voice, a mascot or recurring character, bright warm colours, bouncy motion, conversational marketing copy.
recipes.avoid: Idioms, puns and metaphors as headlines, nav labels or buttons; humour or blame in errors; "please", "simply", "just", "easy" and exclamation points in instructions; white text on bright fills; endless looping motion.

steps.title: Warm fills with ink text
steps.do: Use bright warm colours as fills and put ink on them. Coral #FF6B3D with white text is 2.83:1 and fails; ink #1B1B1F on the same coral is 6.07:1. Sun yellow #FFD23F with ink is 11.89:1. Keep the error red #B42318 (6.57:1 on white, 5.96:1 on its tint) and success green #0B5D3A (7.95:1) for those states only.
steps.how: Link #1D4ED8 is 6.7:1 on white; muted text #4B4B55 is 8.62:1. Field borders carry meaning, so give them a 3:1 colour (the error border is 6.57:1). Rendered in Chrome: computed colours match each claimed pair.
steps.label: standard

steps.title: Plain offer as the headline
steps.do: Write the plain statement of the offer as the headline, nav label or button, and put the pun, joke or character in a kicker or the supporting line. "Plan a trip with friends" is the h1; "Meet Pip" and "Pip keeps the spreadsheets away" carry the personality.
steps.how: NN/g: headlines work out of context and avoid cute or idiomatic language; Google style guide: avoid slang and figurative language; W3C COGA: avoid metaphors and idioms in navigation and calls to action. Test: read each headline, nav label and button aloud to someone who does not know the product; if a literal reading misleads, rewrite it. Buttons start with a verb in sentence case ("Create a free account").
steps.label: craft-consensus

steps.title: Name sections by what they say
steps.do: Name every section by what it says ("Split costs without the maths"), so the heading list read alone summarises the page. Never use "Features", "Overview", "Why choose us" or "Our approach", and do not prefix feature cards with emoji.
steps.how: GOV.UK content guidance and NN/g: headings that describe the content beneath them. The Chrome demo extracts its heading outline and matches it against the rule blocklist (introduction, overview, features, benefits, our approach, why us, about, welcome): none match, and the outline reads as a summary. Order sections by the questions this buyer asks, not by the stock hero, logos, three cards, pricing sequence.
steps.label: craft-consensus

steps.title: Specific, neutral error messages
steps.do: Write errors as specific, neutral instructions: "Enter your email address" for an empty field, "Postcode must be in the format AB1 2CD" for a wrong value. Show them with an icon, text and a changed border, linked to the field with aria-describedby, in an error colour that passes (6.57:1 on white).
steps.how: GOV.UK error-message guidance: say what happened and how to fix it; avoid "valid/invalid", "please", "sorry", "oops", "forbidden", "you forgot" and "This field is required". NN/g: nonblaming positive tone, no humour in errors except a rare total failure. WCAG 1.4.1 and failure F81: errors must not be identified by colour only. Chrome demo: both invalid inputs have a label, a described-by message of real text, an icon and a changed border; the error strings contain none of the banned words or exclamation marks.
steps.label: craft-consensus

code.text: ⚠ Enter your email address

steps.title: Plain imperative instructions
steps.do: Give instructions as plain imperatives: "Enter the email address you use for bookings." Drop "please", "please note", "simply", "just", "easy", "quickly", "it's that simple" and exclamation points from interface text. Marketing headlines may keep their energy.
steps.how: GOV.UK tone guidance and Google developer style guide list these softeners as words to avoid. The check is a grep over UI strings, hints, instructions and help text, excluding marketing headlines and testimonials; the Chrome demo ran that grep over its UI zone and found none.
steps.label: craft-consensus

steps.title: Dial personality down as stakes rise
steps.do: Turn personality down as the stakes go up: full voice in marketing sections, light touches in onboarding, neutral wording on forms and errors, and literal text on payment, security, cancellation, deletion and legal surfaces, with no joke, slang, hype word or exclamation point.
steps.how: Mailchimp: voice stays constant, tone shifts with the reader's state; NN/g: humour only for rare total failures. Write the surface list once ("marketing, onboarding, forms, errors, checkout, security, deletion, legal") with a tone for each, and sample the copy of the risky surfaces. The demo's payment copy ("Your card is charged when the trip is booked...") is deliberately literal.
steps.label: craft-consensus

steps.title: Write a voice sheet first
steps.do: Write a voice sheet before the copy: three or four trait words, each with a do and a don't example, plus the fixed choices (you or we, contractions, US or UK spelling). Allow one quirky element per surface so the oddness stays a signature.
steps.how: Mailchimp and Microsoft publish voice guidance as traits with examples. Sample six surfaces (hero, navigation, buttons, errors, footer, 404) against the sheet and fail mixed spelling or person. The "one quirk per surface" budget is our own heuristic.
steps.label: craft-consensus

code.text:
Voice: warm, specific, a little odd.
Warm      do "Pip sorted the costs"          don't "Users must remit payment"
Specific  do "3 of 5 friends have paid"      don't "Great progress!"
Odd       do one mascot line per page         don't puns in nav labels
Fixed: address the reader as "you", use contractions, UK spelling.

steps.status_note: Voice-sheet practice is in the sources read; the one-quirk-per-surface budget is our heuristic.

steps.title: Limit three quirky copy patterns
steps.do: Watch for the three patterns quirky copy slides into: "not X, it's Y", three parallel slogans ("Save time. Work smarter. Scale faster."), and self-answered questions ("The result?"). Use each at most once per page and say the claim directly otherwise.
steps.how: The rule is advisory and our own take, drawn from lists of AI-writing tells. A regex pass over the page text counts the hits: fail above one of each kind. A list of two or four items, when the items really are distinct, avoids the tricolon.
steps.label: our-take
steps.status_note: Advisory rule labelled our-take; the sources are lists of AI-writing tells, not studies of reader outcomes.

steps.title: Finite, optional bouncy motion
steps.do: Keep bouncy motion finite and optional: a mascot hop that runs three times (3.6 s) and then stops, a prefers-reduced-motion block that removes it, and nothing flashing. Any loop longer than five seconds next to other content needs a visible pause control.
steps.how: MDN: replace large-scale motion with gentler effects under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce. WCAG 2.2.2: moving or blinking content that starts automatically, lasts more than five seconds and sits beside other content needs pause, stop or hide. Measured in Chrome: the hop is one animation of 1.2 s x 3 iterations; with reduced motion emulated it computes to animation-name none and no running animation.
steps.label: standard

code.text:
.mascot { animation: hop 1.2s cubic-bezier(0, 0, 0.2, 1) 3; }
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .mascot { animation: none; } }

steps.title: Wrap the h1, SVG icons
steps.do: Give the h1 overflow-wrap: anywhere (a 3rem h1 overflowed by 35 px at 320 px with 200% text) and draw warning and error icons as inline SVG with currentColor and aria-hidden, never as emoji (distinct-real-imagery-and-icons).
steps.how: Measured 2026-11-06 in Chrome (Playwright, channel chrome) on the recipe demo page at 320 px with the root font size at 200% and the audit probes; 35 px of overflow and two emoji-as-icon minors were both gone after the change.
steps.label: standard
steps.measured: Measured 2026-11-06 in Chrome (Playwright, channel chrome) on the recipe demo page at 320 px with the root font size at 200% and the audit probes; 35 px of overflow and two emoji-as-icon minors were both gone after the change.

recipes.generate_hint: Write the plain headline first and add the quirk as a kicker or supporting line, name every section by what it says, write errors as "Enter..." or "X must be...", and keep payments, security and deletion neutral.

recipes.title: Maximalist, Memphis and collage layouts with order underneath
recipes.summary: Keep the density, the confetti shapes, the clashing colours and the overlapping cut-outs. Put the noise in a decorative layer, keep text on solid plates, and hold a few quiet constants (two typefaces, a size scale, a spacing scale, a line length, one icon family) so the page reads as one loud system.
recipes.keep: Many bright colours, geometric confetti, rotated cut-outs and stickers, layered shapes, big display type, dense compositions.
recipes.avoid: Text directly on patterns or confetti; a link or error colour reused as decoration; more than two typefaces or ad hoc sizes and gaps; stretched cut-outs; dozens of equal-weight choices; cards that are a link wrapper around everything; modals built without dialog semantics; drifting shapes that never stop.

contrast.pair: ink on coral chip (decor, small text)

steps.title: Text on flat plates
steps.do: Put the noise around the text, not under it. Every line of text sits on a flat plate or a plain band, and the shapes, stickers and patterns live in a decorative layer. Ink #1A1033 is 12.47:1 on yellow #FFD23F, 8.47:1 on pink #FF8FB8, 11.58:1 on teal #7DE0D6, 8.4:1 on periwinkle #B8A4FF, 6.49:1 on coral #FF6B6B, 18.01:1 on white.
steps.how: Never set text in a pastel on a pastel. Link blue #2F27CE is 9.12:1 on white and 8.04:1 on the lilac band. The decorative layer is a sibling element with position:absolute, z-index 0, pointer-events:none and aria-hidden="true". Rendered in Chrome: the computed colours of the demo's plates, bands, links and buttons match the claimed pairs.
steps.label: standard

steps.title: Fix quiet constants first
steps.do: Fix the quiet constants before adding colour: two font families (a display face and a body face), six to eight named type sizes, and a spacing scale on a 4 px base (4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 48, 64, 96). Loudness comes from colour, shape and rotation, not from a new size or gap every time.
steps.how: Define the scales as custom properties and use only those. Measured in the Chrome demo: 5 distinct font sizes (14, 16, 20, 40, 64 px), 2 families, 7 distinct spacing values, every one a multiple of 4. The rule caps are 8 sizes, 2 families (advisory, our-take) and 12 spacing values.
steps.label: craft-consensus
steps.status_note: Measured on a demo built to the scales; the two-family limit is an advisory our-take rule and the 8-size and 12-value caps are the rules' own thresholds, not studies.

steps.title: Separate semantic and decorative palettes
steps.do: Keep two palettes apart. The semantic set (link, primary button, focus, error, success) is used only for those jobs; the decorative set (yellow, pink, teal, periwinkle, coral here) carries the Memphis energy. Link blue and error red never appear as a shape, border or text colour on non-interactive content.
steps.how: GOV.UK Design System: colours are assigned by function, and the focus colour is reserved. In the Chrome demo every element was scanned: link blue (#2F27CE) and error red (#B3261E) occur only on links, buttons and the error message; the five decorative colours appear on plates and shapes. Pick decorative hues that are visibly different from the link hue.
steps.label: craft-consensus

steps.title: 50ch text in a 1280 px container
steps.do: Cap running text with max-inline-size around 50ch (not 55ch) and put the content in a centred container of 1280 px or less; let only the coloured band and decorative layer run edge to edge. Then count characters per line in the browser instead of trusting the number.
steps.how: Measured in Chrome 156 on macOS by counting characters on every rendered line: with max-inline-size 66ch, proportional faces gave 87 to 96 characters per line at most (system-ui and Georgia 96, Arial and Helvetica Neue 87), over the 75-character cap; 60ch gave 77 to 89, 55ch gave 69 to 83, 45ch gave 59 to 67, and 50ch gave a longest line of 67 to 74 (average 60 to 69). The reason is that 1ch is the width of the digit 0, wider than an average letter; only a monospace face gets about one character per ch. So 50ch is the safe value for system-ui, Arial, Georgia, Helvetica Neue and Arial Narrow; other platforms' fonts were not measured. In the demo the longest line is 70 characters at 768, 1280 and 1920 px and the container is 1280 px at a 1920 px viewport while the band is 1920 px wide.
steps.label: craft-consensus

code.text:
.prose { max-inline-size: 50ch; }          /* about 60-70 characters in proportional faces; verify */
.wrap  { max-inline-size: 1280px; margin-inline: auto; }  /* the band behind it is full-bleed */

steps.title: Tight inside groups, loose between
steps.do: Dense is not the same as unstructured. Keep the gap inside a group (heading to its content, 16 px) clearly smaller than the gap between groups (48 px), including across overlapping or rotated pieces.
steps.how: Proximity tells the eye what belongs together when colour and shape are all loud. Check each heading: margin above greater than margin below, and the internal gap of a card smaller than the gap to its neighbour. The demo measures 16 px inside groups against 48 px between them.
steps.label: our-take
steps.status_note: The rule is labelled our-take; Apple and Butterick support heading proximity but not the exact gaps.

steps.title: Dense page, about five choices
steps.do: Let the page be visually dense while each viewport-height section offers one dominant action and at most about five choices in total. Move the rest to a footer or a titled "more" link.
steps.how: The COGA guidance and NN/g homepage principles favour one clearly dominant feature. The demo hero has five controls: one filled primary button, three secondary and one text link, counted in Chrome.
steps.label: craft-consensus

steps.title: One icon family on one grid
steps.do: Use one icon family at one stroke weight, corner style and fill treatment on a shared grid (24 px, stroke 2, round caps and joins, stroke currentColor). Stickers, confetti and illustrations are decoration, not icons, and may be as wild as you like. Status and warning icons are inline SVG from the same family, never emoji (distinct-real-imagery-and-icons).
steps.how: Apple HIG: same size, detail and stroke weight across a set, with stroke matched to adjacent text. web.dev: inline SVG so CSS can style it. Chrome demo: all three icons share stroke-width 2, round linecap and linejoin, no fill and a 24x24 viewBox.
steps.label: craft-consensus

steps.title: Cards as list items with stretched link
steps.do: Make each card a list item with one heading level and one link inside the heading; stretch the click area with a ::after pseudo-element. Draw the focus indication on the link itself (a background and a thicker underline), and keep a ring on the card with :has(a:focus-visible) as a bonus. Decorative card images get alt="".
steps.how: Inclusive Components cards pattern. Tested in Chrome: each li has one link inside h3, clicking the lower part of the rotated card follows the link, and keyboard focus on the link draws a solid 3px outline on the card. A rotated card's bounding box is larger than the card, so click inside the shape when testing. Measured 2026-11-06 in Chrome (Playwright, channel chrome) on the recipe demo page with the audit probes; a version that removed the link's outline and drew the ring only on the card through :has() failed a11y-focus-visible on 3 of 9 Tab stops, because the probe (and a person using forced colours) looks at the focused element itself; adding a background and underline change on the link itself fixed it.
steps.label: our-take
steps.status_note: Behaviour tested in Chrome 156; the Inclusive Components page entry in sources.json has no notes, so the pattern details beyond the rule text are from our own testing.
steps.measured: Measured 2026-11-06 in Chrome (Playwright, channel chrome) on the recipe demo page with the audit probes; 3 of 9 Tab stops showed no change on the focused element with a ring only on the card; 0 after the link itself changed.

steps.title: Native dialog with showModal
steps.do: Build modals with a native dialog opened by showModal(), named by aria-labelledby pointing at its visible title, with every control inside it. Style the dialog and ::backdrop as loudly as you like.
steps.how: ARIA Authoring Practices modal dialog: focus moves in, Tab stays inside, Escape closes, focus returns. Measured in Chrome 156: after showModal() the dialog matches :modal, focus is inside, the accessibility tree exposes a dialog named "Delivery details", six Tab presses stay inside, an outside button cannot take focus, and Escape returns focus to the opener. The demo also sets aria-modal="true" because the rule check looks for it; with showModal() the page behind is genuinely blocked, so the attribute is truthful.
steps.label: standard

code.text:
Delivery details

...

steps.title: Rotate and crop without stretching
steps.do: Rotate, overlap and crop cut-outs freely, but with transforms that only rotate or translate, and fit each image with object-fit: contain for cut-outs or cover for cropped photos, never fill.
steps.how: MDN object-fit: fill (the default) distorts. A transform of rotate() keeps scale at 1; measured in Chrome by decomposing the computed matrix of each collage image: scale 1 by 1 on both, object-fit contain and cover. Transparent PNG, AVIF or SVG cut-outs go in with a real alt text when they carry meaning.
steps.label: craft-consensus

steps.title: Pausable confetti, reduced-motion off
steps.do: Give drifting confetti an off switch and an off state: a visible "Pause decoration" toggle with aria-pressed, a prefers-reduced-motion block that removes the animation, and no flashing. Never let the movement run behind text without these.
steps.how: WCAG 2.2.2: automatically starting movement lasting more than five seconds beside other content needs pause, stop or hide. Chrome demo: three drifting shapes run on an infinite 8 s loop; the button pauses all three (playState paused, aria-pressed true); with reduced motion emulated no animation exists. The toggle keeps one stable label and uses aria-pressed.
steps.label: standard

steps.title: Collage with CSS, not reordering
steps.do: Collage by CSS, not by reordering. Keep DOM order equal to reading order, use grid or absolute placement for overlap, avoid CSS order, row-reverse and positive tabindex, and let the layout collapse to one column at 320 px with no horizontal scroll. Give h1 to h3 overflow-wrap: anywhere and size grid tracks as minmax(min(14rem, 100%), 1fr), because large display words and fixed tracks overflow at 320 px when text is zoomed to 200%.
steps.how: MDN: CSS order changes only the visual order, not the logical or tab order; WCAG 1.3.2 and 1.4.10. Chrome demo: no element has order other than 0, flex-direction reverse or tabindex above 0, and document width equals viewport width at 320, 768, 1280 and 1920 px. Measured 2026-11-06 in Chrome (Playwright, channel chrome) on the recipe demo page with the audit probes; with root text at 200% and 320 px the page scrolled 180 px sideways (the word 'patterns' at 4rem is about 594 px wide; a 12rem track is 384 px); it passed at 100% text.
steps.label: standard

steps.title: Loud shapes, literal copy
steps.do: Memphis energy goes in colour and shape. Keep headlines, labels and buttons literal, errors neutral ("Enter a delivery postcode") and payment or account copy free of jokes; save the wordplay for a supporting line.
steps.how: Same sources and tests as the playful-quirky-voice recipe: NN/g error guidance (non-blaming, no humour), GOV.UK error wording, Mailchimp on tone shifting with the reader's state. The demo error string contains none of invalid, incorrect, please, sorry, oops or an exclamation mark.
steps.label: craft-consensus

recipes.generate_hint: Choose a decorative palette separate from the link and error colours, put every line of text on a solid plate, fix two fonts, six to eight sizes and a 4 or 8 px spacing scale, cap text at 55ch inside a container of 1280px or less, and make the decorative layer aria-hidden, pausable and removed under reduced motion.

recipes.title: Illustration, hand-drawn and graphic-only art that stays accessible
recipes.summary: Keep the drawn world: sketchy lines, hand lettering, abstract shapes and patterns. Use real authored artwork instead of code-assembled scenes, keep UI icons in one currentColor family, give informative art an alternative and decorative art none, keep meaningful lines at 3:1, and make draw-on animation end in a finished drawing.
recipes.keep: Hand-drawn lines, doodles, marker highlights, hand lettering, flat or textured illustration, abstract graphic fields.
recipes.avoid: Hero scenes assembled from div or SVG primitives in code; emoji or mixed-weight icons; pale pencil lines that carry meaning; headlines as images of text; the same artwork for light and dark grounds; draw-on animations that hide the art for reduced-motion users; abstract graphics as the only message.

contrast.pair: dark mode: light line art on night ground

steps.title: Use real authored illustration
steps.do: Make the illustration real: commissioned, drawn by you or licensed, exported as SVG, AVIF or PNG files and placed with img or picture. Do not build hero scenes out of div rectangles or a pile of inline SVG primitives, do not use placeholder image hosts, and do not use emoji as icons.
steps.how: The rule flags placeholder hosts (picsum, placehold, via.placeholder), product mock-ups made of div rectangles, hero-sized inline SVG scenes assembled from primitive shapes and emoji used as icons. An illustrator's exported file passes because it is a file, however many paths it has. Chrome demo scan: no emoji in buttons, links or headings, no inline SVG wider than half the viewport with five or more primitives, no placeholder hosts.
steps.label: our-take
steps.status_note: The rule comes from practitioner anti-slop detectors; the remedy (ship authored art as files) is our recommendation, not a standard.

steps.title: Separate UI icons from illustration
steps.do: Keep illustration and UI icons separate. Illustrations may use any palette; UI icons are one inline-SVG family at one stroke weight (24 px grid, stroke 2, round caps) with stroke="currentColor", sized with CSS, so hover, focus, dark mode and forced colours recolour them. Full-colour or raster icons are art, not controls.
steps.how: web.dev icons: inline SVG so CSS can style it; Apple HIG: one stroke weight across a set, matched to adjacent text. Measured in Chrome 156: the icon's computed stroke equals its button's computed colour on rest, on hover (#1D4ED8), in emulated dark scheme (#E8E8EC) and in forced colours (system colour), and the demo icons all use stroke-width 2.
steps.label: craft-consensus

code.text: <button class="btn"><svg class="icon" aria-hidden="true" viewBox="0 0 24 24" width="24" height="24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><path d="M4 12h16M14 6l6 6-6 6"/></svg> Read the latest entry</button>

steps.title: Alt text by purpose of the art
steps.do: Decide for each drawing whether it informs or decorates. Informative art gets alt text that states its purpose in context (about 150 characters at most, no "image of", no repeating nearby text); decorative flourishes get alt="" or are CSS backgrounds; inline SVG that carries meaning gets role="img" and an accessible name; complex diagrams get a longer description in the page text.
steps.how: WCAG 1.1.1: pure decoration should be ignorable by assistive technology. NN/g and WebAIM alt text guidance. Measured in Chrome 156 with Playwright's accessibility snapshot of the demo: the hero sketch and the labelled scribble appear as named images, the alt="" flourish and the aria-hidden pattern do not appear, and the heading is exposed as a level 1 heading.
steps.label: standard

steps.title: Meaningful lines at 3:1
steps.do: Hold every line that carries meaning (diagram strokes, input outlines, chart axes, the outline of a character that explains something) at 3:1 against its ground. On paper #FBF9F4, pencil #595959 is 6.66:1 and the faintest usable line #8C8C8C is 3.2:1. Pale guide lines such as #BDBDBD (1.79:1) are decoration only.
steps.how: WCAG 1.4.11 asks 3:1 for graphics needed to understand content; 1.4.3 asks 4.5:1 for text. Ink text is 15.61:1 on paper, ink on a marker-yellow highlight #FFE066 is 12.6:1, a red-pen annotation #B3261E is 6.21:1, the link #1D4ED8 is 6.37:1. A sketchy look comes from line wobble and texture, not from pale strokes. Rendered stroke and text colours in the Chrome demo match these pairs.
steps.label: standard

steps.title: Hand lettering as real text
steps.do: Set hand lettering as real text in a handwriting or brush webfont at large sizes in dark ink, specified in rem so 200% text zoom works, and keep body copy in a plain face. Lettering that has to be artwork is allowed only as a logotype or when the look is essential, and then it needs alt text with the same words.
steps.how: WCAG 1.4.5: use real text when the technology can achieve the presentation; the exceptions are customizable, essential and logotype. WCAG 1.4.4: text must reach 200%; viewport-unit-only sizing fails (F94). 24 px or larger counts as large text (3:1), but we advise 4.5:1 anyway for thin strokes. Demo: the h1 is a real heading at 48 px (3rem), no image inside it. That handwriting faces read poorly at small sizes is our observation and is not tested here; self-host the font rather than relying on system stacks.
steps.label: craft-consensus
steps.status_note: The WCAG facts are verified; the advice about small handwriting text and the 4.5:1 habit for thin strokes is our judgement, and the 200% zoom was not re-measured for this demo.

steps.title: Draw-on animation ends finished
steps.do: Make the finished drawing the default state and animate toward it: the path is fully visible with no animation, and the draw-on keyframes run once, in under five seconds, from hidden to complete. Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, remove the animation so the finished art is shown.
steps.how: MDN: honour reduce by replacing large motion with gentler effects and do not lose what the animation conveys. WCAG 2.2.2 applies to movement that lasts more than five seconds; a single 2 s draw is under that. Measured in Chrome: one animation of 2 s, 1 iteration; with reduced motion emulated there is no animation and stroke-dashoffset computes to 0, so nothing is hidden. If you set the hidden state in the base CSS and rely on the animation to reveal it, no-JS and reduced-motion users get an empty box.
steps.label: standard

steps.title: Second artwork for dark grounds
steps.do: Do not reuse dark line art on a dark ground. Ink #1F1F23 on a #14141A ground is 1.12:1. Ship a second artwork through picture with a prefers-color-scheme: dark source, or draw line art as inline SVG with currentColor and a token (#E8E8EC on #14141A is 15.01:1).
steps.how: web.dev theming and Apple HIG dark mode: re-check contrast in each theme and dim or swap images rather than inverting. Measured in Chrome with the colour scheme emulated: the picture element's currentSrc switches to the dark artwork, and the line-art token resolves to #E8E8EC on #14141A.
steps.label: craft-consensus

steps.title: Pair abstract graphics with real content
steps.do: When the page uses abstract shapes, gradients or patterns instead of pictures, make them decoration (CSS background or aria-hidden SVG) and pair them with something concrete on the first screen: the product, a real screenshot, a drawing of the actual subject. Abstract art alone cannot say what you sell.
steps.how: A pattern that carries no information should be ignorable by assistive technology (WCAG 1.1.1), so use a CSS background or aria-hidden. The rule also flags hero-size inline SVG scenes built from primitive shapes, so build generative fields in CSS, canvas with fallback content, or ship them as exported files. The demo's pattern is a repeating-linear-gradient on an aria-hidden block, and no inline SVG in it is larger than half the viewport.
steps.label: our-take
steps.status_note: Pairing abstract art with a concrete subject is our recommendation; the decorative-versus-informative handling is verified in il-alt.

steps.title: Wrap long words in display fonts
steps.do: Handwriting and display fonts are wide: give the h1 overflow-wrap: anywhere and a smaller rem size under 30rem so a single word such as 'sketchbook' (446 px at 200%) fits.
steps.how: Measured 2026-11-06 in Chrome (Playwright, channel chrome) on the recipe demo page at 320 px with the root font size at 200%; span.mark right edge was 478 px at 320 px wide; after the fix 0 px of overflow.
steps.label: standard
steps.measured: Measured 2026-11-06 in Chrome (Playwright, channel chrome) on the recipe demo page at 320 px with the root font size at 200%; span.mark right edge was 478 px at 320 px wide; after the fix 0 px of overflow.

recipes.generate_hint: Commission or draw the art and ship it as files, keep UI icons as one inline SVG family in currentColor, write alt text only for informative images, hold meaningful line art at 3:1 or better, set hand lettering as real text, and show the finished drawing when motion is reduced.

recipes.title: Clay, skeuomorphic and dimensional UI with real edges and legible text
recipes.summary: Keep the puffy shapes, soft light, materials and knobs. Let the shadow be mood, not the boundary: give controls a transparent border that survives forced colours and an edge colour that reaches 3:1, put text on opaque plates, flatten groups so cards do not nest, and vary radius and elevation by role.
recipes.keep: Inflated rounded shapes, soft raised and inset shadows, tactile buttons, material textures, knobs and switches.
recipes.avoid: Shadow as the only boundary of an input or control; text directly on a texture; cards inside cards inside cards; one radius for every role; raster or fixed-colour icons for controls; state shown only by a colour shift on a pressed button.

contrast.pair: input edge on clay surface (UI boundary)
ink on brushed-metal plate, worst rendered pixel (measured)
dark: ink on dark clay surface
dark: muted on dark clay surface
dark: input edge on dark surface (UI boundary)
dark: dark text on mint button

steps.title: Real edges on controls
steps.do: Treat shadows as mood and give anything the user must find a real edge or fill. Inputs get a 2px edge in #5E7A70 (4.38:1 on the clay surface, 4.01:1 on the canvas); buttons get a label in dark ink on a coloured fill, not a surface-coloured pill that only a shadow separates from the page.
steps.how: Clay surface #F3F9F6 on canvas #E6F0EC is only 1.09:1, which is a fine look and no boundary. Text pairs: ink #1E2B27 on surface 13.77:1, muted #44524D on surface 7.69:1, ink on peach #FFB8A3 8.84:1, white on blue #2F5BEA 5.52:1. WCAG 1.4.11 asks 3:1 for visual information needed to identify a control. Rendered colours in the Chrome demo match every claimed pair.
steps.label: standard

steps.title: Transparent borders and outline focus
steps.do: Give every raised surface and control a 2px transparent border, and draw keyboard focus with outline. In forced-colors mode the soft shadows disappear and the transparent border becomes a visible system-colour edge; the outline stays.
steps.how: MDN: in forced-colors mode box-shadow is forced to none while border-color and outline-color are kept as system colours. Measured in Chrome 156 with forced colours emulated: card and button box-shadow compute to none, the transparent border computes to rgb(0, 0, 0) at 2px, and a pixel row across the card edge shows black pixels against white where the normal rendering had a soft shadow with no hard edge; keyboard focus is a solid 3px outline in both modes. Normal mode is unchanged because a transparent border draws nothing.
steps.label: craft-consensus

code.text:
.card, .btn { border: 2px solid transparent; box-shadow: var(--raise); }
:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid var(--ink); outline-offset: 3px; }

steps.title: Radius and elevation per role
steps.do: Name a radius per role (control 14, input 10, card 28, media 20, badge pill) and an elevation per state (raise, inset, press) and use each one the same way everywhere. Keep card-row shadow blur modest (14 px here) and do not combine a visible hairline border with a blur of 32 px or more on three or more adjacent cards.
steps.how: The rule fails a page where every role shares one radius of 16 px or more, or where three adjacent cards pair a visible 1px border with a blur of 32 px or more. Chrome demo: card, button, input and badge compute to 28, 14, 10 and 999 px; the three cards in the row have a 14 px blur and a transparent border. Soft clay shadows read well at 12 to 20 px.
steps.label: craft-consensus
steps.status_note: Thresholds are from practitioner detectors and articles; we measured the demo against the rule text only.

steps.title: No raised boxes inside clay cards
steps.do: Let a clay card hold unboxed content: headings, paragraphs and list rows separated by spacing, with no raised or inset container inside it other than interactive controls. If a skeuomorphic panel needs a recessed well, make the well the panel instead of a box inside another box.
steps.how: Rule: no bordered, shadowed or tinted card container inside another. We implemented that check for non-interactive containers with radius of 4 px or more and ran it in Chrome: the demo has no nested container, and a deliberately nested card inserted by the test is flagged. Buttons, inputs and badges are controls, not containers, so they are exempt in our check; the rule text does not say so explicitly.
steps.label: craft-consensus
steps.status_note: Our implementation of the check treats controls as exempt, which is an interpretation; the underlying rule is from practitioner sources.

steps.title: Inline SVG icons with currentColor
steps.do: Draw UI icons as inline SVG with stroke or fill set to currentColor so hover, dark mode and forced colours recolour them. Keep realistic or 3D icon renderings for illustration (decorative, alt="" or named) and never as the only control icon.
steps.how: web.dev icons: inline SVG so CSS can style it. Measured in Chrome: the Reset icon's computed stroke equals its button colour in light and in emulated dark scheme, and the stroke attribute is currentColor.
steps.label: craft-consensus

steps.title: Measure text over textures
steps.do: Put realistic textures (brushed metal, leather, paper) on a solid base colour and measure the worst pixel under each line of text. The demo plate has a #E4E7EA to #B9BEC3 gradient with fine stripes; ink #1B1F23 measured 8.22:1 against its worst rendered pixel (#B3B7BB).
steps.how: Method: hide the text, screenshot the text box, read every pixel and compute the WCAG ratio against the text colour; the smallest ratio is the one to report. The gradient end alone would be 8.85:1, the stripes lower the darkest pixel and the result is 8.22:1. Keep textures subtle at the text and strong around the edges of the plate.
steps.label: craft-consensus

steps.title: Toggle state by shape and text
steps.do: Make pressed, on and selected states differ by shape and text, not by a colour shift: a switch knob that moves, an inset shadow that changes, and a label that says On or Off, with aria-pressed (or a native checkbox) carrying the state.
steps.how: Inclusive Components toggle button and the ARIA switch pattern; WCAG 1.4.1. Chrome demo: aria-pressed flips from false to true, the knob moves 18 px and the text changes from "Eco mode off" to "Eco mode on". The label text changes with the state here, so aria-pressed is not used together with a label that already says the opposite; if you keep the label fixed, keep aria-pressed.
steps.label: craft-consensus
steps.status_note: Behaviour measured in Chrome; the label-versus-aria-pressed point follows the Button pattern note from an earlier verification pass and was not re-read.

steps.title: Lighter surfaces instead of dark shadows
steps.do: In dark mode, replace dark drop shadows with lighter surfaces and a thin inset highlight, and re-pick the edge colour: ink #E8F0EC on surface #1D2426 is 13.59:1, muted #A9B8B2 7.64:1, edge #7E948B 4.87:1, dark text on mint #7FD1B9 8.2:1.
steps.how: Apple HIG dark mode and web.dev theming: define dark tokens separately and re-check contrast per theme. Chrome demo: under emulated dark scheme the tokens resolve to exactly these colours and the raise shadow becomes an inset highlight plus a dark drop. Whether this elevation reads well is a visual judgement; the numbers are measured.
steps.label: our-take
steps.status_note: Contrast values are computed; the elevation treatment for dark clay is our design judgement.

steps.title: Min() grids and wrapping cards
steps.do: Write every auto-fit or auto-fill grid as repeat(auto-fit, minmax(min(15rem, 100%), 1fr)); use overflow-wrap: anywhere on cards and max-inline-size: 100% on buttons; cut card and page padding to 1rem under 30rem.
steps.how: Measured 2026-11-06 in Chrome (Playwright, channel chrome) on the recipe demo page at 320 px with the root font size at 200%; minmax(15rem,1fr) is 480 px at 200% text and made the page scroll 192 px sideways at 320 px; with min(15rem,100%) and reduced padding the overflow was 0.
steps.label: standard
steps.measured: Measured 2026-11-06 in Chrome (Playwright, channel chrome) on the recipe demo page at 320 px with the root font size at 200%; minmax(15rem,1fr) is 480 px at 200% text and made the page scroll 192 px sideways at 320 px; with min(15rem,100%) and reduced padding the overflow was 0.

recipes.generate_hint: Define radius and shadow tokens per role, give inputs a 3:1 edge and every raised surface a transparent 2px border, keep text on solid fills, put the metal or leather texture on a base colour and measure its worst pixel, use outline for focus, and show toggle state with knob position and text.

recipes.title: Organic, botanical and earthy palettes that are not the reflex cream
recipes.summary: Keep the calm, rounded, plant-and-soil feeling. Take the ground colour from the subject (leaf mist, forest, soil) instead of cream with terracotta, vary radius by role with asymmetrical shapes only on images, and darken the greens and browns until text, links and field edges pass.
recipes.keep: Rounded forms, gentle shadows, botanical photography, mossy greens, ochres and soil browns, a slow human tone.
recipes.avoid: Cream background with terracotta accent and a serif display face by reflex; sage-green text on pale green; links that differ from body text only in a muted green; the same large radius on every element; leaf photography under text without a plate.

contrast.pair: dark forest: leaf-white text on forest
dark forest: muted leaf text on forest
soil: leaf-white text on soil brown
soil: amber accent on soil brown
leaf-white text on 86% forest plate over the lightest leaf pixel (#2F402F composite, measured 9.42)

steps.title: Choose ground from the subject
steps.do: Choose the page ground from the subject's world: leaf-tinted mist (#EEF2EA), deep forest (#14231A) or soil brown (#2A1F18), with moss (#3F5D3A) and ochre (#8A5A00) accents. If you do want cream with terracotta and a serif display face, record the subject reason in the direction file.
steps.how: The rule (advisory) reports three things together: a cream background (every channel at least 209, red at least green at least blue, red minus blue between 6 and 48), a terracotta or clay accent (hue about 10 to 30 degrees, moderate saturation) and a serif display face. We ran the rule's cream condition in code: mist #EEF2EA, forest and soil are not cream, while #F5EFE6, #F4EDE0 and #FAF6EE are. Moss is at about 111 degrees, ochre 39, lime 84 and amber 39, outside the terracotta band. An exception record can be one line: "Cream ground chosen because the product is a bakery; paper and flour are cream."
steps.label: craft-consensus
steps.status_note: Thresholds are practitioner detector values, and the alternative palettes are our suggestions; the colour arithmetic was computed.

steps.title: Darken natural colors until they pass
steps.do: Darken the natural colours until they pass, and keep sage for decoration. Ink #1F2A1C on mist is 13.17:1; secondary moss-grey #4A5A40 6.55:1; moss links #3F5D3A 6.53:1; white on a moss button 7.4:1; ochre #8A5A00 5.23:1. Sage #7A8A6C on mist is 3.26:1 and fails as text.
steps.how: A moss link against ink body text is 2.02:1, below the 3:1 needed to tell a link from surrounding text by colour alone, so underline links (WCAG technique G183 and failure F73). Computed colours of the demo's text, links, button and accent match the claimed pairs in Chrome.
steps.label: standard

steps.title: Visible edges on soft fields
steps.do: Soft rounded fields still need an edge: #6B7A5E at 2px is 4.59:1 on white and 4.05:1 on mist. Do not use a pale sage outline or a shadow as the only sign of a field.
steps.how: WCAG 1.4.11: 3:1 for visual information needed to identify a control. Measured: the rendered input border is #6B7A5E in the demo.
steps.label: standard

steps.title: Shape and elevation per role
steps.do: Vary shape by role: controls 12 px, cards 24 px, tags pill, and an asymmetrical organic radius on photographs only. Use two elevations (1px/2px small, 8px 24px soft) and never pair a hairline border with a blur of 32 px or more on a row of three cards.
steps.how: The rule fails a page where every role shares one radius of 16 px or more, which is the default look of soft UI. Measured in Chrome: button 12 px, card 24 px, tag 999 px, photo a four-value elliptical radius, card shadow blur 24 px with no border.
steps.label: craft-consensus
steps.status_note: Rule thresholds come from practitioner detectors; measured against the rule text only.

steps.title: Plate under text on photos
steps.do: Do not set text straight on leaf or garden photography. Put it on a plate: an 86% forest plate (#14231A) gave leaf-white text 9.42:1 against the worst pixel even over the lightest leaf colour in the test image.
steps.how: Method: hide the text, screenshot the plate, compute the WCAG ratio of the text colour against every pixel and report the smallest. The test image runs from #6FBF73 to #D7F5B1; replace it with your brightest real photograph and measure again.
steps.label: craft-consensus

steps.title: Alt text for botanical photos
steps.do: Write real alt text for botanical photography when it informs (species, a visible feature), and alt="" when it only decorates.
steps.how: NN/g and WebAIM: purpose from context, no "image of", empty alt for decoration. Chrome accessibility snapshot of the demo: the photo is exposed as a named image "Monstera deliciosa leaf with natural splits, held against a white wall".
steps.label: standard

steps.title: Dark natural theme colors
steps.do: For a dark natural theme use forest (#14231A) or soil (#2A1F18) with leaf-white text #E8EFE0 (13.89:1 on forest, 13.65:1 on soil), muted #B9C8A8 (9.25:1), lime button #B9D98A with forest text (10.39:1) and amber #E0B15A on soil (8.11:1).
steps.how: Define the dark values as their own tokens and recheck every pair. Chrome demo: under emulated dark scheme the tokens resolve to exactly these colours. Dark forest and soil are the natural-world answer to the near-black plus neon default.
steps.label: craft-consensus
steps.status_note: Pairs are computed and rendered; the framing against near-black plus neon is our opinion.

steps.title: Cap image widths, wrap long words
steps.do: Fixed rem image widths need max-width: 100% (14rem is 448 px at 200%); put overflow-wrap: anywhere on body so long words cannot widen the page.
steps.how: Measured 2026-11-06 in Chrome (Playwright, channel chrome) on the recipe demo page at 320 px with the root font size at 200% and the audit probes; img.photo was 448 px wide in a 320 px viewport plus a 24 px text-spacing overflow; both were gone after the change.
steps.label: standard
steps.measured: Measured 2026-11-06 in Chrome (Playwright, channel chrome) on the recipe demo page at 320 px with the root font size at 200% and the audit probes; img.photo was 448 px wide in a 320 px viewport plus a 24 px text-spacing overflow; both were gone after the change.

steps.title: Caption strip, not nested card
steps.do: Make a caption plate on a rounded photo frame a square-cornered full-width scrim strip along the bottom edge (let the frame's overflow: hidden round its corners); a rounded tinted plate inside a rounded frame counts as a nested card (distinct-no-nested-cards).
steps.how: Measured 2026-11-06 in Chrome (Playwright, channel chrome) on the recipe demo page at 320 px with the root font size at 200% and the audit probes; distinct-no-nested-cards failed with a rounded, tinted .plate inside .leafy and passed after the strip change; the check counts boxes with a radius of 4 px or more.
steps.label: our-take
steps.measured: Measured 2026-11-06 in Chrome (Playwright, channel chrome) on the recipe demo page at 320 px with the root font size at 200% and the audit probes; distinct-no-nested-cards failed with a rounded, tinted .plate inside .leafy and passed after the strip change; the check counts boxes with a radius of 4 px or more.
steps.status_note: Recorded from one audit run on one demo page; the audit check is a heuristic and the technique has no independent source.

recipes.generate_hint: Pick the page ground from the subject (leaf-tinted mist, deep forest or soil) and run the cream test on it, use dark moss for text and links with underlines, give field edges 3:1, set different radii for controls, cards, tags and images, and put text over botanical imagery on a plate.

recipes.title: Atmospheric full-bleed heroes with text you can read
recipes.summary: Keep the edge-to-edge image, the haze, grain and light. Put one scrim under the text column, tuned for the brightest pixel the image can offer, keep a dark colour behind the image for when it fails, and hold the content in a normal container while only the picture bleeds.
recipes.keep: Edge-to-edge photography or illustration, haze, grain, gradients and colour atmosphere.
recipes.avoid: White text on a photo with no scrim; a scrim tuned to the average rather than the brightest pixel; no fallback colour behind the image; text across the full 1920 px of a monitor; relying on a gradient scrim that forced-colours mode removes.

contrast.pair: white on 72% scrim over pure white (worst case)
white on 72% scrim over bright yellow #FFE600
white on 72% scrim over pale sky #BFE9FF
muted #D5DAE6 on 72% scrim over pure white
white on the fallback colour shown if the image fails

steps.title: One scrim for the brightest pixel
steps.do: Lay one scrim under the text column and tune it for the brightest pixel the image can offer, not the average. A #0B1020 scrim at 72% gives white text 7.69:1 over pure white, 8.83:1 over yellow #FFE600 and 8.67:1 over pale sky #BFE9FF; muted #D5DAE6 text is 5.49:1 over pure white.
steps.how: Composite the scrim over the worst backdrop, then compute the WCAG ratio; 72% is where white reaches 7:1 (AAA for body text) on a pure white backdrop, with 4.5:1 as the minimum for muted text. Method used to verify in Chrome 156: hide the text, screenshot the text box, read every pixel and take the smallest ratio. On a test image that is white, bright yellow and pale sky behind the text, the headline measured 7.69, 8.53, 8.64 and 8.64:1 at 375, 768, 1440 and 1920 px, the lead 7.69, 8.53, 7.65 and 7.65, and the muted line 5.49, 5.49, 5.47 and 5.47. The same page without the scrim measured 1.27:1 against the worst pixel.
steps.label: standard

steps.title: Dark hero background fallback
steps.do: Set a dark background-color on the hero element itself, under the image, so white text still has 18.93:1 when the image is slow, blocked or fails to load.
steps.how: Without it, white text on a missing image falls back to the page background and disappears. Chrome demo: with the image and scrim removed the hero computes to rgb(11, 16, 32) behind white text. Also keep real, meaningful alt text on the image when it carries content; the demo image is decorative and has alt="".
steps.label: craft-consensus

steps.title: Forced-colors text block fallback
steps.do: Do not rely on a gradient scrim for readability in forced-colors mode: it is removed. Under @media (forced-colors: active) give the text block a Canvas background and CanvasText colour with a visible border, so the pair is a guaranteed system contrast.
steps.how: MDN: in forced-colors mode background-image is forced to none unless it is URL-based, and colours become system colours. Measured in Chrome 156 with forced colours emulated over a dark photo: the scrim computes to none, the headline is black and the worst rendered contrast is 1.15:1 without a plate, and 21:1 with a Canvas plate. This is a small usability tweak, which MDN allows; do not build a separate forced-colors design. The emulation uses a light system theme; a black high-contrast theme flips the colours, not the logic.
steps.label: craft-consensus

steps.title: Only the picture bleeds
steps.do: Let only the picture bleed. Put the headline, text and call to action in a centred wrapper of 1280 px or less, with a text column of about 36rem, and give the hero image and band the full width.
steps.how: At a 1920 px viewport the Chrome demo measures the hero and image at 1920 px, the wrapper at 1280 px and the text column at 576 px. The advisory rule allows only backgrounds and full-bleed media to exceed 1400 px.
steps.label: craft-consensus

steps.title: Atmosphere layer below the scrim
steps.do: Keep haze, grain and light leaks on their own aria-hidden, pointer-events:none layer between the image and the scrim, and measure the text with that layer on. Never place text on atmosphere alone; scrim first, then text.
steps.how: The grain layer (opacity 0.12, repeating radial dots) is part of the screenshot in the pixel measurements above, so the reported ratios include it. W3C COGA asks for text on solid or low-detail backgrounds or a solid panel or overlay, and says text over photos, video, gradients and patterns of varying luminance is a barrier.
steps.label: craft-consensus

recipes.generate_hint: Choose a scrim colour and alpha from the brightest pixel under the text (0.72 of a near-black reaches 7:1 over pure white), set a dark background-color on the hero, keep atmosphere on its own aria-hidden layer, limit the content to a 1280px wrapper and a text column of about 36rem, and measure the rendered pixels at 375, 768, 1440 and 1920 px.

recipes.title: Futuristic, purple-led and retro-computing looks without the default tells
recipes.summary: Keep the precision, the single bold hue and the terminal nostalgia. Pick an accent from the brand instead of violet or cyan, replace glow with hairlines and flat fills, show status only when it is true, and make pixel and CRT effects finite, measured and motion-safe.
recipes.keep: Thin lines, grids, data motifs, a committed purple, pixel type, terminal windows, phosphor colours, stepped animation.
recipes.avoid: Violet-to-blue gradients and cyan on near-black as defaults; chromatic zero-offset glow; pulsing Live or New or version pills that report nothing; endless blinking cursors and CRT flicker; scanline overlays that eat text contrast; hairlines that carry meaning below 3:1.

palette.name: Graphite signal, committed purple and phosphor, computed

contrast.pair: futuristic: muted text on panel surface
futuristic: signal-orange accent on panel surface (large text, icons, UI)
futuristic: graphite text on signal-orange button
futuristic: input edge on panel surface (UI boundary)
purple brand: white on deep purple
purple brand: sun-yellow on deep purple
purple brand: pale lilac text on deep purple
purple brand: purple link on white
purple brand: deep purple on yellow button
retro: amber phosphor on dark brown-black
retro: green phosphor on dark green-black

steps.title: Flat accent from the brand
steps.do: Take the accent hue from the brand or subject and state it in the direction file. On graphite #0E0F11 use a flat signal colour instead of violet gradients or cyan: orange #FF5B1F (5.83:1 on the #15161A panel, graphite text on an orange button 6.18:1), lime #C8F169 (14.83:1), amber or phosphor green.
steps.how: The rule flags any gradient stop or primary accent with a hue of 260 to 310 degrees and a cyan accent on a near-black ground, unless the brand is that colour and the direction file says so. We ran that hue test in code over the demo's accents: orange is at 16 degrees, so nothing is flagged. Orange is not a neutral choice either: pick the hue because it is the brand or the subject, not because it avoids the check.
steps.label: craft-consensus
steps.status_note: The hue band and the cyan-on-black condition come from practitioner detectors and articles (some rated low weight); contrast and hue arithmetic were computed.

steps.title: Purple as a solid, not gradient
steps.do: If purple is the brand, commit to it as a solid, not a gradient, and record the exception. Deep purple #4C1D95 gives white 10.95:1, sun yellow #FFE45E 8.61:1 and pale lilac #E9D5FF 8.05:1; on white the link purple #5B21B6 is 8.98:1 and deep purple on a yellow button is 8.61:1. Pair it with a warm partner (yellow), not a blue or pink gradient.
steps.how: The rule exempts a purple that is the brand when the direction file says so. The demo section is a flat #4C1D95 (hue 264, inside the 260 to 310 band), computed background-image none, which is why it needs the record. Example record: "Primary colour #4C1D95. Purple chosen because the studio's riso inks are violet and yellow; no gradients." The tag hue-purple only describes that purple is dominant; the exception is what stops it reading as the default. Note: the audit's distinct-no-ai-palette reports purple text pairs in the 260 to 310 degree hue band as a minor even when the exception is recorded in direction.md; accept that minor in writing, it is not a failure of the recipe.
steps.label: our-take

code.text:
direction.md
Accent: #4C1D95 (violet), partner #FFE45E (yellow).
Exception to distinct-no-ai-palette: purple is the brand (violet riso ink). Flat fills only, no violet-to-blue gradient.

steps.status_note: Contrast figures are computed; the advice to commit to a flat purple with a warm partner and to write the exception record is our judgement.

steps.title: Hairlines and flat fills, not glow
steps.do: Build the precise, technical feel from hairlines, grids and flat fills instead of glow. Use a 1px border (#2A2A30 on graphite for decoration), a neutral shadow such as 0 1px 0 rgb(0 0 0 / .4), and keep any coloured halo only where it encodes a state. Draw focus as an outline, not a glow.
steps.how: The rule flags a chromatic box-shadow or text-shadow with zero offset and blur of 3 px or more, and a saturated radial-gradient halo behind a hero on a dark page. We implemented that check in Chrome: the demo has no such shadow or radial gradient, and a deliberately added 0 0 12px #39FF88 shadow is flagged. A glow that shows selection or error is allowed by the rule; here state is shown by outlines and text.
steps.label: craft-consensus
steps.status_note: Rule thresholds are from practitioner detectors; verified only against the rule text on a demo page.

steps.title: Only true, current status labels
steps.do: Show a status label only when it reports something true and current: render the release line from the release record at build time with a real date, link it to the changelog, and drop pulsing dots and "Live", "New" or "Beta" pills that nothing updates.
steps.how: The rule flags pulsing status dots, pills reading new, live, beta or a version number in the first viewport unless bound to a data attribute or release record, and a pill chip above the hero heading. Chrome demo: no element under 1.5 aspect ratio has an infinite animation, no pill matches, and the release line carries a data-source attribute and a time element with a datetime. If something really is live, use role="status" on the text that changes.
steps.label: craft-consensus

code.text: Release 2.4.1 · 28 October 2026

steps.status_note: Rule is from practitioner sources; the data-binding pattern is our implementation of the rule's exception.

steps.title: Meaningful thin lines at 3:1
steps.do: Thin and technical must still be legible: hold lines that carry meaning (input edges, chart axes, dividers that separate controls) at 3:1, and keep decorative grids below that. The input edge #6B6B75 is 3.43:1 on the panel and 3.64:1 on graphite; the decorative grid #2A2A30 is not meant to be seen as content. Text: #F4F4F5 16.45:1 and muted #9A9AA2 6.47:1 on the panel.
steps.how: WCAG 1.4.11 for UI components and graphics; the Enhanced Contrast Understanding page notes that thin fonts render fainter, so use heavier weights or exceed the minimum. Use font-weight 400 or above for small light-on-dark text. Computed colours of the demo's text, accent, button and input edge match the claimed pairs in Chrome.
steps.label: standard

steps.title: Skip link and main in terminal layouts
steps.do: Terminal and retro-computer layouts built from stacked panels still need a skip link as the first focusable element and a main landmark around the content; panels are sections with headings, not bare divs.
steps.how: Measured 2026-11-06 in Chrome (Playwright, channel chrome) on the recipe demo page with the audit probes; the demo page failed a11y-bypass-blocks with 'no skip link and no main landmark' until a Skip to content link (visible on focus, high contrast) and main id=main were added.
steps.label: standard
steps.measured: Measured 2026-11-06 in Chrome (Playwright, channel chrome) on the recipe demo page with the audit probes; a11y-bypass-blocks failed without a skip link and main landmark; passed with both.

steps.title: Self-hosted pixel face at grid multiples
steps.do: Self-host the pixel face and set it in rem at whole multiples of its design grid (an 8 px font at 16 or 24 px), use it for headings and labels, and keep long text in a plain monospace or sans face. Draw pixel art as images with image-rendering: pixelated at integer scales (an 8 px sprite shown at 64 px), with alt text or alt="".
steps.how: WCAG 1.4.4 asks for 200% resize and lists viewport-unit-only sizing as a failure (F94), so size in rem. Integer multiples keep pixel edges crisp; that advice and the legibility of pixel fonts for body text are our judgement and were not measured. Chrome computes image-rendering: pixelated for the demo sprite. The MDN image-rendering page is not in sources.json.
steps.label: our-take
steps.status_note: Resize rule is verified from WCAG pages; the pixel-grid multiples and body-text advice are our judgement.

steps.title: Phosphor colors that pass contrast
steps.do: Use phosphor colours on dark grounds that pass: amber #FFB000 on #1A1100 is 10.2:1 and green #33FF66 on #001A0A is 13.57:1. Skip cyan on near-black; for dim secondary text keep at least 4.5:1 (for example #9A7A33 on #1A1100 is 4.63:1).
steps.how: Amber (hue 41) and green (hue 135) are outside the 260 to 310 band and are not cyan. Rendered colours in the Chrome demo match the claimed pairs.
steps.label: standard

steps.title: Finite CRT and cursor effects
steps.do: Keep CRT and cursor effects finite, static where possible and measured. Blink the cursor for four 1 s cycles with steps(1) and leave it visible; run a typed reveal once as a clip-path inset() animation with steps(), never by animating a fixed width with overflow:hidden and white-space:nowrap (that clips under WCAG text spacing and overflows at 200% text); skip flicker; remove all of it under prefers-reduced-motion. A scanline overlay is pointer-events:none and aria-hidden; 12% black stripes cost amber text only down to 7.88:1.
steps.how: WCAG 2.2.2 covers blinking that lasts more than five seconds beside other content (4 s here); WCAG 2.3.1 passes at no more than three flashes per second (1 per second here). Measured in Chrome 156: the cursor animation computes to 1s, 4 iterations, steps(1); with reduced motion emulated no animation exists. A solid block of text colour under the overlay rendered at rgb(224,155,0) for amber and rgb(45,224,90) for green, against the plain backgrounds 7.88:1 and 10.35:1. Computed: at 30% stripes amber text falls to 5.12:1 and at 20% it is 6.56:1, so keep the overlay at 20% or less. Measured 2026-11-06 in Chrome (Playwright, channel chrome) on the recipe demo page with the audit probes; the width/overflow:hidden/nowrap typed reveal failed a11y-text-spacing (1 element at 1440 px, 1 more at 320 px) and overflowed by 280 px at 200% text; the clip-path version passed.
steps.label: standard
steps.measured: Measured 2026-11-06 in Chrome (Playwright, channel chrome) on the recipe demo page with the audit probes; width-animated typed text failed text-spacing and 200% reflow; clip-path reveal passed.

steps.title: Easing for windows, steps for sprites
steps.do: Keep the 8-bit snap where it belongs and use proper easing for the windows: a window opens in 150 ms with a decelerating curve and closes in 100 ms with an accelerating one; reserve steps() for frame-by-frame sprites and typed text, never linear on a moving window.
steps.how: NN/g and Material motion: enter with ease-out, leave with ease-in, exits shorter than entrances; linear is for non-spatial or looping motion. Measured in Chrome: open state computes to 0.15s cubic-bezier(0, 0, 0.2, 1) and the closed state to 0.1s cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 1, 1); the typed reveal is steps(24). Whether stepped easing on a revealed width counts as spatial linear motion is not settled by the rule; steps() is not "linear", so the rule check passes.
steps.label: craft-consensus
steps.status_note: Durations and curve directions match the sources; the treatment of steps() under the rule is our reading.

steps.title: OS window chrome from real controls
steps.do: Make OS-window chrome out of real controls: buttons with accessible names ("Close window", not an X glyph alone), at least 44 px square, with a visible focus outline, inside a labelled dialog or region.
steps.how: Tiny title-bar buttons are the usual retro-computing target-size failure.
